s.en: Pumas are large, cat-like animals which are found in America.
s.zh: 美洲狮是一种体形似猫的大动物，产于美洲。

s.en: When reports came into London Zoo that a wild puma had been spotted forty-five miles south of London, they were not taken seriously.
s.zh: 当伦敦动物园接到报告说，在伦敦以南45英里处发现一只美洲狮时，这些报告并没有受到重视。

s.en: However, as the evidence began to accumulate, experts from the Zoo felt obliged to investigate, for the descriptions given by people who claimed to have seen the puma were extraordinarily similar.
s.zh: 可是，随着证据越来越多，动物园的专家们感到有必要进行一番调查，因为凡是声称见到过美洲狮的人们所描述的情况竟是出奇地相似。

s.en: The hunt for the puma began in a small village where a woman picking blackberries saw 'a large cat' only five yards away from her.
s.zh: 搜寻美洲狮的工作是从一座小村庄开始的。那里的一位妇女在采摘黑莓时看见“一只大猫”，离她仅5码远，

s.en: It immediately ran away when she saw it,
s.zh: 她刚看见它，它就立刻逃走了。

s.en: and experts confirmed that a puma will not attack a human being unless it is cornered.
s.zh: 专家证实，美洲狮非被逼得走投无路，是决不会伤人的。

s.en: The search proved difficult, for the puma was often observed at one place in the morning and at another place twenty miles away in the evening.
s.zh: 事实上搜寻工作很困难，因为常常是早晨在甲地发现那只美洲狮，晚上却在20英里外的乙地发现它的踪迹。

s.en: Wherever it went, it left behind it a trail of dead deer and small animals like rabbits.
s.zh: 无论它走哪儿， 一路上总会留下一串死鹿及死兔子之类的小动物，

s.en: Paw prints were seen in a number of places and puma fur was found clinging to bushes.
s.zh: 在许多地方看见爪印， 灌木丛中发现了粘在上面的美洲狮毛。

s.en: Several people complained of 'cat-like noises' at night and a businessman on a fishing trip saw the puma up a tree.
s.zh: 有人抱怨说夜里听见“像猫一样的叫声”； 一位商人去钓鱼，看见那只美洲狮在树上。

s.en: The experts were now fully convinced that the animal was a puma,
s.zh: 专家们如今已经完全肯定那只动物就是美洲狮，

s.en: but where had it come from?
s.zh: 但它是从哪儿来的呢？

s.en: As no pumas had been reported missing from any zoo in the country, this one must have been in the possession of a private collector and somehow managed to escape.
s.zh: 由于全国动物园没有一家报告丢了美洲狮，因此那只美洲狮一定是某位私人收藏家豢养的，不知怎么设法逃出来了。

s.en: The hunt went on for several weeks, but the puma was not caught.
s.zh: 搜寻工作进行了好几个星期，但始终未能逮住那只美洲狮。

s.en: It is disturbing to think that a dangerous wild animal is still at large in the quiet countryside.
s.zh: 想到在宁静的乡村里有一头危险的野兽继续逍遥流窜，真令人担心。

q: Where must the puma have come from?
美洲狮一定是从哪里来的？

s.en: Our vicar is always raising money for one cause or another,
s.zh: 我们教区的牧师总是为各种各样的事筹集资金。

s.en: but he has never managed to get enough money to have the church clock repaired.
s.zh: 但始终未能筹足资金把教堂的钟修好。

s.en: The big clock which used to strike the hours day and night was damaged many years ago and has been silent ever since.
s.zh: 教堂的钟很大，以前不分昼夜打点报时，但很多年前遭到毁坏，从此便无声无息了。

s.en: One night, however, our vicar woke up with a start: the clock was striking the hours!
s.zh: 一天夜里，我们的牧师突然被惊醒了，大钟又在“打点”报时了！

s.en: Looking at his watch, he saw that it was one o'clock,
s.zh: 他一看表，才1点钟，

s.en: but the bell struck thirteen times before it stopped.
s.zh: 可是那钟一连敲了13下才停。

s.en: Armed with a torch, the vicar went up into the clock tower to see what was going on.
s.zh: 牧师拿着一支电筒走上钟楼想去看看究竟发生了什么事情。

s.en: In the torchlight, he caught sight of a figure whom he immediately recognized as Bill Wilkins, our local grocer.
s.zh: 借着电筒光，他看见一个人，马上认出那是本地杂货店主比尔.威尔金斯。

s.en: 'Whatever are you doing up here, Bill?' asked the vicar in surprise.
s.zh: “你究竟在这上面干什么，比尔？” 牧师惊讶地问。

s.en: 'I'm trying to repair the bell,' answered Bill.
s.zh: “我想把这口钟修好，”比尔回答说。

s.en: 'I've been coming up here night after night for weeks now. You see, I was hoping to give you a surprise.'
s.zh: “好几个星期了，我天天夜里到钟楼上来。 嗯，我是想让你大吃一惊。”

s.en: 'You certainly did give me a surprise!' said the vicar.
s.zh: “你确实使我大吃了一惊！” 牧师说，

s.en: 'You've probably woken up everyone in the village as well. Still, I'm glad the bell is working again.'
s.zh: “也许同时你把村里所有的人都吵醒了。不过，钟又能报时了，我还是很高兴的。”

s.en: 'That's the trouble, vicar,' answered Bill.
s.zh: “问题就在这里，牧师，”比尔回答说。

s.en: 'It's working all right, but I'm afraid that at one o'clock it will strike thirteen times and there's nothing I can do about it.'
s.zh: “不错，钟能报时了，但是，恐怕每到1点钟，它总要敲13下，对此我已无能为力了。”

s.en: 'We'll get used to that, Bill,' said the vicar. 'Thirteen is not as good as one, but it's better than nothing. Now let's go downstairs and have a cup of tea.'
s.zh: “大家慢慢就习惯了，比尔，”牧师说。“13下是不如1下好，但总比1下也不敲强。来，咱们下楼去喝杯茶吧。”

q: Was the vicar pleased that the clock was striking? Why?
牧师对钟在报时感到高兴吗？为什么？

s.en: Some time ago, an interesting discovery was made by archaeologists on the Aegean island of Kea.
s.zh: 不久之前，在爱琴海的基亚岛上，考古工作者有一项有趣的发现。

s.en: An American team explored a temple which stands in an ancient city on the promontory of Ayia Irini.
s.zh: 一个美国考古队在阿伊亚. 依里尼海角的一座古城里考察了一座庙宇。

s.en: The city at one time must have been prosperous, for it enjoyed a high level of civilization.
s.zh: 这座古城肯定一度很繁荣，因为它曾享有高度的文明，

s.en: Houses--often three storeys high--were built of stone.
s.zh: 房子一般有3层楼高，用石块修建。

s.en: They had large rooms with beautifully decorated walls.
s.zh: 里面房间很大，墙壁装饰华丽。

s.en: The city was equipped with a drainage system, for a great many clay pipes were found beneath the narrow streets.
s.zh: 城里甚至还敷设了排水系统，因为在狭窄的街道底下发现了许许多多陶土制作的排水管道。

s.en: The temple which the archaeologists explored was used as a place of worship from the fifteenth century B.C. until Roman times.
s.zh: 考古工作者考察的这座庙宇从公元前15世纪直到罗马时代一直是祭祀祈祷的场所。

s.en: In the most sacred room of the temple, clay fragments of fifteen statues were found.
s.zh: 在庙中最神圣的一间殿堂里发现了15尊陶雕像的碎片。

s.en: Each of these represented a goddess and had, at one time, been painted.
s.zh: 每一尊雕像代表一位女神，而且一度上过色。

s.en: The body of one statue was found among remains dating from the fifteenth century B.C.
s.zh: 其中有一尊雕像，她的躯体是在公元前15世纪的历史文物中发现的，

s.en: Its missing head happened to be among remains of the fifth century B.C.
s.zh: 而她那身首异处的脑袋却碰巧是在公元前5世纪的文物中找到的。

s.en: This head must have been found in Classical times and carefully preserved.
s.zh: 她的脑袋一定是在古希腊罗马时代就为人所发现，并受到精心的保护。

s.en: It was very old and precious even then.
s.zh: 即使在当时，它也属历史悠久的珍奇之物。

s.en: When the archaeologists reconstructed the fragments, they were amazed to find that the goddess turned out to be a very modern-looking woman.
s.zh: 考古工作者把这些碎片重新拼装起来后，惊奇地发现那位女神原来是一位相貌十分摩登的女郎。

s.en: She stood three feet high and her hands rested on her hips.
s.zh: 她身高3英尺，双手叉腰。

s.en: She was wearing a full-length skirt which swept the ground.
s.zh: 身穿一条拖地长裙，

s.en: Despite her great age, she was very graceful indeed,
s.zh: 尽管上了年纪，但体态确实优美。

s.en: but, so far, the archaeologists have been unable to discover her identity.
s.zh: 不过，考古工作者至今未能确定这位女神的身份。

q: How did the archaeologists know that the statue was a goddess?
考古学家是如何知道这座雕像是女神的呢？

lessons.t: The double life of Alfred Bloggs

s.en: These days, people who do manual work often receive far more money than people who work in offices.
s.zh: 如今，从事体力劳动的人的收入一般要比坐办公室的人高出许多。

s.en: People who work in offices are frequently referred to as 'white-collar workers' for the simple reason that they usually wear a collar and tie to go to work.
s.zh: 坐办公室的人之所以常常被称作“白领工人”，就是因为他们通常是穿着硬领白衬衫，系着领带去上班。

s.en: Such is human nature, that a great many people are often willing to sacrifice higher pay for the privilege of becoming white-collar workers.
s.zh: 许多人常常情愿放弃较高的薪水以换取做白领工人的殊荣，此乃人之常情。

s.en: This can give rise to curious situations, as it did in the case of Alfred Bloggs who worked as a dustman for the Ellesmere Corporation.
s.zh: 而这常常会引起种种奇怪的现象，在埃尔斯米尔公司当清洁工的艾尔弗雷德·布洛格斯就是一个例子。

s.en: When he got married, Alf was too embarrassed to say anything to his wife about his job.
s.zh: 艾尔弗结婚时，感到非常难为情，而没有将自己的职业告诉妻子。

s.en: He simply told her that he worked for the Corporation.
s.zh: 他只说在埃尔斯米尔公司上班。

s.en: Every morning, he left home dressed in a smart black suit.
s.zh: 每天早晨，他穿上一身漂亮的黑色西装离家上班。

s.en: He then changed into overalls and spent the next eight hours as a dustman.
s.zh: 然后换上工作服，当 8 个小时清洁工。

s.en: Before returning home at night, he took a shower and changed back into his suit.
s.zh: 晚上回家前，他洗个淋浴，重新换上那身黑色西服。

s.en: Alf did this for over two years and his fellow dustmen kept his secret.
s.zh: 两年多以来，艾尔弗一直这样，他的同事也为他保守秘密。

s.en: Alf's wife has never discovered that she married a dustman and she never will, for Alf has just found another job.
s.zh: 艾尔弗的妻子一直不知道她嫁给了一个清洁工，而且她永远也不会知道了，因为艾尔弗已找到新职。

s.en: He will soon be working in an office.
s.zh: 不久就要坐办公室里工作了。

s.en: He will be earning only half as much as he used to, but he feels that his rise in status is well worth the loss of money.
s.zh: 他将来挣的钱只有他现在的一半，不过他觉得，地位升高了，损失点儿钱也值得。

s.en: From now on, he will wear a suit all day and others will call him 'Mr. Bloggs', not 'Alf'.
s.zh: 从此，艾尔弗可以一天到晚穿西服了。别人将称呼他为“布洛格斯先生”，而不再叫他“艾尔弗”了。

q: Why did Alf want a white-collar job?
为什么阿尔夫想要一份白领工作呢？

s.en: Editors of newspapers and magazines often go to extremes to provide their readers with unimportant facts and statistics.
s.zh: 报刊杂志的编辑常常为了向读者提供一些无关紧要的事实和统计数字而走极端 。

s.en: Last year a journalist had been instructed by a well-known magazine to write an article on the president's palace in a new African republic.
s.zh: 去年，一位记者受一家有名的杂志的委托写一篇关于非洲某个新成立共和国总统府的文章。

s.en: When the article arrived, the editor read the first sentence and then refused to publish it.
s.zh: 稿子寄来后，编辑看了第一句话就拒绝予以发表。

s.en: The article began: 'Hundreds of steps lead to the high wall which surrounds the president's palace'.
s.zh: 文章的开头是这样的：“几百级台阶通向环绕总统府的高墙。”

s.en: The editor at once sent the journalist a fax instructing him to find out the exact number of steps and the height of the wall.
s.zh: 编辑立即给那位记者发去传真，要求他核实一下台阶的确切数字和围墙的高度。

s.en: The journalist immediately set out to obtain these important facts,
s.zh: 记者立即出发去核实这些重要的事实，

s.en: but he took a long time to send them. Meanwhile, the editor was getting impatient, for the magazine would soon go to press.
s.zh: 但过了好长时间不见他把数字寄来， 在此期间，编辑等得不耐烦了，因为杂志马上要付印。

s.en: He sent the journalist two more faxes, but received no reply.
s.zh: 他给记者先后发去两份传真，但对方毫无反应。

s.en: He sent yet another fax informing the journalist that if he did not reply soon he would be fired.
s.zh: 于是他又发了一份传真， 通知那位记者说，若再不迅速答复，将被解雇。

s.en: When the journalist again failed to reply, the editor reluctantly published the article as it had originally been written.
s.zh: 但记者还是没有回复。 编辑无奈，勉强按原样发稿了。

s.en: A week later, the editor at last received a fax from the journalist.
s.zh: 一周之后，编辑终于接到记者的传真。

s.en: Not only had the poor man been arrested,
s.zh: 那个可怜的记者不仅被捕了，

s.en: but he had been sent to prison as well.
s.zh: 而且还被送进了监狱。

s.en: However, he had at last been allowed to send a fax in which he informed the editor that he had been arrested while counting the 1,084 steps leading to the fifteen-foot wall which surrounded the president's palace.
s.zh: 不过，他终于获准发回了一份传真。在传真中他告诉编辑，就在他数通向15英尺高的总统府围墙的1,084级台阶时，被抓了起来。

q: What was the consequence of the editor's insistence on facts and statistics?
编辑坚持要事实和统计数据，造成了什么后果？

s.en: The expensive shops in a famous arcade near Piccadilly were just opening.
s.zh: 皮卡迪利大街附近的一条著名拱廊街道上，几家高档商店刚刚开始营业。

s.en: At this time of the morning, the arcade was almost empty.
s.zh: 在早晨的这个时候，拱廊街上几乎空无一人。

s.en: Mr. Taylor, the owner of a jewellery shop was admiring a new display.
s.zh: 珠宝店主泰勒先生正在欣赏新布置的橱窗。

s.en: Two of his assistants had been working busily since eight o'clock and had only just finished.
s.zh: 他手下两名店员从早上8点就开始忙碌，这时刚刚布置完毕。

s.en: Diamond necklaces and rings had been beautifully arranged on a background of black velvet.
s.zh: 钻石项链、戒指漂亮地陈列在黑色丝绒上面。

s.en: After gazing at the display for several minutes, Mr. Taylor went back into his shop.
s.zh: 泰勒先生站在橱窗外凝神欣赏了几分钟就回到了店里。

s.en: The silence was suddenly broken when a large car, with its headlights on and its horn blaring, roared down the arcade.
s.zh: 宁静突然被打破，一辆大轿车亮着前灯，响着喇叭，呼啸着冲进了拱廊街，

s.en: It came to a stop outside the jeweller's.
s.zh: 在珠宝店门口停了下来。

s.en: One man stayed at the wheel while two others with black stockings over their faces jumped out and smashed the window of the shop with iron bars.
s.zh: 一人留在驾驶座上，另外两个用黑色长筒丝袜蒙面的人跳下车来。 他们用铁棒把商店橱窗的玻璃砸碎。

s.en: While this was going on, Mr. Taylor was upstairs.
s.zh: 这开始发生时，泰勒先生正在楼上。

s.en: He and his staff began throwing furniture out of the window.
s.zh: 他与店员动手向窗外投掷家具，

s.en: Chairs and tables went flying into the arcade.
s.zh: 椅子、桌子纷纷飞落在拱廊街上。

s.en: One of the thieves was struck by a heavy statue,
s.zh: 一个窃贼被一尊很重的雕像击中，

s.en: but he was too busy helping himself to diamonds to notice any pain.
s.zh: 但由于他忙着抢钻石首饰，竟连疼痛都顾不上了。

s.en: The raid was all over in three minutes, for the men scrambled back into the car and it moved off at a fantastic speed.
s.zh: 这场抢劫只持续了3分钟，因为窃贼争先恐后地爬上轿车，以惊人的速度开跑了。

s.en: Just as it was leaving, Mr. Taylor rushed out and ran after it throwing ashtrays and vases,
s.zh: 就在轿车离开的时候，泰勒先生从店里冲了出来，跟在车后追赶，一边还往车上扔烟灰缸、花瓶。

s.en: but it was impossible to stop the thieves.
s.zh: 但他已无法抓住那些窃贼了。

s.en: They had got away with thousands of pounds worth of diamonds.
s.zh: 他们已带着价值数千镑的首饰逃之夭夭了。

q: How did Mr. Taylor try to stop the thieves?
泰勒先生是如何试图阻止那些小偷的？

s.en: Has it ever happened to you?
s.zh: 这种事情在你身上出现过吗？

s.en: Have you ever put your trousers in the washing machine and then remembered there was a large bank note in your back pocket?
s.zh: 你有没有把裤子塞进洗衣机后 ，却又想起在裤子的后兜有一张大面值的纸币？

s.en: When you rescued your trousers, did you find the note was whiter than white?
s.zh: 当你把裤子抢救出来时，你有没有发现那张纸币已经变得比白纸还白？

s.en: People who live in Britain needn't despair when they make mistakes like this (and a lot of people do)!
s.zh: 当英国人犯这种错误时， 他们不必感到绝望（而许多人确实会犯这种错误）。

s.en: Fortunately for them, the Bank of England has a team called Mutilated Ladies which deals with claims from people who fed their money to a machine or to their dog.
s.zh: 对英国人来说，值得庆幸的是英国银行有一个残钞鉴别组， 负责处理那些把钱塞进机器或塞给狗的人提出的索赔要求。

s.en: Dogs, it seems, love to chew up money!
s.zh: 看起来，狗很喜欢咀嚼钱币。

s.en: A recent case concerns Jane Butlin whose fiancé, John, runs a successful furniture business.
s.zh: 最近的一个案例与简. 巴特林有关，她的未婚夫约翰拥有一家生意兴隆的家具店。

s.en: John had a very good day and put his wallet containing $3,000 into the microwave oven for safekeeping.
s.zh: 有一天约翰的生意很好，他把一只装有3,000 英镑的钱包放进微波炉内保存。

s.en: Then he and Jane went horse-riding.
s.zh: 然后，他和简一起去骑马。

s.en: When they got home, Jane cooked their dinner in the microwave oven and without realizing it, cooked her fiancé's wallet as well.
s.zh: 回家后，简用微波炉煮了晚饭，无意之中把她未婚夫的钱包也一起煮了。

s.en: Imagine their dismay when they found a beautifully-cooked wallet and notes turned to ash!
s.zh: 可以想像他们发现一只煮得很好看的钱包，钞票已化成灰时的沮丧心情。

s.en: John went to see his bank manager who sent the remains of the wallet and the money to the special department of the Bank of England in Newcastle: the Mutilated Ladies!
s.zh: 约翰去找银行经理，经理把约翰的钱包和纸币的残留物送到英国银行在纽卡斯尔的一个专门部门——残钞鉴别组。

s.en: They examined the remains and John got all his money back.
s.zh: 他们鉴定了这些残留物。 约翰拿回了他损失的全部数额。

s.en: 'So long as there's something to identify, we will give people their money back,' said a spokeswoman for the Bank.
s.zh: “只要有东西可供识别，我们会把钱还给人家的，”银行的一位女发言人说。

s.en: 'Last year, we paid $1.5m on 21,000 claims.'
s.zh: “去年我们处理了 21,000 起关于损坏纸币的索赔，总共赔付 150 万美元。”

s.zh: *这是英国银行专门负责识别和鉴定残缺或被毁纸币的小组，其中的“lady”是指英国纸币上印的女王头像。

q: Why did Jane cook John's wallet?
简为什么把约翰的钱包煮了？

s.en: The Great St. Bernard Pass connects Switzerland to Italy.
s.zh: 圣伯纳德山口连接瑞士和意大利。

s.en: At 2,473 metres, it is the highest mountain pass in Europe.
s.zh: 海拔2473米，是欧洲最高的山口。

s.en: The famous monastery of St. Bernard, which was founded in the eleventh century, lies about a mile away.
s.zh: 著名的圣伯纳德修道院建于十一世纪，距离山口约一英里。

s.en: For hundreds of years, St. Bernard dogs have saved the lives of travellers crossing the dangerous Pass.
s.zh: 数百年来，圣伯纳德犬拯救了穿越危险山口的旅行者的生命。

s.en: These friendly dogs, which were first brought from Asia, were used as watchdogs even in Roman times.
s.zh: 这些友好的狗最早是从亚洲带来的，甚至在罗马时代也被用作看门狗。

s.en: Now that a tunnel has been built through the mountains, the Pass is less dangerous,
s.zh: 现在已经修建了一条穿过山脉的隧道，山口的危险性就小了，

s.en: but each year, the dogs are still sent out into the snow whenever a traveller is in difficulty.
s.zh: 但每年，每当旅行者遇到困难时，狗仍会被派往雪地里。

s.en: Despite the new tunnel, there are still a few people who rashly attempt to cross the Pass on foot.
s.zh: 尽管有了新隧道，仍有一些人鲁莽地试图步行穿过山口。

s.en: During the summer months, the monastery is very busy, for it is visited by thousands of people who cross the Pass in cars.
s.zh: 在夏季的几个月里，修道院非常繁忙，因为成千上万的人开车穿过山口来参观。

s.en: As there are so many people about, the dogs have to be kept in a special enclosure.
s.zh: 由于周围人太多，狗必须被关在一个特殊的围栏里。

s.en: In winter, however, life at the monastery is quite different.
s.zh: 然而，在冬天，修道院的生活却截然不同。

s.en: The temperature drops to--30 o and very few people attempt to cross the Pass.
s.zh: 气温降至零下30度，很少有人试图穿过山口。

s.en: The monks prefer winter to summer for they have more privacy.
s.zh: 僧侣们更喜欢冬天而不是夏天，因为他们有更多的隐私。

s.en: The dogs have greater freedom, too, for they are allowed to wander outside their enclosure.
s.zh: 狗也有更大的自由，因为它们被允许在围栏外漫步。

s.en: The only regular visitors to the monastery in winter are parties of skiers who go there at Christmas and Easter.
s.zh: 冬天唯一经常来修道院的人是圣诞节和复活节去那里的滑雪者。

s.en: These young people, who love the peace of the mountains, always receive a warm welcome at St. Bernard's monastery.
s.zh: 这些热爱山区宁静的年轻人，在圣伯纳德修道院总是受到热烈欢迎。

q: What are the St.Bernard dogs used for?
圣伯纳德犬是用来做什么的？

s.en: Cats never fail to fascinate human beings.
s.zh: 猫总是让人着迷。

s.en: They can be friendly and affectionate towards humans,
s.zh: 它们可以对人类友好和深情，

s.en: but they lead mysterious lives of their own as well.
s.zh: 但它们也过着神秘的生活。

s.en: They never become submissive like dogs and horses.
s.zh: 它们永远不会像狗和马那样顺从。

s.en: As a result, humans have learned to respect feline independence.
s.zh: 因此，人类已经学会尊重猫的独立性。

s.en: Most cats remain suspicious of humans all their lives.
s.zh: 大多数猫一生都怀疑人类。

s.en: One of the things that fascinates us most about cats is the popular belief that they have nine lives.
s.zh: 猫最让我们着迷的一点是，人们普遍认为猫有九条命。

s.en: Apparently, there is a good deal of truth in this idea.
s.zh: 显然，这个想法有很多道理。

s.en: A cat's ability to survive falls is based on fact.
s.zh: 猫从高处坠落后的生存能力是基于事实的。

s.en: Recently the New York Animal Medical Center made a study of 132 cats over a period of five months.
s.zh: 最近，纽约动物医学中心对132只猫进行了为期五个月的研究。

s.en: All these cats had one experience in common: they had fallen off high buildings, yet only eight of them died from shock or injuries.
s.zh: 所有这些猫都有一个共同的经历：它们从高楼上摔下来，但只有八只死于休克或受伤。

s.en: Of course, New York is the ideal place for such an interesting study,
s.zh: 当然，纽约是进行如此有趣研究的理想之地，

s.en: because there is no shortage of tall buildings.
s.zh: 因为这里不乏高楼大厦。

s.en: There are plenty of high-rise windowsills to fall from!
s.zh: 有很多高层窗台可以掉下来！

s.en: One cat, Sabrina, fell 32 storeys, yet only suffered from a broken tooth.
s.zh: 一只名叫萨布丽娜的猫从32层楼摔了下来，但只摔断了一颗牙。

s.en: 'Cats behave like well-trained paratroopers,' a doctor said.
s.zh: “猫的行为就像训练有素的伞兵，”一位医生说。

s.en: It seems that the further cats fall, the less they are likely to injure themselves.
s.zh: 猫坠落的距离越长，受伤的可能性就越小。

s.en: In a long drop, they reach speeds of 60 miles an hour and more.
s.zh: 在长时间的下降中，它们的速度达到每小时60英里甚至更高。

s.en: At high speeds, falling cats have time to relax.
s.zh: 在高速下落时，猫有时间放松。

s.en: They stretch out their legs like flying squirrels.
s.zh: 它们像飞鼠一样伸展腿。

s.en: This increases their air-resistance and reduces the shock of impact when they hit the ground.
s.zh: 这增加了它们的空气阻力，减少了它们撞击地面时的冲击力

q: How do cats try to protect themselves when falling from great heights?
当猫从高处坠落时，它们会如何保护自己呢？

s.en: The great ship, Titanic, sailed for New York from Southampton on April 10th, 1912.
s.zh: 1912年4月10日，泰坦尼克号从南安普敦驶向纽约。

s.en: She was carrying 1,316 passengers and a crew of 891.
s.zh: 它载有1316名乘客和891名船员。

s.en: Even by modern standards, the 46,000 ton Titanic was a colossal ship.
s.zh: 即使按照现代标准，46000吨的泰坦尼克号也是一艘巨大的船。

s.en: At the time, however, she was not only the largest ship that had ever been built,
s.zh: 然而，在当时，她不仅是有史以来建造的最大的船，

s.en: but was regarded as unsinkable, for she had sixteen watertight compartments.
s.zh: 而且它被认为是不会沉没的，因为它有十六个水密舱。

s.en: Even if two of these were flooded, she would still be able to float.
s.zh: 即使其中两个被淹没，她仍然可以漂浮。

s.en: The tragic sinking of this great liner will always be remembered, for she went down on her first voyage with heavy loss of life.
s.zh: 这艘大客轮的悲惨沉没将永远被铭记，因为它在第一次航行中沉没，造成了巨大的生命损失。

s.en: Four days after setting out, while the Titanic was sailing across the icy water of the North Atlantic, a huge iceberg was suddenly spotted by a lookout.
s.zh: 出发四天后，当泰坦尼克号在北大西洋的冰水中航行时，一名了望员突然发现了巨大的冰山。

s.en: After the alarm had been given, the great ship turned sharply to avoid a direct collision.
s.zh: 警报发出后，大船急转弯以避免直接碰撞。

s.en: The Titanic turned just in time, narrowly missing the immense wall of ice which rose over 100 feet out of the water beside her.
s.zh: 泰坦尼克号及时转弯，险些撞上从她旁边的水中升起100多英尺的巨大冰块。

s.en: Suddenly, there was a slight trembling sound from below,
s.zh: 突然，下面传来一阵轻微的颤抖声，

s.en: and the captain went down to see what had happened.
s.zh: 船长下去看看发生了什么事。

s.en: The noise had been so faint that no one thought that the ship had been damaged.
s.zh: 声音太微弱了，没有人认为船已经损坏了。

s.en: Below, the captain realized to his horror that the Titanic was sinking rapidly, for five of her sixteen watertight compartments had already been flooded!
s.zh: 下面，船长惊恐地意识到泰坦尼克号正在迅速沉没，因为她的十六个水密舱中有五个已经被淹没了！

s.en: The order to abandon ship was given and hundreds of people plunged into the icy water.
s.zh: 弃船的命令下达后，数百人跳入冰冷的水中。

s.en: As there were not enough lifeboats for everybody, 1,500 lives were lost.
s.zh: 由于没有足够的救生艇供所有人使用，1500人丧生。

q: What'd have happened if only two of the 16 water-tight compartments had been flooded?
如果16个防水隔舱中只有两个进水，会发生什么？

s.en: Customs Officers are quite tolerant these days, but they can still stop you when you are going through the Green Channel and have nothing to declare.
s.zh: 如今的海关官员通常比较宽容，但即便你通过绿色通道且没有任何需要申报的物品，他们仍有可能拦下你。

s.en: Even really honest people are often made to feel guilty.
s.zh: 即使是那些非常诚实的人，也常常会因此感到内疚。

s.en: The hardened professional smuggler, on the other hand, is never troubled by such feelings,
s.zh: 另一方面，那些老练的走私者则完全不会受到这种情绪的困扰——

s.en: even if he has five hundred gold watches hidden in his suitcase.
s.zh: 即使他们的行李箱里藏着五百块金表。

s.en: When I returned from abroad recently, a particularly officious young Customs Officer
s.zh: 最近我从国外回来时，一位特别爱管闲事的年轻海关官员

s.en: clearly regarded me as a smuggler.
s.zh: 明显把我当成了走私者。

s.en: 'Have you anything to declare?' he asked, looking me in the eye.
s.zh: “您有什么需要申报的吗？”他直视着我的眼睛问道。

s.en: 'No,' I answered confidently.
s.zh: “没有，”我自信地回答。

s.en: 'Would you mind unlocking this suitcase please? '
s.zh: “请您把这个行李箱打开好吗？”

s.en: 'Not at all,' I answered.
s.zh: “好的，”我回答道。

s.en: The Officer went through the case with great care.
s.zh: 这位官员非常仔细地检查了行李箱。

s.en: All the things I had packed so carefully were soon in a dreadful mess.
s.zh: 我精心打包的所有东西，很快就变得一片狼藉。

s.en: I felt sure I would never be able to close the case again.
s.zh: 我确信自己再也无法关上这个箱子了。

s.en: Suddenly, I saw the Officer's face light up.
s.zh: 突然，我看到那位海关官员的脸上露出了笑容。

s.en: He had spotted a tiny bottle at the bottom of my case
s.zh: 他在我的行李箱底部发现了一个小瓶子。

s.en: and he pounced on it with delight.
s.zh: 他高兴地抓住了它。

s.en: 'Perfume, eh?' he asked sarcastically.
s.zh: “香水，是吗？”他讽刺地问道。

s.en: 'You should have declared that.
s.zh: “你本应该申报这个的。

s.en: Perfume is not exempt from import duty.  '
s.zh: 香水同样需要缴纳进口关税。”

s.en: 'But it isn't perfume,' I said. 'It's hair gel.  '
s.zh: “但这不是香水，”我说，“这是发胶。”

s.en: Then I added with a smile,
s.zh: 然后我微笑着补充道：

s.en: 'It's a strange mixture I make myself.'
s.zh: “这是我自己调制的一种奇怪混合物。”

s.en: As I expected, he did not believe me.
s.zh: 正如我所料，他根本不相信我的话。

s.en: 'Try it!' I said encouragingly.
s.zh: “试试看吧！”我鼓励地说道。

s.en: The Officer unscrewed the cap and put the bottle to his nostrils.
s.zh: 那位海关官员拧开了瓶盖，将瓶子靠近自己的鼻孔。

s.en: He was greeted by an unpleasant smell which convinced him that I was telling the truth.
s.zh: 一股难闻的气味扑面而来，这让他确信我说的是实话。

s.en: A few minutes later, I was able to hurry away with precious chalk marks on my baggage.
s.zh: 几分钟后，我终于带着行李匆匆离开了——我的行李上留下了那些珍贵的粉笔痕迹。

q: What was the Customs Officer looking for?
海关官员在寻找什么？

s.en: Most of us have formed an unrealistic picture of life on a desert island.
s.zh: 我们大多数人都对在荒岛上生活有着不切实际的想象。

s.en: We sometimes imagine a desert island to be a sort of paradise where the sun always shines.
s.zh: 我们有时会想象，荒岛是一种天堂般的地方——那里阳光永远明媚。

s.en: Life there is simple and good.
s.zh: 那里的生活简单而美好。

s.en: Ripe fruit falls from the trees and you never have to work.
s.zh: 成熟的果实从树上掉下来，你根本不用工作。

s.en: The other side of the picture is quite the opposite.
s.zh: 事情的另一面则完全相反。

s.en: Life on a desert island is wretched.
s.zh: 在荒岛上生活是非常艰苦的。

s.en: You either starve to death or live like Robinson Crusoe, waiting for a boat which never comes.
s.zh: 要么你饿死；要么你像鲁滨逊·克鲁索一样孤独地生活，等待着一艘永远都不会到来的船。

s.en: Perhaps there is an element of truth in both these pictures, but few of us have had the opportunity to find out.
s.zh: 也许这两种想象都有几分道理，但我们很少有人有机会去弄个明白。

s.en: Two men who recently spent five days on a coral island wished they had stayed there longer.
s.zh: 两名最近在珊瑚岛上度过了五天时间的男子，希望自己能多待一段时间。

s.en: They were taking a badly damaged boat from the Virgin Islands to Miami to have it repaired.
s.zh: 他们正将一艘严重损坏的船只从维尔京群岛运往迈阿密进行修理。

s.en: During the journey, their boat began to sink.
s.zh: 在旅途中，他们的船开始下沉了。

s.en: They quickly loaded a small rubber dinghy with food, matches, and cans of beer and rowed for a few miles across the Caribbean until they arrived at a tiny coral island.
s.zh: 他们迅速将食物、火柴和几罐啤酒装进了一艘小橡皮艇里，然后划船穿越了加勒比海，行驶了几英里，最终抵达了一个小小的珊瑚岛。

s.en: There were hardly any trees on the island and there was no water, but this did not prove to be a problem.
s.zh: 岛上几乎没有树木，也没有水源，但这并没有成为什么问题。

s.en: The men collected rainwater in the rubber dinghy.
s.zh: 他们用橡皮艇收集雨水。

s.en: As they had brought a spear gun with them, they had plenty to eat.
s.zh: 因为他们带了一支鱼枪，所以食物很充足。

s.en: They caught lobster and fish every day, and as one of them put it 'ate like kings'.
s.zh: 他们每天都会捕到龙虾和鱼，用其中一个人的话来说：“我们吃得像国王一样丰盛。”

s.en: When a passing tanker rescued them five days later, both men were genuinely sorry that they had to leave.
s.zh: 五天后，当一艘路过的油轮救起了他们时，两名男子都真心感到遗憾——因为他们不得不离开那里。

q: What was exceptional about the two men's stay on the desert island?
这两位男士在荒岛上的经历有什么特别之处呢？

s.en: After her husband had gone to work, Mrs. Richards sent her children to school and went upstairs to her bedroom.
s.zh: 在她丈夫上班后，理查兹夫人送孩子们去了学校，然后上楼去了自己的卧室。

s.en: She was too excited to do any housework that morning, for in the evening she would be going to a fancy-dress party with her husband.
s.zh: 那天早上她兴奋得根本无心做任何家务，因为晚上她要和丈夫一起去参加一个化装舞会。

s.en: She intended to dress up as a ghost and as she had made her costume the night before, she was impatient to try it on.
s.zh: 她打算打扮成鬼的样子，由于她前一天晚上就已经做好了服装，因此迫不及待地想试穿它了。

s.en: Though the costume consisted only of a sheet, it was very effective.
s.zh: 虽然这套服装只由一块床单制成，但效果非常好。

s.en: After putting it on, Mrs. Richards went downstairs.
s.zh: 穿上它之后，理查兹夫人下楼去了。

s.en: She wanted to find out whether it would be comfortable to wear.
s.zh: 她想知道穿起来是否舒适。

s.en: Just as Mrs. Richards was entering the dining-room, there was a knock on the front door.
s.zh: 就在理查兹夫人刚走进餐厅的时候，前门突然传来了敲门声。

s.en: She knew that it must be the baker.
s.zh: 她知道一定是面包师来了。

s.en: She had told him to come straight in if ever she failed to open the door and to leave the bread on the kitchen table.
s.zh: 她曾告诉他：如果她没能打开门，就直接进来，并把面包放在厨房的桌子上。

s.en: Not wanting to frighten the poor man, Mrs. Richards quickly hid in the small storeroom under the stairs.
s.zh: 为了不吓到那个可怜的人，理查兹夫人迅速躲进了楼梯下方的小储藏室里。

s.en: She heard the front door open and heavy footsteps in the hall.
s.zh: 她听到前门被打开的声音，以及大厅里沉重的脚步声。

s.en: Suddenly the door of the storeroom was opened and a man entered.
s.zh: 突然，储藏室的门被打开了，一个男人走了进来。

s.en: Mrs. Richards realized that it must be the man from the Electricity Board who had come to read the meter.
s.zh: 理查兹夫人意识到，来读取电表数据的肯定就是电力公司的工作人员。

s.en: She tried to explain the situation, saying
s.zh: 她试图解释当时的情况，说道：

s.en: 'It's only me', but it was too late.
s.zh: “是我。”但为时已晚。

s.en: The man let out a cry and jumped back several paces.
s.zh: 那个男人突然大叫一声，然后向后跳了几步。

s.en: When Mrs. Richards walked towards him, he fled, slamming the door behind him.
s.zh: 当理查兹夫人朝他走去时，他立刻逃跑了，并砰的一声关上身后的门。

q: What did the man expect to find under the stairs?
那个男人原本期望在楼梯下面找到什么呢？

s.en: There was a time when the owners of shops and businesses in Chicago had to pay large sums of money to gangsters in return for 'protection'.
s.zh: 曾经有一段时间，芝加哥的商店和企业的老板们不得不向黑帮支付巨额费用，以换取他们的“保护”。

s.en: If the money was not paid promptly, the gangsters would quickly put a man out of business by destroying his shop.
s.zh: 如果钱没有及时支付，黑帮分子会迅速毁掉他的店铺，让他破产。

s.en: Obtaining 'protection money' is not a modern crime.
s.zh: 收取“保护费”这种行为其实并非现代才有的犯罪行为。

s.en: As long ago as the fourteenth century, an Englishman, Sir John Hawkwood, made the remarkable discovery that people would rather pay large sums of money than have their life work destroyed by gangsters.
s.zh: 早在十四世纪，一位名叫约翰·霍克伍德（Sir John Hawkwood）的英国人就发现了一个惊人的事实：人们宁愿花大钱，也不愿自己的毕生心血被强盗毁掉。

s.en: Six hundred years ago, Sir John Hawkwood arrived in Italy with a band of soldiers and settled near Florence.
s.zh: 六百年前，约翰·霍克伍德带着一队士兵来到意大利，并在佛罗伦萨附近安顿下来。

s.en: He soon made a name for himself and came to be known to the Italians as Giovanni Acuto.
s.zh: 他很快就声名鹊起，在意大利人中被称为乔瓦尼·阿库托（Giovanni Acuto）。

s.en: Whenever the Italian city-states were at war with each other, Hawkwood used to hire his soldiers to princes who were willing to pay the high price he demanded.
s.zh: 每当意大利各城邦之间发生战争时，霍克伍德就会把他的士兵出租给那些愿意出高价的王子们。

s.en: In times of peace, when business was bad, Hawkwood and his men would march into a city-state, and after burning down a few farms, would offer to go away if protection money was paid to them.
s.zh: 在和平时期，当没生意可做时，霍克伍德和他的手下就会开进某个城邦，烧毁几个农场，然后提出只要付给他们保护费，他们就会离开。

s.en: Hawkwood made large sums of money in this way.
s.zh: 霍克伍德就是通过这种方式赚到了大量的钱。

s.en: In spite of this, the Italians regarded him as a sort of hero.
s.zh: 尽管如此，意大利人仍将他视为一位英雄。

s.en: When he died at the age of eighty, the Florentines gave him a state funeral and had a picture painted which was dedicated to the memory of 'the most valiant soldier and most notable leader, Signor Giovanni Haukodue'.
s.zh: 他八十岁去世时，佛罗伦萨人为他举行了国葬，还请人画了一幅像，以纪念'最勇敢的战士和最杰出的领袖，乔瓦尼·阿库托先生'。

q: How did Hawkwood make money in times of peace?
霍克伍德在和平时期是如何赚钱的？

s.en: Children always appreciate small gifts of money.
s.zh: 孩子们总是很乐意接受小额的金钱礼物。

s.en: Mum or dad, of course, provides a regular supply of pocket money, but uncles and aunts are always a source of extra income.
s.zh: 当然，爸爸妈妈会定期给他们零花钱，但叔叔阿姨们也是他们额外的收入来源。

s.en: With some children, small sums go a long way.
s.zh: 对一些孩子来说，这些小额的钱可以派上大用场。

s.en: If fifty pence pieces are not exchanged for sweets, they rattle for months inside money boxes.
s.zh: 如果五十便士硬币没有被用来买糖果，它们就会在存钱罐里待上好几个月。

s.en: Only very thrifty children manage to fill up a money box.
s.zh: 只有非常节俭的孩子才能真正把存钱罐填满。

s.en: For most of them, fifty pence is a small price to pay for a nice big bar of chocolate.
s.zh: 对大多数孩子来说，五十便士不过是买一块美味巧克力的小小代价罢了。

s.en: My nephew, George, has a money box but it is always empty.
s.zh: 我的侄子乔治有一个存钱罐，但里面总是空空如也。

s.en: Very few of the fifty pence pieces and pound coins I have given him have found their way there.
s.zh: 我给他的那些五十便士硬币和一英镑硬币，几乎没有一个真正进了那个存钱罐。

s.en: I gave him fifty pence yesterday and advised him to save it.
s.zh: 昨天我又给了他五十便士，并建议他要把钱存起来。

s.en: Instead, he bought himself fifty pence worth of trouble.
s.zh: 相反，他给自己惹来了价值五十便士的麻烦。

s.en: On his way to the sweet shop, he dropped his fifty pence and it bounced along the pavement and then disappeared down a drain.
s.zh: 在去糖果店的路上，他掉了那50便士硬币；硬币沿着人行道弹跳着滚去，最后掉进了下水道里不见了。

s.en: George took off his jacket,
s.zh: 乔治脱下了他的夹克。

s.en: rolled up his sleeves and pushed his right arm through the drain cover.
s.zh: 他卷起了袖子，然后将右臂伸进了排水口的盖子里。

s.en: He could not find his 50 pence piece anywhere, and what is more, he could not get his arm out.
s.zh: 他到处都找不到那枚50便士的硬币，而且更糟糕的是，他的手臂还拔不出来了。

s.en: A crowd of people gathered round him and a lady rubbed his arm with soap and butter, but George was firmly stuck.
s.zh: 一群人围了上来，一位女士用肥皂和黄油涂抹他的手臂，但乔治还是被卡得牢牢的。

s.en: The fire brigade was called and two fire fighters freed George using a special type of grease.
s.zh: 消防队被叫来了，两名消防员用一种特殊的润滑剂把乔治解救了出来。

s.en: George was not too upset by his experience because the lady who owns the sweet shop heard about his troubles and rewarded him with a large box of chocolates.
s.zh: 乔治对他的遭遇并不太在意，因为那家糖果店的老板听说了他的麻烦后，送了他一盒大巧克力作为奖励。

q: Did George get anything for his fifty pence? What?
乔治用那五十便士得到了什么吗？是什么？

s.en: Mary and her husband Dimitri lived in the tiny village of Perachora in southern Greece.
s.zh: 玛丽和她的丈夫迪米特里住在希腊南部的佩拉乔拉小村庄。

s.en: One of Mary's prize possessions was a little white lamb which her husband had given her.
s.zh: 玛丽最珍贵的财产之一是她丈夫送给她的一只小白羊。

s.en: She kept it tied to a tree in a field during the day and went to fetch it every evening.
s.zh: 白天，她把它绑在田里的一棵树上，每天晚上都去拿。

s.en: One evening, however, the lamb was missing.
s.zh: 然而，有一天晚上，小羊不见了。

s.en: The rope had been cut, so it was obvious that the lamb had been stolen.
s.zh: 绳子被剪断了，很明显小羊被偷了。

s.en: When Dimitri came in from the fields, his wife told him what had happened.
s.zh: 迪米特里从田里回来时，他的妻子告诉了他发生了什么事。

s.en: Dimitri at once set out to find the thief.
s.zh: 迪米特里立刻出发去找小偷。

s.en: He knew it would not prove difficult in such a small village.
s.zh: 他知道在这样一个小村庄里并不难。

s.en: After telling several of his friends about the theft,
s.zh: 迪米特里告诉几个朋友失窃的事后，

s.en: Dimitri found out that his neighbour, Aleko, had suddenly acquired a new lamb.
s.zh: 发现他的邻居阿列科突然买了一只新羊羔。

s.en: Dimitri immediately went to Aleko's house and angrily accused him of stealing the lamb.
s.zh: 迪米特里立刻去了阿列科家，愤怒地指责他偷了羔羊。

s.en: He told him he had better return it or he would call the police.
s.zh: 迪米特里告诉阿列科，最好把羊还给他，否则他就报警。

s.en: Aleko denied taking it and led Dimitri into his back-yard.
s.zh: 阿列科否认拿走了它，并把迪米特里带进了他的后院。

s.en: It was true that he had just bought a lamb, he explained,
s.zh: 他解释说，他确实刚买了一只小羊，

s.en: but his lamb was black.
s.zh: 但他的小羊是黑色的。

s.en: Ashamed of having acted so rashly, Dimitri apologized to Aleko for having accused him.
s.zh: 迪米特里为自己的鲁莽行为感到羞愧，向阿列科道歉，因为他指责了阿列科。

s.en: While they were talking it began to rain and Dimitri stayed in Aleko's house until the rain stopped.
s.zh: 他们说话的时候，天开始下雨了，迪米特里一直呆在阿列科的房子里，直到雨停了。

s.en: When he went outside half an hour later, he was astonished to find that the little black lamb was almost white.
s.zh: 半小时后，当他走到外面时，他惊讶地发现小黑羊几乎是白色的。

s.en: Its wool, which had been dyed black, had been washed clean by the rain!
s.zh: 它的羊毛被染成了黑色，被雨水洗得干干净净！

s.en: Verrazano, an Italian about whom little is known, sailed into New York Harbour in 1524 and named it Angouleme.
s.zh: 维拉扎诺（Verrazano）是一位鲜为人知的意大利人。他在1524年航行至纽约港，并将其命名为“昂古莱姆”（Angouleme）。

s.en: He described it as 'a very agreeable situation located within two small hills in the midst of which flowed a great river.'
s.zh: 他将其描述为“一个非常宜人的地方，位于两座小山之间；这两座小山中间流淌着一条大河。”

s.en: Though Verrazano is by no means considered to be a great explorer, his name will probably remain immortal,
s.zh: 虽然维拉扎诺绝不能被视为一位伟大的探险家，但他的名字很可能会永垂不朽。

s.en: for on November 21st, 1964, the longest suspension bridge in the world was named after him.
s.zh: 因为在1964年11月21日，世界上最长的悬索桥被以他的名字命名。

s.en: The Verrazano Bridge, which was designed by Othmar Ammann, joins Brooklyn to Staten Island.
s.zh: 维拉扎诺大桥（Verrazano Bridge）由奥特马尔·阿曼（Othmar Ammann）设计，它连接了布鲁克林（Brooklyn）和斯塔滕岛（Staten Island）。

s.en: It has a span of 4,260 feet.
s.zh: 它的跨度为 4,260 英尺。

s.en: The bridge is so long that the shape of the earth had to be taken into account by its designer.
s.zh: 这座桥非常长，以至于设计者必须考虑到地球的曲率。

s.en: Two great towers support four huge cables.
s.zh: 两座高大的塔架支撑着四根巨大的缆绳。

s.en: The towers are built on immense underwater platforms made of steel and concrete.
s.zh: 这些塔架建在巨大的水下平台上，这些平台由钢铁和混凝土制成。

s.en: The platforms extend to a depth of over 100 feet under the sea.
s.zh: 这些平台延伸至海面下100英尺以上的深度。

s.en: These alone took sixteen months to build.
s.zh: 仅这些部分的建设就花费了十六个月的时间。

s.en: Above the surface of the water, the towers rise to a height of nearly 700 feet.
s.zh: 在水面之上，这些塔楼的高度接近700英尺。

s.en: They support the cables from which the bridge has been suspended.
s.zh: 它们支撑着悬挂着桥梁的缆绳。

s.en: Each of the four cables contains 26,108 lengths of wire.
s.zh: 这四根缆绳中的每一根都包含26,108股钢丝。

s.en: It has been estimated that if the bridge were packed with cars, it would still only be carrying a third of its total capacity.
s.zh: 据估计，即使这座桥上挤满了汽车，它所承载的重量也仅相当于其总承载能力的三分之一。

s.en: However, size and strength are not the only important things about this bridge.
s.zh: 然而，这座桥的重要性并不仅仅体现在它的规模和承重能力上。

s.en: Despite its immensity, it is both simple and elegant,
s.zh: 尽管它规模庞大，但它却既简洁又优雅。

s.en: fulfilling its designer's dream to create 'an enormous object drawn as faintly as possible'.
s.zh: 实现了设计师的梦想：创造出一个“尽可能轻描淡写地勾勒出的庞然大物”。

q: How is the bridge supported?
这座桥是如何被支撑起来的？

s.en: Modern sculpture rarely surprises us any more.
s.zh: 现代雕塑已很少再让我们感到惊讶。

s.en: The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken.
s.zh: 认为现代艺术只能在博物馆里看到，这种看法是错误的。

s.en: Even people who take no interest in art cannot have failed to notice examples of modern sculpture on display in public places.
s.zh: 即使对艺术毫无兴趣的人，也不可能注意不到公共场所里展出的现代雕塑。

s.en: Strange forms stand in gardens, and outside buildings and shops.
s.zh: 奇形怪状的雕塑矗立在花园里、建筑物和商店外面。

s.en: We have got quite used to them.
s.zh: 我们已经习惯了它们的存在。

s.en: Some so-called 'modern' pieces have been on display for nearly eighty years.
s.zh: 有些所谓的“现代”艺术品已经展出了近八十年。

s.en: In spite of this, some people--including myself--were surprised by a recent exhibition of modern sculpture.
s.zh: 尽管如此，包括我在内的一些人，还是被最近的一场现代雕塑展览所震撼。

s.en: The first thing I saw when I entered the art gallery was a notice which said: 'Do not touch the exhibits, some of them are dangerous!'
s.zh: 当我走进艺术画廊时，首先看到的是一张告示，上面写着：“请勿触摸展品，其中一些具有危险性！”

s.en: The objects on display were pieces of moving sculpture.
s.zh: 展出的作品都是动态雕塑。

s.en: Oddly shaped forms that are suspended from the ceiling and move in response to a gust of wind are quite familiar to everybody.
s.zh: 那些形状奇特、悬挂在天花板上的物体，会随着一阵风吹动而移动——这种景象对每个人来说都十分熟悉。

s.en: These objects, however, were different.
s.zh: 然而，这些物体有所不同。

s.en: Lined up against the wall, there were long thin wires attached to metal spheres.
s.zh: 靠墙排列着一排排细长的金属丝，每根都连接着一个金属球。

s.en: The spheres had been magnetized and attracted or repelled each other all the time.
s.zh: 这些球体被磁化了，因此它们会不断地相互吸引或相互排斥。

s.en: In the centre of the hall,
s.zh: 在大厅的中央，

s.en: there were a number of tall structures which contained coloured lights.
s.zh: 矗立着许多高大的结构，上面装有彩色的灯光。

s.en: These lights flickered continuously like traffic lights which have gone mad.
s.zh: 这些灯光不停地闪烁，就像那些失控的交通信号灯一样。

s.en: Sparks were emitted from small black boxes and red lamps flashed on and off angrily.
s.zh: 从小巧的黑色盒子中迸发出火花；红色的灯泡则愤怒地闪烁着。

s.en: It was rather like an exhibition of prehistoric electronic equipment.
s.zh: 这有点像一场展示史前电子设备的展览。

s.en: These peculiar forms not only seemed designed to shock people emotionally, but to give them electric shocks as well!
s.zh: 这些奇特的设计不仅旨在从情感上震撼人们，还似乎能够让他们真的触电！

q: How might some of the exhibits have been dangerous?
有些展品可能会有什么危险？

s.en: Kidnappers are rarely interested in animals, but they recently took considerable interest in Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay's cat.
s.zh: 绑匪通常对动物不感兴趣，但他们最近却对埃莉诺·拉姆齐夫人的猫产生了浓厚的兴趣。

s.en: Mrs. Eleanor Ramsay, a very wealthy old lady, has shared a flat with her cat, Rastus, for a great many years.
s.zh: 埃莉诺·拉姆齐夫人是一位非常富有的老太太，她多年来一直和她的猫拉斯图斯合住一套公寓。

s.en: Rastus leads an orderly life.
s.zh: 拉斯图斯的生活非常有规律。

s.en: He usually takes a short walk in the evenings and is always home by seven o'clock.
s.zh: 他通常在傍晚散会儿步，并且总是在七点前回家。

s.en: One evening, however, he failed to arrive.
s.zh: 然而，一天晚上他没有按时回家。

s.en: Mrs. Ramsay got very worried.
s.zh: 拉姆齐夫人非常担心。

s.en: She looked everywhere for him but could not find him.
s.zh: 她到处找他，但没能找到。

s.en: Three days after Rastus' disappearance, Mrs. Ramsay received an anonymous letter.
s.zh: 拉斯图斯失踪三天后，拉姆齐夫人收到了一封匿名信。

s.en: The writer stated that Rastus was in safe hands and would be returned immediately if Mrs. Ramsay paid a ransom of ￡1,000.
s.zh: 写信人声称拉斯图斯安然无恙，如果拉姆齐夫人支付1000英镑的赎金，他会立即被送回。

s.en: Mrs. Ramsay was instructed to place the money in a cardboard box and to leave it outside her door.
s.zh: 拉姆齐夫人被要求把钱放在一个纸板箱里，然后把它放在门外。

s.en: At first, she decided to go to the police,
s.zh: 起初，她决定去报警，

s.en: but fearing that she would never see Rastus again--the letter had made that quite clear--she changed her mind.
s.zh: 但害怕再也见不到拉斯图斯——信里已经说得很清楚了——她改变了主意。

s.en: She withdrew ￡1000 from her bank and followed the kidnapper's instructions.
s.zh: 她从银行取了1000英镑，并按照绑匪的指示做了。

s.en: The next morning, the box had disappeared but Mrs. Ramsay was sure that the kidnapper would keep his word.
s.zh: 第二天早上，箱子不见了，但拉姆齐夫人确信绑匪会信守承诺。

s.en: Sure enough, Rastus arrived punctually at seven o'clock that evening.
s.zh: 果然，那天晚上七点整，拉斯图斯准时回来了。

s.en: He looked very well, though he was rather thirsty, for he drank half a bottle of milk.
s.zh: 他看起来很好，只是相当渴，因为他喝了半瓶牛奶。

s.en: The police were astounded when Mrs. Ramsay told them what she had done.
s.zh: 当拉姆齐夫人告诉警察她做了什么时，他们都非常震惊。

s.en: She explained that Rastus was very dear to her.
s.zh: 她解释说拉斯图斯对她来说非常珍贵。

s.en: Considering the amount she paid, he was dear in more ways than one!
s.zh: 考虑到她支付的金额，他可真是“昂贵”啊！

q: Why was Rastus 'very dear' in more ways than one?
拉斯图斯为什么在不止一种意义上都很“贵”？

s.en: In 1908 Lord Northcliffe offered a prize of ￡1,000 to the first man who would fly across the English Channel.
s.zh: 1908年，诺斯克利夫勋爵（Lord Northcliffe）宣布设立一项奖金，金额为1,000英镑，奖励第一个成功飞越英吉利海峡的人。

s.en: Over a year passed before the first attempt was made.
s.zh: 一年多过去了，才有人进行第一次尝试。

s.en: On July 19th, 1909, in the early morning,
Hubert Latham took off from the French coast in his plane the 'Antoinette IV.'
s.zh: 休伯特·拉瑟姆驾驶他的飞机“安托瓦内特IV号”从法国海岸起飞了。

s.en: He had travelled only seven miles across the Channel when his engine failed and he was forced to land on the sea.
s.zh: 他刚刚飞越英吉利海峡七英里，引擎就发生了故障，他不得不迫降在海面上。

s.en: The 'Antoinette' floated on the water until Latham was picked up by a ship.
s.zh: “安托瓦内特”号漂浮在水面上，直到拉瑟姆被一艘船救起。

s.en: Two days later, Louis Bleriot arrived near Calais with a plane called 'No.XI'.
s.zh: 两天后，路易·布莱里奥驾驶着一架名为“No.XI”的飞机抵达了加莱附近。

s.en: Bleriot had been making planes since 1905 and this was his latest model.
s.zh: 布莱里奥自1905年起就开始制造飞机，而这架飞机是他最新的设计作品。

s.en: A week before, he had completed a successful overland flight during which he covered twenty-six miles.
s.zh: 一周前，他完成了一次成功的陆上飞行，飞行距离达到了26英里。

s.en: Latham, however, did not give up easily.
s.zh: 然而，拉瑟姆并没有轻易放弃。

s.en: He, too, arrived near Calais on the same day with a new 'Antoinette'.
s.zh: 他也在同一天，驾驶一架新的“安托瓦内特”号飞机，抵达了加莱附近。

s.en: It looked as if there would be an exciting race across the Channel.
s.zh: 看起来将会有一场跨越英吉利海峡的精彩比赛。

s.en: Both planes were going to take off on July 25th, but Latham failed to get up early enough.
s.zh: 这两架飞机都原定于7月25日起飞，但拉瑟姆没能及时起床。

s.en: After making a short test flight at 4.15 a.m., Bleriot set off half an hour later.
s.zh: 在凌晨4点15分进行了一次短暂的试飞后，布莱里奥于半小时后出发了。

s.en: His great flight lasted thirty-seven minutes.
s.zh: 他的这次精彩飞行持续了三十七分钟。

s.en: When he landed near Dover, the first person to greet him was a local policeman.
s.zh: 当他降落在多佛附近时，第一个迎接他的是一名当地警察。

s.en: Latham made another attempt a week later and got within half a mile of Dover,
s.zh: 一周后，拉瑟姆再次尝试，最终距离多佛仅剩下半英里。

s.en: but he was unlucky again.
s.zh: 但他又一次运气不佳了。

s.en: His engine failed and he landed on the sea for the second time.
s.zh: 他的引擎发生了故障，他第二次降落在海面上。

q: What was the name of the first plane to fly across the English Channel?
第一架飞越英吉利海峡的飞机叫什么名字？

s.en: Boxing matches were very popular in England two hundred years ago.
s.zh: 两百年前，拳击比赛在英格兰非常流行。

s.en: In those days, boxers fought with bare fists for prize money.
s.zh: 在那个时候，拳击手们为了奖金而徒手搏斗。

s.en: Because of this, they were known as 'prizefighters'.
s.zh: 正因如此，他们被称为“职业拳击手”（prizefighters）。

s.en: However, boxing was very crude,
s.zh: 然而，当时的拳击运动还非常粗糙，

s.en: for there were no rules and a prizefighter could be seriously injured or even killed during a match.
s.zh: 因为当时没有任何规则可言，拳击手在比赛中很可能会受到严重伤害，甚至丧命。

s.en: One of the most colourful figures in boxing history was Daniel Mendoza, who was born in 1764.
s.zh: 拳击历史上最富有传奇色彩的人物之一是丹尼尔·门多萨（Daniel Mendoza），他出生于1764年。

s.en: The use of gloves was not introduced until 1860, when the Marquis of Queensberry drew up the first set of rules.
s.zh: 手套的使用直到1860年才被引入；那一年，昆斯贝里侯爵制定了第一套比赛规则。

s.en: Though he was technically a prizefighter,
s.zh: 虽然从技术上讲他是一名职业拳击手，

s.en: Mendoza did much to change crude prizefighting into a sport, for he brought science to the game.
s.zh: 门多萨为将这种原始的拳击比赛转变为一项体育运动做出了巨大贡献，因为他为这项运动引入了科学。

s.en: In his day, Mendoza enjoyed tremendous popularity.
s.zh: 在门多萨的时代，他享有极高的声望。

s.en: He was adored by rich and poor alike.
s.zh: 无论贫富，大家都非常喜爱他。

s.en: Mendoza rose to fame swiftly after a boxing match when he was only fourteen years old.
s.zh: 门多萨在十四岁时参加了一场拳击比赛后，迅速成名。

s.en: This attracted the attention of Richard Humphries who was then the most eminent boxer in England.
s.zh: 这引起了理查德·汉弗莱斯（Richard Humphries）的注意，他当时是英格兰最著名的拳击手。

s.en: He offered to train Mendoza and his young pupil was quick to learn.
s.zh: 他主动提出训练门多萨，而他的这位年轻学生学得很快。

s.en: In fact, Mendoza soon became so successful that Humphries turned against him.
s.zh: 事实上，门多萨很快就取得了巨大的成功，以至于汉弗莱斯转而与他为敌。

s.en: The two men quarrelled bitterly and it was clear that the argument could only be settled by a fight.
s.zh: 这两个人激烈地争吵起来，很明显，这场争执只能通过打架来解决。

s.en: A match was held at Stilton, where both men fought for an hour.
s.zh: 比赛在斯蒂尔顿举行，两人打了一个小时。

s.en: The public bet a great deal of money on Mendoza, but he was defeated.
s.zh: 公众在门多萨身上下了巨额赌注，但他被击败了。

s.en: Mendoza met Humphries in the ring on a later occasion and he lost for a second time.
s.zh: 后来，门多萨在拳击场上再次与汉弗莱斯相遇，但他又一次输了。

s.en: It was not until his third match in 1790 that he finally beat Humphries and became Champion of England.
s.zh: 直到1790年的第三次比赛，他才终于击败了汉弗莱斯，成为英格兰冠军。

s.en: Meanwhile, he founded a highly successful Academy and even Lord Byron became one of his pupils.
s.zh: 与此同时，他创办了一所非常成功的拳击学校，连拜伦勋爵也成了他的学生。

s.en: He earned enormous sums of money and was paid as much as ￡100 for a single appearance.
s.zh: 他赚了巨额的钱，单次出场费就高达100英镑。

s.en: Despite this, he was so extravagant that he was always in debt.
s.zh: 尽管如此，他挥霍无度，总是负债累累。

s.en: After he was defeated by a boxer called Gentleman Jackson, he was quickly forgotten.
s.zh: 在被一位名叫“绅士杰克逊”的拳击手击败后，他很快就被遗忘了。

s.en: He was sent to prison for failing to pay his debts and died in poverty in 1836.
s.zh: 他因无力偿还债务而被送进监狱，并于1836年在贫困中去世。

q: How many unsuccessful attempts did Mendoza make before becoming Champion of all England?
门多萨在成为全英格兰冠军之前，失败了多少次？

s.en: Some plays are so successful that they run for years on end.
s.zh: 有些剧目非常成功，以至于可以连续上演多年。

s.en: In many ways, this is unfortunate for the poor actors who are required to go on repeating the same lines night after night.
s.zh: 在很多方面，这对那些可怜的演员来说确实很不公平——他们不得不夜复一夜地重复同样的台词。

s.en: One would expect them to know their parts by heart and never have cause to falter.
s.zh: 人们会以为他们早就把台词背得滚瓜烂熟，永远不会有结巴的时候。

s.en: Yet this is not always the case.
s.zh: 然而，情况并不总是如此。

s.en: A famous actor in a highly successful play was once cast in the role of an aristocrat who had been imprisoned in the Bastille for twenty years.
s.zh: 一位在非常成功的戏剧中表现出色的著名演员，曾饰演过这样一个角色：一位被关押在巴士底狱长达二十年的贵族。

s.en: In the last act, a gaoler would always come on to the stage with a letter which he would hand to the prisoner.
s.zh: 在最后一幕中，总是会有一个狱卒走上舞台，递给囚犯一封信。

s.en: Even though the noble was expected to read the letter at each performance, he always insisted that it should be written out in full.
s.zh: 尽管人们期望这位贵族在每次演出时都能宣读这封信，但他始终坚持要求必须把信的内容完整地写出来。

s.en: One night, the gaoler decided to play a joke on his colleague to find out if,
s.zh: 一天晚上，狱卒决定捉弄他的同事，想看看经过这么多次表演后，他是否已经把信的内容背下来了。

s.en: after so many performances, he had managed to learn the contents of the letter by heart.
s.zh: 戏剧的最后一幕开始了：那位贵族独自坐在黑暗的牢房里，被关在铁栅栏后面。

s.en: The curtain went up on the final act of the play and revealed the aristocrat sitting alone behind bars in his dark cell.
s.zh: 就在这时，狱卒出现了，他手里拿着那封珍贵的信。

s.en: Just then, the gaoler appeared with the precious letter in his hands.
s.zh: 他走进牢房，将那封信交给了那位贵族。

s.en: He entered the cell and presented the letter to the aristocrat.
s.zh: 但他递给他的那份信并没有像往常一样写满字。

s.en: But the copy he gave him had not been written out in full as usual.
s.zh: 那只是一张空白的纸而已。

s.en: It was simply a blank sheet of paper.
s.zh: 狱卒热切地注视着，急于想知道他的搭档演员是否终于记住了台词。

s.en: The gaoler looked on eagerly, anxious to see if his fellow actor had at last learnt his lines.
s.zh: 那位贵族盯着那张空白的纸张看了几秒钟。

s.en: The noble stared at the blank sheet of paper for a few seconds.
s.zh: 然后，他眯起眼睛说：“光线太暗了。把那封信读给我听吧。”

s.en: Then, squinting his eyes, he said: 'The light is dim. Read the letter to me.'
s.zh: 然后他立刻把那张纸交给了狱卒。

s.en: And he promptly handed the sheet of paper to the gaoler.
s.zh: 结果狱卒发现自己也一个字都记不起来。

s.en: Finding that he could not remember a word of the letter either,
s.zh: 狱卒回答说：“光线确实很暗，大人。我得去拿我的眼镜。”

s.en: the gaoler replied: 'The light is indeed dim, sire.  I must get my glasses.  '
s.zh: 说完这些，他便匆忙走下了舞台。

s.en: With this, he hurried off the stage.
s.zh: 让贵族觉得好笑的是，

s.en: Much to the aristocrat's amusement,
s.zh: 过了一会儿，狱卒拿着一副眼镜和那封熟悉的信回来了，然后开始把信的内容读给囚犯听。

s.en: the gaoler returned a few moments later with a pair of glasses and the usual copy of the letter which he proceeded to read to the prisoner.

q: Which actor read the letter in the end, the aristocrat or the gaoler?
最后是谁读了那封信——是那位贵族，还是狱卒？

lessons.t: One man's meat is another man's poison

s.en: People become quite illogical when they try to decide what can be eaten and what cannot be eaten.
s.zh: 当人们试图决定什么能吃、什么不能吃时，他们的想法会变得非常不合逻辑。

s.en: If you lived in the Mediterranean, for instance, you would consider octopus a great delicacy.
s.zh: 例如，如果你生活在地中海地区，你会认为章鱼是一种非常美味的佳肴。

s.en: You would not be able to understand why some people find it repulsive.
s.zh: 你无法理解为什么有些人会觉得它令人反感。

s.en: On the other hand, your stomach would turn at the idea of frying potatoes in animal fat-the normally accepted practice in many northern countries.
s.zh: 另一方面，一想到要用动物油脂来煎土豆，你就会感到恶心——而在许多北方国家，这种做法却是被普遍接受的。

s.en: The sad truth is that most of us have been brought up to eat certain foods and we stick to them all our lives.
s.zh: 令人遗憾的事实是，我们大多数人都被教导要吃某些特定的食物，并且一生都坚持吃这些食物。

s.en: No creature has received more praise and abuse than the common garden snail.
s.zh: 没有哪种生物像普通的花园蜗牛那样，既备受赞誉，又饱受诟病。

s.en: Cooked in wine, snails are a great luxury in various parts of the world.
s.zh: 用葡萄酒烹制的蜗牛，在世界各地都被视为一种高级的美食。

s.en: There are countless people who, ever since their early years, have learned to associate snails with food.
s.zh: 有无数的人，从很小的时候起，就学会了将蜗牛与食物联系在一起。

s.en: My friend, Robert, lives in a country where snails are despised.
s.zh: 我的朋友罗伯特住在一个人们非常厌恶蜗牛的国家。

s.en: As his flat is in a large town, he has no garden of his own.
s.zh: 由于他的公寓位于一个较大的城镇里，所以他并没有自己的花园。

s.en: For years he has been asking me to collect snails from my garden and take them to him.
s.zh: 多年来，他一直让我从我的花园里采集蜗牛，然后带给他。

s.en: The idea never appealed to me very much, but one day, after a heavy shower,
s.zh: 这个想法我一直不太感兴趣，但有一天，在一场大雨之后，

s.en: I happened to be walking in my garden when I noticed a huge number of snails taking a stroll on some of my prize plants.
s.zh: 我正好在花园里散步，突然发现大量的蜗牛正在我的那些珍贵的植物上爬来爬去。

s.en: Acting on a sudden impulse, I collected several dozen, put them in a paper bag, and took them to Robert.
s.zh: 一时冲动之下，我收集了几十只蜗牛，把它们装进一个纸袋里，然后拿给了罗伯特。

s.en: Robert was delighted to see me and equally pleased with my little gift.
s.zh: 罗伯特见到我非常高兴，对我的小礼物也同样感到满意。

s.en: I left the bag in the hall and Robert and I went into the living room where we talked for a couple of hours.
s.zh: 我把袋子放在门厅里，然后和罗伯特一起进了客厅，我们在那里聊了两个小时。

s.en: I had forgotten all about the snails when Robert suddenly said that I must stay to dinner.
s.zh: 我完全把那些蜗牛的事给忘了，直到罗伯特突然说：“你必须留下来吃晚饭。”

s.en: Snails would, of course, be the main dish.
s.zh: 当然，蜗牛会是主菜。

s.en: I did not fancy the idea and I reluctantly followed Robert out of the room.
s.zh: 我并不喜欢这个主意，但还是不情愿地跟着罗伯特走出了房间。

s.en: To our dismay,
s.zh: 令我们惊恐的是，

s.en: we saw that there were snails everywhere:
s.zh: 我们发现到处都有蜗牛。

s.en: they had escaped from the paper bag
s.zh: 它们从那个纸袋里逃出来了。

s.en: and had taken complete possession of the hall! I have never been able to look at a snail since then.
s.zh: 并且完全占领了门厅！从那以后，我再也没法看蜗牛了。

q: What was it about snails that made the writer collect them for his friend on that day in particular?
究竟是蜗牛的什么特性，让作者在那天特意为他的朋友收集了它们呢？

s.en: We often read in novels how a seemingly respectable person
s.zh: 我们在小说中经常看到这样的情节：一个表面上看起来很体面、值得尊敬的人

s.en: or family has some terrible secret which has been concealed from strangers for years.
s.zh: 或者家庭隐藏着一个可怕的秘密，这个秘密多年来一直被对外人隐瞒着。

s.en: The English language possesses a vivid saying to describe this sort of situation.
s.zh: 英语中有一句非常生动的表达，用来形容这种情况。

s.en: The terrible secret is called 'a skeleton in the cupboard'.
s.zh: 这个可怕的秘密就叫“柜中骷髅”。

s.en: At some dramatic moment in the story, the terrible secret becomes known and a reputation is ruined.
s.zh: 在故事中的某个关键时刻，那个可怕的秘密被揭露了，从而导致一个人的声誉彻底毁掉。

s.en: The reader's hair stands on end when he reads in the final pages of the novel that the heroine,
s.zh: 当读者在小说最后几页读到，女主角——

s.en: a dear old lady who had always been so kind to everybody, had, in her youth, poisoned every one of her five husbands.
s.zh: 那位一直对所有人都很友善的老妇人——年轻时竟毒死了她的五位丈夫时，不禁毛骨悚然。

s.en: It is all very well for such things to occur in fiction.
s.zh: 这种事发生在小说里倒也罢了。

s.en: To varying degrees, we all have secrets which we do not want even our closest friends to learn,
s.zh: 在某种程度上，我们每个人都有自己不想让最亲密的朋友知道的秘密。

s.en: but few of us have skeletons in the cupboard.
s.zh: 但我们中很少有人真有“柜中骷髅”。

s.en: The only person I know who has a skeleton in the cupboard is George Carlton, and he is very proud of the fact.
s.zh: 我认识的唯一有“柜中骷髅”的人是乔治·卡尔顿，而且他还对此引以为豪。

s.en: George studied medicine in his youth.
s.zh: 乔治年轻时学习过医学。

s.en: Instead of becoming a doctor, however, he became a successful writer of detective stories.
s.zh: 然而，他并没有成为医生，而是成为了一名成功的侦探小说作家。

s.en: I once spent an uncomfortable weekend which I shall never forget at his house.
s.zh: 我曾在他的家里度过了一个极其不愉快的周末，那个经历我永远都不会忘记。

s.en: George showed me to the guestroom which, he said, was rarely used.
s.zh: 乔治带我去了客房，他说这个房间很少有人使用。

s.en: He told me to unpack my things and then come down to dinner.
s.zh: 他让我先把行李收拾好，然后再下来吃晚饭。

s.en: After I had stacked my shirts and underclothes in two empty drawers, I decided to hang one of the two suits I had brought with me in the cupboard.
s.zh: 我把衬衫和内衣整理好后，放进了两个空抽屉里；接着，我决定把带来的两套西装中的一套挂在衣柜里。

s.en: I opened the cupboard door and then stood in front of it petrified.
s.zh: 我打开了橱柜的门，然后站在那里，吓得动弹不得。

s.en: A skeleton was dangling before my eyes.
s.zh: 一具骷髅悬挂在我的眼前。

s.en: The sudden movement of the door made it sway slightly and it gave me the impression that it was about to leap out at me.
s.zh: 门的突然晃动让它也跟着摇摆起来，给我的感觉是它好像要朝我扑过来似的。

s.en: Dropping my suit, I dashed downstairs to tell George.
s.zh: 我立刻放下西装，冲下楼去告诉乔治。

s.en: This was worse than 'a terrible secret'; this was a real skeleton!
s.zh: 这比“一个可怕的秘密”还要糟糕；那简直是一具真正的骷髅！

s.en: But George was unsympathetic.
s.zh: 但乔治却毫无同情之心。

s.en: 'Oh, that,' he said with a smile as if he were talking about an old friend.
s.zh: “哦，那个啊，”他笑着说，仿佛在谈论一个老朋友一样，

s.en: 'That's Sebastian. You forget that I was a medical student once upon a time.'
s.zh: “那是塞巴斯蒂安。你忘了，我曾经也是一名医学生。”

q: Who was Sebastian?
塞巴斯蒂安是谁？

s.en: One of the most famous sailing ships of the nineteenth century, the Cutty Sark, can still be seen at Greenwich.
s.zh: 作为19世纪最著名的帆船之一，“Cutty Sark”至今仍可以在格林尼治博物馆看到。

s.en: She stands on dry land and is visited by thousands of people each year.
s.zh: 她站在陆地上，每年都有成千上万的人前来参观她。

s.en: She serves as an impressive reminder of the great ships of the past.
s.zh: 它令人印象深刻，使人想起昔日那些宏伟的帆船。

s.en: Before they were replaced by steamships,
s.zh: 在它们被蒸汽船取代之前，

s.en: sailing vessels like the Cutty Sark were used to carry tea from China and wool from Australia.
s.zh: 像“Cutty Sark”这样的帆船曾被用来从中国运输茶叶，从澳大利亚运输羊毛。

s.en: The Cutty Sark was one of the fastest sailing ships that has ever been built.
s.zh: “Cutty Sark”是有史以来建造的最快的帆船之一。

s.en: The only other ship to match her was the Thermopylae.
s.zh: 唯一能与她相媲美的船只就是“Thermopylae”号了。

s.en: Both these ships set out from Shanghai on June 18th, 1872 on an exciting race to England.
s.zh: 这两艘船都于1872年6月18日从上海出发，参加了一场前往英国的激动人心的竞赛。

s.en: This race, which went on for exactly four months, was the last of its kind.
s.zh: 这场比赛持续了整整四个月，也是这类比赛中的最后一场比赛。

s.en: It marked the end of the great tradition of ships with sails and the beginning of a new era.
s.zh: 这标志着帆船这一伟大传统的终结，以及一个新时代的开始。

s.en: The first of the two ships to reach Java after the race had begun was the Thermopylae,
s.zh: 在比赛开始后，最先抵达爪哇的两艘船只中，第一艘是“Thermopylae”号。

s.en: but on the Indian Ocean, the Cutty Sark took the lead.
s.zh: 但在印度洋上，库蒂·萨克号（Cutty Sark）却取得了领先地位。

s.en: It seemed certain that she would be the first ship home,
s.zh: 看起来她肯定会成为第一艘返抵英国的船。

s.en: but during the race she had a lot of bad luck.
s.zh: 但在比赛中，它遭遇了许多不幸。

s.en: In August, she was struck by a very heavy storm during which her rudder was torn away.
s.zh: 八月份，她遭遇了一场猛烈的风暴，风暴中她的舵被彻底损坏（即被风暴中的力量扯掉了）。

s.en: The Cutty Sark rolled from side to side and it became impossible to steer her.
s.zh: “Cutty Sark”号开始左右摇晃，根本无法再控制它的航向了。

s.en: A temporary rudder was made on board from spare planks and it was fitted with great difficulty.
s.zh: 他们在船上用多余的木板制作了一个临时舵，并且安装这个临时舵的过程非常困难。

s.en: This greatly reduced the speed of the ship, for there was a danger that if she travelled too quickly,
s.zh: 这大大降低了船的速度，因为如果船行驶得太快，就存在危险。

s.en: this rudder would be torn away as well.
s.zh: 这个舵也会被扯掉的。

s.en: Because of this, the Cutty Sark lost her lead.
s.zh: 正因如此，Cutty Sark失去了领先优势。

s.en: After crossing the Equator, the captain called in at a port to have a new rudder fitted,
s.zh: 在越过赤道后，船长停靠在一个港口，更换了船上的舵。

s.en: but by now the Thermopylae was over five hundred miles ahead.
s.zh: 但那时，Thermopylae号已经领先了五百多英里。

s.en: Though the new rudder was fitted at tremendous speed, it was impossible for the Cutty Sark to win.
s.zh: 尽管新的舵被迅速安装上了，Cutty Sark号还是无法赶上它。

s.en: She arrived in England a week after the Thermopylae.
s.zh: Cutty Sark号在Thermopylae号之后一周才抵达英格兰。

s.en: Even this was remarkable, considering that she had had so many delays.
s.zh: 考虑到途中经历了许多延误，这一成绩已经非常了不起了。

s.en: There is no doubt that if she had not lost her rudder she would have won the race easily.
s.zh: 毫无疑问，如果她没有失去舵，她本可以轻松赢得比赛。

q: What piece of bad luck prevented the Cutty Sark from winning the race?
是什么倒霉的事情导致“Cutty Sark”号没能赢得这场比赛呢？

s.en: No one can avoid being influenced by advertisements.
s.zh: 没有人能够完全不受广告的影响。

s.en: Much as we may pride ourselves on our good taste,
s.zh: 尽管我们常常为自己的品味感到自豪，

s.en: we are no longer free to choose the things we want,
s.zh: 但实际上我们已不再能够自由选择自己真正想要的东西，

s.en: for advertising exerts a subtle influence on us.
s.zh: 因为广告对我们产生了潜移默化的影响。

s.en: In their efforts to persuade us to buy this or that product,
s.zh: 为了说服我们购买某种产品，

s.en: advertisers have made a close study of human nature and have classified all our little weaknesses.
s.zh: 广告商们深入研究了人类的心理，并分类整理了我们所有的小弱点。

s.en: Advertisers discovered years ago that all of us love to get something for nothing.
s.zh: 多年前，广告商们就发现：我们都喜欢免费获得东西。

s.en: An advertisement which begins with the magic word FREE can rarely go wrong.
s.zh: 任何以“免费”这个词开头的广告几乎都不会失败。

s.en: These days, advertisers not only offer free samples,
s.zh: 如今，广告商们不仅提供免费样品，

s.en: but free cars, free houses, and free trips round the world as well.
s.zh: 还有免费的汽车、免费的房子，以及免费的环球旅行机会。

s.en: They devise hundreds of competitions which will enable us to win huge sums of money.
s.zh: 他们设计了数百种比赛，让我们有机会赢得巨额奖金。

s.en: Radio and television have made it possible for advertisers to capture the attention of millions of people in this way.
s.zh: 广播和电视使得广告商能够以这种方式吸引数百万人的注意力。

s.en: During a radio programme, a company of biscuit manufacturers once asked listeners to bake biscuits and send them to their factory.
s.zh: 在一次广播节目中，一家饼干制造商邀请听众们烤制饼干并寄到他们的工厂。

s.en: They offered to pay $10 a pound for the biggest biscuit baked by a listener.
s.zh: 他们提出愿意以每磅10美元的价格购买听众们烤制的最大尺寸的饼干。

s.en: The response to this competition was tremendous.
s.zh: 这次比赛的反响非常热烈。

s.en: Before long, biscuits of all shapes and sizes began arriving at the factory.
s.zh: 不久之后，各种形状和大小的饼干开始运送到工厂里。

s.en: One lady brought a biscuit on a wheelbarrow. It weighed nearly 500 pounds.
s.zh: 一位女士用手推车运来一块饼干，它重达近500磅。

s.en: A little later, a man came along with a biscuit which occupied the whole boot of his car.
s.zh: 过了一会儿，一个男人走了过来，他带来的饼干占据了他汽车整个后备箱的空间。

s.en: All the biscuits that were sent were carefully weighed.
s.zh: 所有被寄出的饼干都经过了仔细的称重。

s.en: The largest was 713 pounds. It seemed certain that this would win the prize.
s.zh: 最大的那个重达713磅；看起来它肯定会赢得这个奖项。

s.en: But just before the competition closed,
s.zh: 但在比赛即将结束之前，

s.en: a lorry arrived at the factory with a truly colossal biscuit which weighed 2,400 pounds.
s.zh: 一辆卡车将一块重量高达2,400磅的巨型饼干送到了工厂。

s.en: It had been baked by a college student who had used over 1,000 pounds of flour, 800 pounds of sugar,
s.zh: 这块饼干是由一名大学生烤制的；他用了超过1000磅的面粉和800磅的糖、

s.en: 200 pounds of fat, and 400 pounds of various other ingredients.
s.zh: 200磅的脂肪，以及400磅的其他各种成分。

s.en: It was so heavy that a crane had to be used to remove it from the lorry.
s.zh: 它太重了，必须使用起重机才能将其从卡车上卸下来。

s.en: The manufacturers had to pay more money than they had anticipated, for they bought the biscuit from the student for $24,000.
s.zh: 制造商们不得不支付比预期更多的钱，因为他们以24,000美元的价格从那位学生手中买下了这块饼干。

q: Who won the prize for the biggest biscuit?
谁赢得了“最大饼干”奖呢？

lessons.t: Nothing to sell and nothing to buy

s.en: It has been said that everyone lives by selling something.
s.zh: 有人说过，每个人都是通过出售某种东西来谋生的。

s.en: In the light of this statement, teachers live by selling knowledge,
s.zh: 根据这一说法，教师的工作就是通过传授知识来谋生。

s.en: philosophers by selling wisdom and priests by selling spiritual comfort.
s.zh: 哲学家通过传授智慧来谋生，而牧师则通过提供精神慰藉来获得收入。

s.en: Though it may be possible to measure the value of material goods in terms of money,
s.zh: 虽然可以用金钱来衡量物质财富的价值，

s.en: it is extremely difficult to estimate the true value of the services which people perform for us.
s.zh: 很难准确估计人们为我们提供的服务的真正价值。

s.en: There are times when we would willingly give everything we possess to save our lives,
s.zh: 有时候，为了挽救自己的生命，我们甚至愿意放弃自己拥有的一切。

s.en: yet we might grudge paying a surgeon a high fee for offering us precisely this service.
s.zh: 然而，外科医生为我们提供的恰恰是挽救生命的服务，我们却可能舍不得为此支付高额费用。

s.en: The conditions of society are such that skills have to be paid for in the same way that goods are paid for at a shop.
s.zh: 当前的社会状况决定了：技能的价值必须像商品在商店里被出售时那样，通过金钱来体现（即技能也需要通过金钱来获得）。

s.en: Everyone has something to sell.
s.zh: 每个人都有东西可以出售。

s.en: Tramps seem to be the only exception to this general rule.
s.zh: 流浪汉似乎是这条普遍规则的唯一例外。

s.en: Beggars almost sell themselves as human beings to arouse the pity of passers-by.
s.zh: 乞丐们几乎是在“出卖自己的人格”，以激起路人的同情心。

s.en: But real tramps are not beggars.
s.zh: 但是，真正的流浪者并不是乞丐。

s.en: They have nothing to sell and require nothing from others.
s.zh: 他们没有什么可以出售的，也不需要从别人那里得到任何东西。

s.en: In seeking independence, they do not sacrifice their human dignity.
s.zh: 在追求独立的过程中，他们并没有牺牲自己的人格尊严。

s.en: A tramp may ask you for money, but he will never ask you to feel sorry for him.
s.zh: 一个流浪汉可能会向你乞讨钱财，但他永远不会要求你同情他。

s.en: He has deliberately chosen to lead the life he leads and is fully aware of the consequences.
s.zh: 他自己是主动选择了这样的生活方式，并且完全清楚这样做会带来什么样的后果。

s.en: He may never be sure where the next meal is coming from,
s.zh: 他可能永远都无法确定下一顿饭从哪里来。

s.en: but he is free from the thousands of anxieties which afflict other people.
s.zh: 但他摆脱了那些困扰其他人的成千上万种焦虑情绪。

s.en: His few material possessions make it possible for him to move from place to place with ease.
s.zh: 他仅有的一些物质财富使他能够轻松地从一个地方搬到另一个地方。

s.en: By having to sleep in the open, he gets far closer to the world of nature than most of us ever do.
s.zh: 由于不得不在户外露宿，他比我们大多数人更接近大自然的世界。

s.en: He may hunt, beg, or steal occasionally to keep himself alive;
s.zh: 他可能会偶尔通过打猎、乞讨或偷窃来维持生计。

s.en: he may even, in times of real need, do a little work; but he will never sacrifice his freedom.
s.zh: 在真正需要的时候，他或许也会稍微工作一下；但他永远不会牺牲自己的自由。

s.en: We often speak of tramps with contempt and put them in the same class as beggars,
s.zh: 我们常常轻蔑地看待流浪者，把他们和乞丐归为同一类，

s.en: but how many of us can honestly say that we have not felt a little envious of their simple way of life and their freedom from care?
s.zh: 但又有多少人能坦诚地说，自己没有羡慕过他们简单的生活方式以及无忧无虑的生活状态呢？

q: What is the most important thing for a tramp?
对于一个流浪者来说，最重要的是什么？

s.en: Small boats loaded with wares sped to the great liner as she was entering the harbour.
s.zh: 当那艘大型客轮驶入港口时，载满货物的小船迅速朝它驶去。

s.en: Before she had anchored, the men from the boats had climbed on board
s.zh: 在它抛锚之前，小船上的人就已经爬上了大船。

s.en: and the decks were soon covered with colourful rugs from Persia,
s.zh: 很快，这些甲板上就铺上了来自波斯的彩色地毯。

s.en: silks from India, copper coffee pots, and beautiful handmade silverware.
s.zh: 来自印度的丝绸、铜制的咖啡壶，以及精美的手工银器。

s.en: It was difficult not to be tempted.
s.zh: 很难抗拒这种诱惑。

s.en: Many of the tourists on board had begun bargaining with the tradesmen,
s.zh: 船上的许多游客已经开始与商贩们讨价还价了。

s.en: but I decided not to buy anything until I had disembarked.
s.zh: 但我决定在离船之前不买任何东西。

s.en: I had no sooner got off the ship than I was assailed by a man who wanted to sell me a diamond ring.
s.zh: 我刚下船，就立刻被一个男人缠住了——他想要向我推销一枚钻石戒指。

s.en: I had no intention of buying one,
s.zh: 我本来就没有打算买一个的。

s.en: but I could not conceal the fact that I was impressed by the size of the diamonds.
s.zh: 但我无法隐瞒这样一个事实：这些钻石的尺寸确实让我印象深刻。

s.en: Some of them were as big as marbles.
s.zh: 其中一些钻石有弹珠那么大。

s.en: The man went to great lengths to prove that the diamonds were real.
s.zh: 这个人付出了巨大的努力来证明这些钻石是真品。

s.en: As we were walking past a shop, he held a diamond firmly against the window and made a deep impression in the glass.
s.zh: 当我们经过一家商店时，他用力将那颗钻石压在窗户上，从而在玻璃上留下了一个明显的印记。

s.en: It took me over half an hour to get rid of him.
s.zh: 我花了半个多小时才把他打发走。

s.en: The next man to approach me was selling expensive pens and watches.
s.zh: 下一个向我走来的人在推销昂贵的钢笔和手表。

s.en: I examined one of the pens closely. It certainly looked genuine.
s.zh: 我仔细检查了其中一支笔。它看起来确实是真的。

s.en: At the base of the gold cap, the words 'made in the U.S.A.' had been neatly inscribed.
s.zh: 在金笔帽的底部，刻着‘美国制造’的字样，非常工整。

s.en: The man said that the pen was worth ￡50, but as a special favour, he would let me have it for ￡30.
s.zh: 那个人说这支笔的价值是 50 英镑，但作为一项特别的优惠，他愿意以 30 英镑的价格把笔卖给我。

s.en: I shook my head and held up five fingers indicating that I was willing to pay ￡5.
s.zh: 我摇了摇头，然后竖起了五根手指，表示我愿意支付 5 英镑。

s.en: Gesticulating wildly, the man acted as if he found my offer outrageous,
s.zh: 那男人夸张地比划着，好像我的报价让他很生气，

s.en: but he eventually reduced the price to 10 pounds.
s.zh: 但他最终将价格降到了10英镑。

s.en: Shrugging my shoulders I began to walk away when,
s.zh: 我耸了耸肩，正准备走开时，

s.en: a moment later, he ran after me and thrust the pen into my hands.
s.zh: 片刻后，他追上来，把那支笔塞到了我的手里。

s.en: Though he kept throwing up his arms in despair, he readily accepted the ￡5 I gave him.
s.zh: 尽管他绝望地举起双臂，但还是爽快地收下了我给的5英镑。

s.en: I felt especially pleased with my wonderful bargain--until I got back to the ship.
s.zh: 我对这笔“超值”的交易感到非常满意——直到我回到船上。

s.en: No matter how hard I tried,
s.zh: 不管我怎么试，

s.en: it was impossible to fill this beautiful pen with ink and to this day it has never written a single word!
s.zh: 这枝漂亮的钢笔根本无法装上墨水；直到今天，它仍然一个字也没写过！

q: Why was even five pounds 'too dear' ?
为什么连五英镑都嫌贵呢？

s.en: Whether we find a joke funny or not largely depends on where we have been brought up.
s.zh: 我们是否觉得某个笑话好笑，很大程度上取决于我们的成长环境。

s.en: The sense of humour is mysteriously bound up with national characteristics.
s.zh: 幽默感似乎与一个国家的民族特性有着某种神秘的联系。

s.en: A Frenchman, for instance, might find it hard to laugh at a Russian joke.
s.zh: 例如，一个法国人可能很难被一个俄罗斯笑话逗笑。

s.en: In the same way, a Russian might fail to see anything amusing in a joke
s.zh: 同样地，一个俄罗斯人可能根本看不出某个笑话有什么好笑的地方。

s.en: which would make an Englishman laugh to tears.
s.zh: 而这个笑话却能让英国人笑出眼泪。

s.en: Most funny stories are based on comic situations.
s.zh: 大多数有趣的故事都是基于一些滑稽、搞笑的情境创作的。

s.en: In spite of national differences, certain funny situations have a universal appeal.
s.zh: 尽管存在文化差异，但某些有趣的情境却具有普遍的吸引力。

s.en: No matter where you live,
s.zh: 无论你住在哪里，

s.en: you would find it difficult not to laugh at, say, Charlie Chaplin's early films.
s.zh: 你很难不笑出来，比如说，看查理·卓别林的早期电影。

s.en: However, a new type of humour, which stems largely from the U.S., has recently come into fashion.
s.zh: 然而，最近一种新型的幽默风格开始流行起来，这种幽默主要源自美国。

s.en: It is called 'sick humour'. Comedians base their jokes on tragic situations like violent death or serious accidents.
s.zh: 这被称为“病态幽默”。喜剧演员的笑料往往基于一些悲剧性场景，比如暴力死亡或严重事故。

s.en: Many people find this sort of joke distasteful.
s.zh: 很多人觉得这种类型的笑话很令人反感。

s.en: The following example of 'sick humour' will enable you to judge for yourself.
s.zh: 以下这个“病态幽默”的例子，可以让你自己判断一下这种幽默风格到底如何。

s.en: A man who had broken his right leg was taken to hospital a few weeks before Christmas.
s.zh: 一名右腿骨折的男子在圣诞节前几周被送往医院。

s.en: From the moment he arrived there,
s.zh: 从他到达那里的那一刻起，

s.en: he kept on pestering his doctor to tell him when he would be able to go home.
s.zh: 他一直缠着医生，想知道自己什么时候可以回家。

s.en: He dreaded having to spend Christmas in hospital.
s.zh: 他非常害怕不得不在医院里度过圣诞节。

s.en: Though the doctor did his best, the patient's recovery was slow.
s.zh: 尽管医生尽了最大努力，患者的康复进程仍然很缓慢。

s.en: On Christmas day, the man still had his right leg in plaster.
s.zh: 在圣诞节那天，那个人的右腿仍然打着石膏。

s.en: He spent a miserable day in bed thinking of all the fun he was missing.
s.zh: 他在床上度过了痛苦的一天，一直在想着自己错过的所有乐趣。

s.en: The following day, however, the doctor consoled him by telling him
s.zh: 然而，第二天医生安慰他说：

s.en: that his chances of being able to leave hospital in time for New Year celebrations were good.
s.zh: 他按时出院、能够参加新年庆祝活动的几率很大。

s.en: The man took heart and sure enough, on New Year's Eve he was able to hobble along to a party.
s.zh: 那男人重新振作起来，果然在公历新年前夜，他还能一瘸一拐地赶到参加派对。

s.en: To compensate for his unpleasant experiences in hospital,
s.zh: 为了弥补他在医院里所经历的不愉快经历，

s.en: the man drank a little more than was good for him.
s.zh: 那个人喝得有点过量了。

s.en: In the process, he enjoyed himself thoroughly and kept telling everybody how much he hated hospitals.
s.zh: 在这个过程中，他玩得非常开心，还不停地告诉所有人他有多讨厌医院。

s.en: He was still mumbling something about hospitals at the end of the party when he slipped on a piece of ice and broke his left leg.
s.zh: 派对结束时，他还在嘟囔着关于医院的事情；突然，他踩到一块冰，摔倒了，导致左腿骨折。

q: What is the basis of 'sick' humour?
“病态”幽默（即那些令人不适、甚至反感的幽默）的依据是什么呢？

s.en: For years, villagers believed that Endley farm was haunted.
s.zh: 多年来，村民们一直相信恩德利农场有鬼魂出没。

s.en: The farm was owned by two brothers, Joe and Bob Cox.
s.zh: 这个农场归两兄弟乔·考克斯和鲍勃·考克斯所有。

s.en: They employed a few farmhands, but no one was willing to work there long.
s.zh: 他们雇了一些农场工人，但没有人愿意在那里长期工作。

s.en: Every time a worker gave up his job, he told the same story.
s.zh: 每次有工人辞职时，他都会讲述同一个故事。

s.en: Farm labourers said that they always woke up to find that work had been done overnight.
s.zh: 农场工人们说，他们早上醒来时总会发现，头天晚上的活儿都干完了。

s.en: Hay had been cut and cowsheds had been cleaned.
s.zh: 干草已经被割下，牛棚也已经被清理干净了。

s.en: A farm worker, who stayed up all night, claimed to have seen a figure cutting corn in the moonlight.
s.zh: 一位熬夜的农场工人声称，他曾在月光下看见一个人影在收割庄稼。

s.en: In time, it became an accepted fact that the Cox brothers employed a conscientious ghost that did most of their work for them.
s.zh: 久而久之，大家就都相信考克斯兄弟雇了个勤快的鬼，帮他们干了大部分的活儿。

s.en: No one suspected that there might be someone else on the farm who had never been seen.
s.zh: 谁也没想到农场里还藏着个谁也没见过的人。

s.en: This was indeed the case.
s.zh: 事实确实如此。

s.en: A short time ago, villagers were astonished to learn that the ghost of Endley had died.
s.zh: 不久前，村民们听说恩德利的鬼魂死了，都大吃一惊。

s.en: Everyone went to the funeral, for the 'ghost' was none other than Eric Cox,
s.zh: 大家都参加了葬礼，因为那个“鬼魂”其实就是埃里克·考克斯。

s.en: a third brother who was supposed to have died as a young man.
s.zh: 他是兄弟三人中的另一位，人们原以为他年轻时就死了。

s.en: After the funeral, Joe and Bob revealed a secret which they had kept for over fifty years.
s.zh: 葬礼结束后，乔和鲍勃透露了一个他们保守了五十多年的秘密。

s.en: Eric had been the eldest son of the family, very much older than his two brothers.
s.zh: 埃里克是家中的老大，比两个弟弟年长很多。

s.en: He had been obliged to join the army during the Second World War.
s.zh: 在第二次世界大战期间，他被迫加入了军队。

s.en: As he hated army life, he decided to desert his regiment.
s.zh: 因为他特别讨厌军队生活，就决定当逃兵。

s.en: When he learnt that he would be sent abroad,
s.zh: 当他得知自己将被派往国外时，

s.en: he returned to the farm and his father hid him until the end of the war.
s.zh: 他回到了农场，他的父亲把他藏了起来，直到战争结束。

s.en: Fearing the authorities, Eric remained in hiding after the war as well.
s.zh: 因为怕被政府发现，埃里克战后也一直躲着。

s.en: His father told everybody that Eric had been killed in action.
s.zh: 他的父亲告诉所有人，埃里克在战斗中牺牲了。

s.en: The only other people who knew the secret were Joe and Bob.
s.zh: 除了乔和鲍勃，再没有别人知道这个秘密了。

s.en: They did not even tell their wives.
s.zh: 他们甚至都没有告诉自己的妻子。

s.en: When their father died they thought it their duty to keep Eric in hiding.
s.zh: 父亲去世后，他们觉得继续把埃里克藏起来是自己的责任。

s.en: All these years, Eric had lived as a recluse.
s.zh: 这些年来，埃里克一直过着隐居的生活。

s.en: He used to sleep during the day and work at night,
s.zh: 他过去常常在白天睡觉，晚上工作。

s.en: quite unaware of the fact that he had become the ghost of Endley.
s.zh: 他压根儿不知道自己已经成了恩德利的鬼。

s.en: When he died, however, his brothers found it impossible to keep the secret any longer.
s.zh: 然而，当他去世后，他的兄弟们发现再也无法保守这个秘密了。

q: Why did the two brothers keep the secret?
为什么这两兄弟要保守这个秘密呢？

s.en: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.
s.zh: 真正的怪人从来都不会刻意去吸引别人的注意。

s.en: They disregard social conventions without being conscious that they are doing anything extraordinary.
s.zh: 他们无视社会习俗，却完全没有意识到自己的行为有什么特别之处。

s.en: This invariably wins them the love and respect of others, for they add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
s.zh: 这无疑为他们赢得了他人的喜爱与尊重，因为他们为平淡的日常生活增添了色彩。

s.en: Up to the time of his death, Richard Colson was one of the most notable figures in our town.
s.zh: 直到去世，理查德·科尔森一直是我们镇上最杰出的人物之一。

s.en: He was a shrewd and wealthy businessman,
s.zh: 他是一位精明且富有的商人。

s.en: but most people in the town hardly knew anything about this side of his life.
s.zh: 但镇上的大多数人对他这一面的生活几乎一无所知。

s.en: He was known to us all as Dickie and his eccentricity had become legendary long before he died.
s.zh: 我们都叫他迪基，他的古怪行为早在他去世前就已成了传奇。

s.en: Dickie disliked snobs intensely.
s.zh: 迪基极其讨厌势利小人。

s.en: Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
s.zh: 尽管他拥有一辆豪车，但他几乎从不使用它，总是更喜欢步行出行。

s.en: Even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.
s.zh: 即使下着大雨，他也拒绝打伞。

s.en: One day, he walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
s.zh: 一天，他在一场倾盆大雨中淋得湿透后，走进了一家高档商店。

s.en: He wanted to buy a ￡300 watch for his wife,
s.zh: 他想给妻子买一块价值300英镑的手表。

s.en: but he was in such a bedraggled condition that an assistant refused to serve him.
s.zh: 但他当时的样子实在太狼狈了，以至于店员拒绝为他服务。

s.en: Dickie left the shop without a word and returned carrying a large cloth bag.
s.zh: 迪基一言不发地离开了商店，然后回来时手里拿着一个大布袋。

s.en: As it was extremely heavy, he dumped it on the counter.
s.zh: 由于它非常重，他就把它扔在了柜台上。

s.en: The assistant asked him to leave, but Dickie paid no attention to him and requested to see the manager.
s.zh: 助理让他离开，但迪基根本没理会，反而要求见经理。

s.en: Recognizing who the customer was,
s.zh: 认出了这位顾客是谁，

s.en: the manager was most apologetic and reprimanded the assistant severely.
s.zh: 经理非常抱歉，并严厉地训斥了那位助理。

s.en: When Dickie was given the watch, he presented the assistant with the cloth bag.
s.zh: 当迪基收到那块手表时，他把那个布袋送给了助手。

s.en: It contained ￡300 in pennies.
s.zh: 里面装着300英镑的便士。

s.en: He insisted on the assistant's counting the money before he left--30,000 pennies in all!
s.zh: 他坚持要求店员当面把钱点清——总共三万枚便士！

s.en: On another occasion, he invited a number of important critics to see his private collection of modern paintings.
s.zh: 还有一次，他邀请了许多知名评论家来参观他的私人现代绘画收藏。

s.en: This exhibition received a great deal of attention in the press,
s.zh: 这个展览在媒体上受到了极大的关注。

s.en: for though the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists,
s.zh: 因为尽管这些画被认为是著名艺术家的作品，

s.en: they had in fact been painted by Dickie.
s.zh: 实际上，这些画都是迪基画的。

s.en: It took him four years to stage this elaborate joke simply to prove that critics do not always know what they are talking about.
s.zh: 他花了四年时间精心策划这个恶作剧，只是为了证明评论家们并非总是言之有物。

q: Why did the shop assistant refuse to serve Dickie?
为什么店员拒绝为迪基提供服务呢？

s.en: The salvage operation had been a complete failure.
s.zh: 这次打捞作业彻底失败了。

s.en: The small ship, Elkor, which had been searching the Barents Sea for weeks, was on its way home.
s.zh: 那艘名为“Elkor”的小船已经在巴伦支海搜寻了数周，现在正返回家中。

s.en: A radio message from the mainland had been received by the ship's captain instructing him to give up the search.
s.zh: 船长接收到了一则来自大陆的无线电消息，命令他停止搜索。

s.en: The captain knew that another attempt would be made later,
s.zh: 船长知道，稍后还会有人再次尝试。

s.en: for the sunken ship he was trying to find had been carrying a precious cargo of gold bullion.
s.zh: 因为他试图寻找的那艘沉船，当时正载着一批珍贵的黄金货物。

s.en: Despite the message, the captain of the Elkor decided to try once more.
s.zh: 尽管收到了那条消息，埃尔科号（Elkor）的船长还是决定再试一次。

s.en: The sea bed was scoured with powerful nets and there was tremendous excitement on board when a chest was raised from the bottom.
s.zh: 海床被强大的渔网彻底清理过；当一个箱子从海底被打捞上来时，船上的所有人都兴奋不已。

s.en: Though the crew were at first under the impression that the lost ship had been found,
s.zh: 虽然船员们最初以为那艘失踪的船只已经被找到了，

s.en: the contents of the chest proved them wrong.
s.zh: 箱子里的物品证明他们是错的。

s.en: What they had in fact found was a ship which had been sunk many years before.
s.zh: 他们实际上发现的是一艘多年前就已经沉没的船只。

s.en: The chest contained the personal belongings of a seaman, Alan Fielding.
s.zh: 这个箱子里装着水手艾伦·菲尔丁的个人物品。

s.en: There were books, clothing and photographs, together with letters which the seaman had once received from his wife.
s.zh: 里面有书籍、衣物、照片，还有那位水手从妻子那里收到的一些信件。

s.en: The captain of the Elkor ordered his men to salvage as much as possible from the wreck.
s.zh: 埃尔科号（Elkor）的船长命令他的船员们从残骸中尽可能多地抢救出有用的物品。

s.en: Nothing of value was found,
s.zh: 没有发现任何有价值的东西。

s.en: but the numerous items which were brought to the surface proved to be of great interest.
s.zh: 但是，那些被发掘出来的众多物品都引起了极大的兴趣。

s.en: From a heavy gun that was raised, the captain realized that the ship must have been a cruiser.
s.zh: 当那门大炮被抬起来时，船长意识到这艘船应该是一艘巡洋舰。

s.en: In another chest which contained the belongings of a ship's officer,
s.zh: 在另一个箱子里，装着一名船员的个人物品。

s.en: there was an unfinished letter which had been written on March 14th, 1943.
s.zh: 有一封未完成的信，写于1943年3月14日。

s.en: The captain learnt from the letter that the name of the lost ship was the Karen.
s.zh: 从这封信中，船长得知那艘失踪的船只的名字叫“Karen”。

s.en: The most valuable find of all was the ship's log book, parts of which it was still possible to read.
s.zh: 最珍贵的发现是那艘船的航海日志；其中的一部分内容仍然可以辨认出来。

s.en: From this the captain was able to piece together all the information that had come to light.
s.zh: 通过这些信息，船长得以拼凑出所有已经发现的情况。

s.en: The Karen had been sailing in a convoy to Russia when she was torpedoed by an enemy submarine.
s.zh: 那艘名为“Karen”的船当时正与一支船队一起前往俄罗斯，途中被敌方潜艇发射的鱼雷击中。

s.en: This was later confirmed by a naval official at the Ministry of Defence after the Elkor had returned home.
s.zh: 这一事件在“Elkor”号返回国内后，得到了国防部海军官员的证实。

s.en: All the items that were found were sent to the War Museum.
s.zh: 船上发现的所有物品都被送到了战争博物馆。

q: Did the crew of the Elkor find what they were looking for? Why?
埃尔科号（Elkor）的船员们找到他们想要的东西了吗？为什么？

s.en: We have all experienced days when everything goes wrong.
s.zh: 我们都经历过那些一切都出错的日子。

s.en: A day may begin well enough, but suddenly everything seems to get out of control.
