s.zh: 一天可能开始得很顺利，但突然间，一切似乎都失控了。

s.en: What invariably happens is that a great number of things choose to go wrong at precisely the same moment.
s.zh: 不可避免的是，许多事情会在同一时刻同时出错。

s.en: It is as if a single unimportant event set up a chain of reactions.
s.zh: 就好像某个看似微不足道的事件引发了一连串的连锁反应。

s.en: Let us suppose that you are preparing a meal and keeping an eye on the baby at the same time.
s.zh: 假设你一边准备饭菜，一边还要照看婴儿。

s.en: The telephone rings and this marks the prelude to an unforeseen series of catastrophes.
s.zh: 电话突然响了，而这成了随后一系列意外事件的导火线。

s.en: While you are on the phone, the baby pulls the tablecloth off the table,
s.zh: 你在打电话时，婴儿把桌布从桌子上扯了下来，

s.en: smashing half your best crockery and cutting himself in the process.
s.zh: 打碎了你一半最好的餐具，还把自己划伤了。

s.en: You hang up hurriedly and attend to baby, crockery, etc.
s.zh: 你匆忙挂断电话，忙着照顾婴儿、收拾餐具，

s.en: Meanwhile, the meal gets burnt.
s.zh: 与此同时，饭菜被烧焦了。

s.en: As if this were not enough to reduce you to tears, your husband arrives, unexpectedly bringing three guests to dinner.
s.zh: 仿佛这些还不够让你心烦意乱似的，你的丈夫突然回来了，还带着三位客人一起来吃晚饭。

s.en: Things can go wrong on a big scale as a number of people recently discovered in Parramatta, a suburb of Sydney.
s.zh: 最近，在悉尼的郊区帕拉马塔，许多人发现事情也可能在大范围内出错。

s.en: During the rush hour one evening two cars collided and both drivers began to argue.
s.zh: 一天晚上的高峰时段，两辆车发生了碰撞，两名司机随即开始争吵。

s.en: The woman immediately behind the two cars happened to be a learner.
s.zh: 就坐在那两辆车后面的那位女士，恰好是一名正在学习驾驶的新手。

s.en: She suddenly got into a panic and stopped her car.
s.zh: 她突然陷入了恐慌，立刻停下了车子。

s.en: This made the driver following her brake hard.
s.zh: 这导致跟在她后面的司机也紧急踩下了刹车。

s.en: His wife was sitting beside him holding a large cake.
s.zh: 他的妻子坐在他旁边，手里拿着一个大蛋糕。

s.en: As she was thrown forward,
s.zh: 当她被向前抛出时，

s.en: the cake went right through the windscreen and landed on the road.
s.zh: 蛋糕直接穿过了挡风玻璃，落在了路上。

s.en: Seeing a cake flying through the air,
s.zh: 看到一个蛋糕在空中飞过，

s.en: a lorry driver who was drawing up alongside the car, pulled up all of a sudden.
s.zh: 一名正在靠近那辆汽车的卡车司机突然停了下来。

s.en: The lorry was loaded with empty beer bottles and hundreds of them slid off the back of the vehicle and on to the road.
s.zh: 卡车上装满了空啤酒瓶，结果有数百个瓶子从卡车后部滑落到了路上。

s.en: This led to yet another angry argument. Meanwhile, the traffic piled up behind.
s.zh: 这又引发了一场激烈的争吵。与此同时，后面的交通也陷入了堵塞。

s.en: It took the police nearly an hour to get the traffic on the move again.
s.zh: 警察花了将近一个小时才让交通恢复正常。

s.en: In the meantime, the lorry driver had to sweep up hundreds of broken bottles.
s.zh: 在此期间，卡车司机不得不把那些破碎的瓶子全部清理干净。

s.en: Only two stray dogs benefited from all this confusion, for they greedily devoured what was left of the cake.
s.zh: 只有两只流浪狗从这场混乱中得到了好处——它们贪婪地吃掉了剩下的蛋糕。

s.en: It was just one of those days!
s.zh: 唉，真是诸事不顺的一天！

q: What incident began the series of traffic accidents?
是什么事件引发了这一连串的交通事故？

s.en: Antique shops exert a peculiar fascination on a great many people.
s.zh: 古董店对许多人来说具有独特的吸引力。

s.en: The more expensive kind of antique shop where rare objects are beautifully displayed in glass cases
s.zh: 那种高档古董店通常令人望而却步，里面的珍品

s.en: to keep them free from dust is usually a forbidding place.
s.zh: 被精美地陈列在玻璃展柜中，以免落上灰尘。

s.en: But no one has to muster up courage to enter a less pretentious antique shop.
s.zh: 不过，进入那些不那么讲究排场的古董店时，根本不需要鼓起什么勇气。

s.en: There is always hope that in its labyrinth of musty, dark, disordered rooms a real rarity will be found amongst the piles of assorted junk that litter the floors.
s.zh: 总有一种希望：在那充满霉味、黑暗且杂乱无章的房间里，人们或许能在散落在地板上的各种杂物堆中找到某件真正珍贵的东西。

s.en: No one discovers a rarity by chance.
s.zh: 没有人能偶然发现稀有物品。

s.en: A truly dedicated bargain hunter must have patience,
s.zh: 一个真正热衷于寻找便宜货的人，必须具备耐心。

s.en: and above all, the ability to recognize the worth of something when he sees it.
s.zh: 最重要的是，当他看到某样东西时，能够认识到它的价值。

s.en: To do this, he must be at least as knowledgeable as the dealer.
s.zh: 为了做到这一点，他至少必须具备与经销商同等的知识水平。

s.en: Like a scientist bent on making a discovery,
s.zh: 就像一位致力于有所发现的科学家一样，

s.en: he must cherish the hope that one day he will be amply rewarded.
s.zh: 他必须珍惜这个希望：总有一天，他会得到丰厚的回报。

s.en: My old friend, Frank Halliday, is just such a person.
s.zh: 我的老朋友弗兰克·霍利迪，就是这样的一个人。

s.en: He has often described to me how he picked up a masterpiece for a mere ￡50.
s.zh: 他经常跟我讲述自己是如何以仅仅 50 英镑的价格买到了一件杰作的。

s.en: One Saturday morning, Frank visited an antique shop in my neighbourhood.
s.zh: 一个星期六的早晨，弗兰克去了我家附近的一家古董店。

s.en: As he had never been there before, he found a great deal to interest him.
s.zh: 由于他以前从未去过那里，因此发现了许多令他感兴趣的东西。

s.en: The morning passed rapidly and Frank was about to leave when he noticed a large packing case lying on the floor.
s.zh: 早晨过得很快，弗兰克正准备离开时，他注意到地上放着一个大包裹箱。

s.en: The dealer told him that it had just come in, but that he could not be bothered to open it.
s.zh: 经销商告诉他，这个商品刚刚到货，但他懒得去打开它。

s.en: Frank begged him to do so and the dealer reluctantly prised it open.
s.zh: 弗兰克恳求他这么做，于是经销商不情愿地撬开了那个箱子。

s.en: The contents were disappointing.
s.zh: 里面的东西令人失望。

s.en: Apart from an interesting-looking carved dagger, the box was full of crockery, much of it broken.
s.zh: 除了那把外观精美的雕刻匕首外，盒子里还装满了陶器，其中大部分都已经破碎了。

s.en: Frank gently lifted the crockery out of the box and suddenly noticed a miniature painting at the bottom of the packing case.
s.zh: 弗兰克小心翼翼地将陶器从盒子里取出来，突然发现包装箱的底部有一幅微型画。

s.en: As its composition and line reminded him of an Italian painting he knew well, he decided to buy it.
s.zh: 由于这幅画的构图和线条让他联想到一幅他非常熟悉的意大利画作，他决定买下它。

s.en: Glancing at it briefly the dealer told him that it was worth ￡50.
s.zh: 经销商匆匆看了一眼后告诉他，这幅画的价值是50英镑。

s.en: Frank could hardly conceal his excitement, for he knew that he had made a real discovery.
s.zh: 弗兰克几乎无法掩饰自己的兴奋之情，因为他知道自己发现了一件真正的珍宝。

s.en: The tiny painting proved to be an unknown masterpiece by Correggio and was worth hundreds of thousands of pounds.
s.zh: 这幅小小的画作后来被证实是科雷乔（Correggio）的一幅不为人知的杰作，价值高达数十万英镑。

q: What was the 'happy discovery' ?
这个“令人高兴的发现”是什么呢？

s.en: The word justice is usually associated with courts of law.
s.zh: “正义”这个词通常与法庭联系在一起。

s.en: We might say that justice has been done when a man's innocence or guilt has been proved beyond doubt.
s.zh: 我们可以说，当一个人的清白或罪行被确凿无疑地证明时，正义就得到了伸张。

s.en: Justice is part of the complex machinery of the law.
s.zh: 正义是法律这一复杂体系的重要组成部分。

s.en: Those who seek it, undertake an arduous journey and can never be sure that they will find it.
s.zh: 那些追寻它的人，必须踏上一段艰辛的旅程；而且他们永远无法确定自己是否真的能够找到它。

s.en: Judges, however wise or eminent, are human and can make mistakes.
s.zh: 然而，无论法官多么明智或德高望重，他们终究也是人，因此也可能会犯错。

s.en: There are rare instances when justice almost ceases to be an abstract concept.
s.zh: 在极少数情况下，正义几乎不再是一个抽象的概念。

s.en: Reward or punishment are meted out quite independent of human interference.
s.zh: 奖惩的施行完全不受人为干预。

s.en: At such times, justice acts like a living force.
s.zh: 在这样的时刻，正义就像一股活生生的力量。

s.en: When we use a phrase like 'it serves him right',
s.zh: 当我们使用“这是他应得的”这样的表达时，

s.en: we are, in part, admitting that a certain set of circumstances has enabled justice to act of its own accord.
s.zh: 在某种程度上，我们承认：某些特定的情况让正义自行发挥了作用。

s.en: When a thief was caught on the premises of a large jewellery store one morning,
s.zh: 一天早晨，一个小偷在一家大型珠宝店的店内被抓获。

s.en: the shop assistants must have found it impossible to resist the temptation to say 'it serves him right'.
s.zh: 店员们肯定忍不住想说：“他活该。”

s.en: The shop was an old converted house with many large, disused fireplaces and tall, narrow chimneys.
s.zh: 这家商店是一栋经过改造的旧房子，里面有许多大型、已经废弃的壁炉，以及高而狭窄的烟囱。

s.en: Towards midday, a girl heard a muffled cry coming from behind one of the walls.
s.zh: 临近中午时分，一个女孩听到从某面墙后面传来的微弱哭声。

s.en: As the cry was repeated several times,
s.zh: 由于那呼喊声又传来了几次，

s.en: she ran to tell the manager who promptly rang up the fire brigade.
s.zh: 她跑去告诉了经理，经理立刻拨打了消防队的电话。

s.en: The cry had certainly come from one of the chimneys,
s.zh: 那声哭喊肯定是从其中一根烟囱里传出来的。

s.en: but as there were so many of them, the firemen could not be certain which one it was.
s.zh: 但由于烟囱太多，消防员们无法确定是哪一根。

s.en: They located the right chimney by tapping at the walls and listening for the man's cries.
s.zh: 他们通过敲击墙壁并聆听那个人的呼喊声，最终找到了正确的烟囱。

s.en: After chipping through a wall which was eighteen inches thick,
s.zh: 在凿穿了一面厚达十八英寸的墙壁后，

s.en: they found that a man had been trapped in the chimney.
s.zh: 他们发现有一名男子被困在了烟囱里。

s.en: As it was extremely narrow, the man was unable to move,
s.zh: 由于通道非常狭窄，那个人根本无法移动。

s.en: but the fire fighters were eventually able to free him by cutting a huge hole in the wall.
s.zh: 但是消防员最终通过在墙上切出一个大洞，成功将他救了出来。

s.en: The sorry-looking, blackened figure that emerged,
s.zh: 那个狼狈不堪、满身漆黑的身影一出现，

s.en: admitted at once that he had tried to break into the shop during the night but had got stuck in the chimney.
s.zh: 他立刻承认，自己确实在夜里试图闯入那家商店，但结果被困在了烟囱里。

s.en: He had been there for nearly ten hours.
s.zh: 他已经在那里待了将近十个小时了。

s.en: Justice had been done even before the man was handed over to the police.
s.zh: 正义已经得到了伸张，甚至在那个男人被交给警察之前就已经如此了。

q: The word 'justice' is given two different meanings in the text. What is the distinction between them?
在这段文字中，“justice”这个词被赋予了两种不同的含义。它们之间的区别是什么？

s.en: We are less credulous than we used to be.
s.zh: 我们不再像过去那样容易轻信他人或事物了。

s.en: In the nineteenth century, a novelist would bring his story to a conclusion
s.zh: 在十九世纪，小说家会通过一系列巧合来结束他的故事

s.en: by presenting his readers with a series of coincidences--most of them wildly improbable.
s.zh: ——其中大多数都极不可能发生。

s.en: Readers happily accepted the fact that an obscure maidservant was really the hero's mother.
s.zh: 读者们欣然接受了这样一个事实：那位默默无闻的女仆其实就是这位英雄的母亲。

s.en: A long-lost brother, who was presumed dead, was really alive all the time
s.zh: 一个被认定已经去世的“失散多年的兄弟”，其实一直都活着。

s.en: and wickedly plotting to bring about the hero's downfall. And so on.
s.zh: 并且一直在暗中策划要毁掉英雄，诸如此类。

s.en: Modern readers would find such naive solutions totally unacceptable.
s.zh: 现代读者会认为这种天真的解决方案完全不可接受。

s.en: Yet, in real life, circumstances do sometimes conspire to bring about coincidences which anyone but a nineteenth century novelist would find incredible.
s.zh: 然而，在现实生活中，情况确实有时会凑巧促成一些巧合，这些巧合除了十九世纪的小说家外，任何人都会觉得难以置信。

s.en: When I was a boy, my grandfather told me how a German taxi driver, Franz Bussman,
s.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我的祖父给我讲过一个德国出租车司机弗朗茨·布斯曼的故事。

s.en: found a brother who was thought to have been killed twenty years before.
s.zh: 找到了一个被认为在二十年前就已经去世的兄弟。

s.en: While on a walking tour with his wife, he stopped to talk to a workman.
s.zh: 在与妻子一起散步时，他停下来与一位工人交谈。

s.en: After they had gone on, Mrs. Bussman commented on the workman's close resemblance to her husband
s.zh: 在他们离开后，布斯曼夫人评论说那个工人和她丈夫长得非常像。

s.en: and even suggested that he might be his brother.
s.zh: 甚至暗示他可能是她丈夫的兄弟。

s.en: Franz poured scorn on the idea,
s.zh: 弗朗茨对这个想法嗤之以鼻。

s.en: pointing out that his brother had been killed in action during the war.
s.zh: 他指出他的兄弟在战争中阵亡了。

s.en: Though Mrs. Bussman was fully acquainted with this story,
s.zh: 尽管布斯曼夫人对这件事了如指掌，

s.en: she thought that there was a chance in a million that she might be right.
s.zh: 她认为自己有百万分之一的可能性是对的。

s.en: A few days later, she sent a boy to the workman to ask him if his name was Hans Bussman.
s.zh: 几天后，她派了一个男孩去问那个工人，他的名字是不是汉斯·布斯曼（Hans Bussman）。

s.en: Needless to say, the man's name was Hans Bussman and he really was Franz's long-lost brother.
s.zh: 不用说，这个男人的名字是汉斯·布斯曼，他确实是弗朗茨失散已久的兄弟。

s.en: When the brothers were reunited,
s.zh: 当兄弟俩重聚时，

s.en: Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
s.zh: 汉斯解释了自己是如何活下来的。

s.en: After having been wounded towards the end of the war,
s.zh: 在战争接近尾声时受伤之后，

s.en: he had been sent to hospital and was separated from his unit.
s.zh: 他被送到了医院，也因此与他的部队分开了。

s.en: The hospital had been bombed and Hans had made his way back into Western Germany on foot.
s.zh: 这家医院遭到了轰炸，汉斯只好徒步回到了西德。

s.en: Meanwhile, his unit was lost and all records of him had been destroyed.
s.zh: 与此同时，他的部队被打散了，关于他的所有记录也被毁掉了。

s.en: Hans returned to his family home, but the house had been bombed
s.zh: 汉斯回到了他的家庭住宅，但房子已经被炸毁了。

s.en: and no one in the neighbourhood knew what had become of the inhabitants.
s.zh: 而且邻居中没有人知道住户们后来怎么样了。

s.en: Assuming that his family had been killed during an air raid,
s.zh: 汉斯以为他的家人在一次空袭中丧生了，

s.en: Hans settled down in a village fifty miles away where he had remained ever since.
s.zh: 汉斯在五十英里外的一个村庄安顿了下来，从那以后他就一直住在那里。

q: What was the chance in a million?
那百万分之一的机会究竟是什么呢？

lessons.tz: 开往威斯特海温的快车

s.en: We have learnt to expect that trains will be punctual.
s.zh: 我们已经习惯了火车会准点到达这一情况。

s.en: After years of conditioning, most of us have developed an unshakable faith in railway timetables.
s.zh: 经过多年的习惯养成，我们大多数人都对铁路时刻表产生了坚定不移的信念。

s.en: Ships may be delayed by storms;
s.zh: 船只可能会因为风暴而延误。

s.en: flights may be cancelled because of bad weather; but trains must be on time.
s.zh: 航班可能会因为恶劣天气而被取消；但火车必须准时运行。

s.en: Only an exceptionally heavy snow fall might temporarily dislocate railway services.
s.zh: 只有当降雪量异常大时，铁路服务才可能暂时中断。

s.en: It is all too easy to blame the railway authorities when something does go wrong.
s.zh: 当出现问题时，人们很容易将责任归咎于铁路管理部门。

s.en: The truth is that when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs.
s.zh: 事实上，当错误发生时，这些错误更有可能是我们自己造成的，而不是他们的。

s.en: After consulting my railway timetable, I noted with satisfaction that there was an express train to Westhaven.
s.zh: 在查看了铁路时刻表后，我满意地发现有一趟直达韦斯特黑文的快车。

s.en: It went direct from my local station and the journey lasted a mere hour and seventeen minutes.
s.zh: 它直接从我所在的车站出发，全程仅需一小时十七分钟。

s.en: When I boarded the train, I could not help noticing that a great many local people got on as well.
s.zh: 当我登上火车时，我不禁注意到有很多当地人也都上了车。

s.en: At the time, this did not strike me as odd.
s.zh: 当时，我并没有觉得这有什么奇怪的。

s.en: I reflected that there must be a great many people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service.
s.zh: 我想，除了我之外，肯定还有很多人希望能够利用这项优质的服务。

s.en: Neither was I surprised when the train stopped at Widley, a tiny station a few miles along the line.
s.zh: 当火车在威德利（Widley）这个位于铁路线上几英里外的小车站停下来的时候，我也没有感到惊讶。

s.en: Even a mighty express train can be held up by signals.
s.zh: 即使是强大的特快列车也可能被信号灯拦停。

s.en: But when the train dawdled at station after station, I began to wonder.
s.zh: 但是当火车在一个又一个车站上缓慢停留、迟迟不前时，我开始感到疑惑了。

s.en: It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty.
s.zh: 我突然意识到，这趟特快列车并非以每小时90英里的速度飞驰，而是以每小时30英里的速度缓慢行驶。

s.en: One hour and seventeen minutes passed and we had not even covered half the distance.
s.zh: 一个小时十七分钟过去了，我们甚至还没有走完一半的路程。

s.en: I asked a passenger if this was the Westhaven Express, but he had not even heard of it.
s.zh: 我问了一位乘客这是否是“Westhaven Express”列车，但他甚至从未听说过这趟列车。

s.en: I determined to lodge a complaint as soon as we arrived.
s.zh: 我决定一到达就立即提出投诉。

s.en: Two hours later, I was talking angrily to the station master at Westhaven.
s.zh: 两小时后，我正在韦斯特黑文（Westhaven）愤怒地与车站站长交谈。

s.en: When he denied the train's existence, I borrowed his copy of the timetable.
s.zh: 当他否认火车的存在时，我就借用了他的时刻表。

s.en: There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white.
s.zh: 当我告诉他白纸黑字写着这趟列车时，我的声音带着一丝得意的语气。

s.en: Glancing at it briefly, he told me to look again.
s.zh: 他匆匆瞥了一眼后，让我再仔细看一遍。

s.en: A tiny asterisk conducted me to a footnote at the bottom of the page.
s.zh: 一个小小的星号指引我看到了页面底部的脚注。

s.en: It said: 'This service has been suspended.'
s.zh: 上面写着：‘此班次已暂停运营。’

q: What was the mistake the author made?
作者犯了什么错误？

s.en: Future historians will be in a unique position when they come to record the history of our own times.
s.zh: 未来的历史学家在记录我们这个时代的历史时，将会处于一个非常独特的地位。

s.en: They will hardly know which facts to select from the great mass of evidence that steadily accumulates.
s.zh: 他们几乎无法从不断积累的大量证据中判断出应该选择哪些事实。

s.en: What is more, they will not have to rely solely on the written word.
s.zh: 此外，他们将不必仅仅依赖书面文字。

s.en: Films, videos, CDs and CD-ROMs are just some of the bewildering amount of information they will have.
s.zh: 电影、视频、CD以及CD-ROM只是他们所拥有的海量信息中的一部分而已。

s.en: They will be able, as it were, to see and hear us in action.
s.zh: 他们将能够，可以说是，亲眼看到我们的活动，亲耳听到我们的声音。

s.en: But the historian attempting to reconstruct the distant past is always faced with a difficult task.
s.zh: 但是，试图重建遥远过去的历史学家总是面临着一项艰巨的任务。

s.en: He has to deduce what he can from the few scanty clues available.
s.zh: 他必须从现有的一些零星线索中尽可能地进行推断。

s.en: Even seemingly insignificant remains can shed interesting light on the history of early man.
s.zh: 即使是一些看似微不足道的遗物，也能为了解早期人类的历史提供有趣的线索。

s.en: Up to now, historians have assumed that calendars came into being with the advent of agriculture,
s.zh: 到目前为止，历史学家们一直认为日历的出现是与农业的诞生同时发生的。

s.en: for then man was faced with a real need to understand something about the seasons.
s.zh: 因为那时，人类确实迫切需要了解关于季节变化的规律。

s.en: Recent scientific evidence seems to indicate that this assumption is incorrect.
s.zh: 最近的科学证据似乎表明，这一假设是不正确的。

s.en: Historians have long been puzzled by dots, lines and symbols which have been engraved on walls, bones, and the ivory tusks of mammoths.
s.zh: 历史学家们长期以来一直对这些刻在墙壁上、骨头以及猛犸象象牙上的点、线条和符号感到困惑。

s.en: The nomads who made these markings lived by hunting and fishing during the last Ice Age which began about 35,000 B.C. and ended about 10,000 B.C.
s.zh: 制造这些标记的游牧民族在最后一次冰河时代（大约始于公元前35000年，结束于公元前10000年）以狩猎和捕鱼为生。

s.en: By correlating markings made in various parts of the world,
s.zh: 通过将世界各地留下的标记进行关联分析，

s.en: historians have been able to read this difficult code.
s.zh: 历史学家们已经成功解读了这段难以理解的代码。

s.en: They have found that it is connected with the passage of days and the phases of the moon.
s.zh: 他们发现这与日期的流逝和月亮的相位有关。

s.en: It is, in fact, a primitive type of calendar.
s.zh: 实际上，这是一种非常原始的日历形式。

s.en: It has long been known that the hunting scenes depicted on walls were not simply a form of artistic expression.
s.zh: 人们早就知道，墙上描绘的狩猎场景并非仅仅是一种艺术表达形式。

s.en: They had a definite meaning, for they were as near as early man could get to writing.
s.zh: 这些符号具有明确的含义，因为它们是早期人类所能达到的最接近文字的表达方式。

s.en: It is possible that there is a definite relation between these paintings and the markings that sometimes accompany them.
s.zh: 这些壁画与有时伴随出现的标记之间可能存在某种明确的联系。

s.en: It seems that man was making a real effort to understand the seasons 20,000 years earlier than has been supposed.
s.zh: 看来，早在人们原先认为的时间之前2万年，人类就已经在努力理解四季的变化规律了。

q: What is the importance of the dots, lines, and symbols engraved on stone, bones and ivory?
刻在石头、骨头和象牙上的点、线以及符号究竟有什么重要性呢？

s.en: The rough road across the plain soon became so bad that we tried to get Bruce to drive back to the village we had come from.
s.zh: 穿过平原的崎岖道路状况越来越糟糕，我们便决定让布鲁斯开车把我们送回我们出发的村庄。

s.en: Even though the road was littered with boulders and pitted with holes, Bruce was not in the least perturbed.
s.zh: 尽管路上布满了巨石，还有许多坑洞，布鲁斯却丝毫没有感到不安。

s.en: Glancing at his map, he informed us that the next village was a mere twenty miles away.
s.zh: 他看了一眼地图，然后告诉我们下一个村庄只有二十英里远。

s.en: It was not that Bruce always underestimated difficulties.
s.zh: 并不是说布鲁斯总是低估困难。

s.en: He simply had no sense of danger at all.
s.zh: 他完全没有任何危险意识。

s.en: No matter what the conditions were, he believed that a car should be driven as fast as it could possibly go.
s.zh: 无论条件如何，他都认为汽车应该能开多快就开多快。

s.en: As we bumped over the dusty track, we swerved to avoid large boulders.
s.zh: 我们在颠簸的土路上行驶时，不断转向以避开那些巨大的岩石。

s.en: The wheels scooped up stones which hammered ominously under the car.
s.zh: 车轮卷起了石子，这些石子在汽车下方发出令人不安的撞击声。

s.en: We felt sure that sooner or later a stone would rip a hole in our petrol tank or damage the engine.
s.zh: 我们确信，迟早会有石头划破我们的油箱，或者损坏发动机。

s.en: Because of this, we kept looking back, wondering if we were leaving a trail of oil and petrol behind us.
s.zh: 正因如此，我们不断回头查看，担心自己是否留下了一道油迹。

s.en: What a relief it was when the boulders suddenly disappeared,
s.zh: 当那些巨石突然消失的时候，真是让人松了一口气啊。

s.en: giving way to a stretch of plain where the only obstacles were clumps of bushes.
s.zh: 取而代之的是一片开阔的平原，唯一的障碍只是一些灌木丛。

s.en: But there was worse to come. Just ahead of us there was a huge fissure.
s.zh: 但更糟糕的事情还在后面。就在我们前方，有一条巨大的裂缝。

s.en: In response to renewed pleadings, Bruce stopped.
s.zh: 在我们再次恳求下，布鲁斯停了下来。

s.en: Though we all got out to examine the fissure, he remained in the car.
s.zh: 虽然我们都下车去查看那条裂缝，但他却留在了车里。

s.en: We informed him that the fissure extended for fifty yards and was two feet wide and four feet deep.
s.zh: 我们告诉他，那条裂缝长达五十码（约45.7米），宽度为两英尺（约0.6米），深度为四英尺（约1.2米）。

s.en: Even this had no effect.
s.zh: 即使这样，也没有任何效果。

s.en: Bruce went into a low gear and drove at a terrifying speed,
s.zh: 布鲁斯挂上低速挡，以惊人的速度向前冲去，

s.en: keeping the front wheels astride the crack as he followed its zigzag course.
s.zh: 他让前轮分别跨在裂缝两侧，沿着蜿蜒的路线前进。

s.en: Before we had time to worry about what might happen, we were back on the plain again.
s.zh: 我们还来不及担心会发生什么，就已经回到了平原上。

s.en: Bruce consulted the map once more and told us that the village was now only fifteen miles away.
s.zh: 布鲁斯再次查看了地图，然后告诉我们那个村庄现在距离我们只有十五英里了。

s.en: Our next obstacle was a shallow pool of water about half a mile across.
s.zh: 我们的下一个障碍是一个大约半英里宽的浅水池。

s.en: Bruce charged at it, but in the middle, the car came to a grinding halt.
s.zh: 布鲁斯驾车冲了过去，但车子在半路上突然停了下来。

s.en: A yellow light on the dashboard flashed angrily and Bruce cheerfully announced that there was no oil in the engine!
s.zh: 仪表盘上的黄灯愤怒地闪烁着，布鲁斯却高兴地宣布：发动机里没机油了！

q: What was the differnce between Bruce's behaviour and that of other people?
布鲁斯的行为与其他人的行为有什么不同？

s.en: It has never been explained why university students seem to enjoy practical jokes more than anyone else.
s.zh: 一直没有人解释为什么大学生似乎比任何人都更喜欢恶作剧。

s.en: Students specialize in a particular type of practical joke: the hoax.
s.zh: 学生们专精于一种特定类型的恶作剧——那就是“骗局”（即通过虚假信息或欺骗手段来制造混乱或误导他人）。

s.en: Inviting the fire brigade to put out a nonexistent fire is a crude form of deception which no self-respecting student would ever indulge in.
s.zh: 请消防队来扑灭不存在的火灾是一种低劣的骗术，任何有自尊的学生都不会染指。

s.en: Students often create amusing situations which are funny to everyone except the victims.
s.zh: 学生们经常制造一些有趣的、滑稽的情境，但这些情境只有受害者自己觉得不好笑，其他人反而都觉得很好笑。

s.en: When a student recently saw two workmen using a pneumatic drill outside his university,
s.zh: 最近，一名学生在自己的大学外面看到两名工人正在使用气动钻机。

s.en: he immediately telephoned the police and informed them that two students dressed up as workmen
s.zh: 他立即拨打了报警电话，并告诉警方有两名学生装扮成工人。

s.en: were tearing up the road with a pneumatic drill.
s.zh: 正用气动钻破坏路面。

s.en: As soon as he had hung up, he went over to the workmen and told them that if a policeman ordered them to go away,
s.zh: 他一挂断电话，就走到工人们跟前，告诉他们如果警察命令他们离开，

s.en: they were not to take him seriously.
s.zh: 他们不应该把他当回事。

s.en: He added that a student had dressed up as a policeman and was playing all sorts of silly jokes on people.
s.zh: 他还补充说，有个学生打扮成警察的样子，对周围的人开了各种滑稽的玩笑。

s.en: Both the police and the workmen were grateful to the student for this piece of advance information.
s.zh: 警察和工人们都很感谢这名学生提供的这个消息。

s.en: The student hid in an archway nearby where he could watch and hear everything that went on.
s.zh: 那个学生躲在附近的一个拱门里，从那里他可以观察到发生的一切，也能听到所有的声音。

s.en: Sure enough, a policeman arrived on the scene and politely asked the workmen to go away.
s.zh: 果然，一名警察来到了现场，并礼貌地要求工人们离开。

s.en: When he received a very rude reply from one of the workmen, he threatened to remove them by force.
s.zh: 当他收到其中一名工人的粗鲁回复时，他威胁说要强行将他们赶走。

s.en: The workmen told him to do as he pleased and the policeman telephoned for help.
s.zh: 工人们让他随意行事，而警察则拨打了求救电话。

s.en: Shortly afterwards, 4 more policemen arrived and remonstrated with the workmen.
s.zh: 不久，又有4名警察赶到，他们劝告工人们。

s.en: As the men refused to stop working, the police attempted to seize the pneumatic drill.
s.zh: 由于那些工人拒绝停止工作，警方试图没收那台气动钻机。

s.en: The workmen struggled fiercely and one of them lost his temper.
s.zh: 工人们激烈反抗，其中一人发火了。

s.en: He threatened to call the police.
s.zh: 他威胁说要报警。

s.en: At this, the police pointed out ironically that this would hardly be necessary as the men were already under arrest.
s.zh: 这时，警察讽刺地指出，这实在没必要，因为这些人已经被逮捕了。

s.en: Pretending to speak seriously, one of the workmen asked if he might make a telephone call before being taken to the station.
s.zh: 装出一副认真的样子，其中一名工人询问是否可以在被带到警察局之前打个电话。

s.en: Permission was granted and a policeman accompanied him to a pay phone.
s.zh: 获得了许可后，一名警察陪同他前往了一部公用电话。

s.en: Only when he saw that the man was actually telephoning the police did he realize that they had all been the victims of a hoax.
s.zh: 直到看到那个人真的在报警时，他才意识到他们所有人其实都成了一个骗局的受害者。

q: How did the policeman discover that the whole thing was a joke?
警察是怎么发现这一切其实只是个玩笑的呢？

s.en: The quiet life of the country has never appealed to me.
s.zh: 乡村的宁静生活从来都没有吸引过我。

s.en: City born and city bred,
s.zh: 我出生并成长在这座城市。

s.en: I have always regarded the country as something you look at through a train window, or something you occasionally visit during the weekend.
s.zh: 我一直认为乡村就像是通过火车窗户看到的风景，或者是一个偶尔在周末才会去参观的地方。

s.en: Most of my friends live in the city, yet they always go into raptures at the mere mention of the country.
s.zh: 我的大多数朋友都住在城市里，然而每当提到乡村时，他们总是表现出极大的热情和向往。

s.en: Though they extol the virtues of the peaceful life,
s.zh: 尽管他们推崇和平生活的种种美德，

s.en: only one of them has ever gone to live in the country and he was back in town within six months.
s.zh: 他们当中只有一个人真正搬去乡村居住，不过他在六个月后就回到了城里。

s.en: Even he still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.
s.zh: 即使他现在也仍然抱有一种错觉，认为乡村生活比城市生活优越。

s.en: He is forever talking about the friendly people, the clean atmosphere, the closeness to nature and the gentle pace of living.
s.zh: 他总是谈论那里友好的人民、清新的空气、与自然的亲密关系，以及悠闲的生活节奏。

s.en: Nothing can be compared, he maintains, with the first cockcrow, the twittering of birds at dawn,
s.zh: 他坚持认为：没有任何东西能够与清晨的第一声鸡鸣、以及鸟儿啁啾的声音相媲美。

s.en: the sight of the rising sun glinting on the trees and pastures.
s.zh: 朝阳的光芒在树木和牧场上闪烁的景象。

s.en: This idyllic pastoral scene is only part of the picture.
s.zh: 这幅田园诗般的景象只不过是整个画面的一部分罢了。

s.en: My friend fails to mention the long and friendless winter evenings in front of the TV--virtually the only form of entertainment.
s.zh: 我的朋友没有提到那些漫长而孤独的冬夜：那些夜晚，他们只能坐在电视机前，电视几乎是他们唯一的娱乐来源。

s.en: He says nothing about the poor selection of goods in the shops,
s.zh: 他对商店里商品种类少的问题只字未提。

s.en: or about those unfortunate people who have to travel from the country to the city every day to get to work.
s.zh: 或者，那些不幸的人——他们每天不得不从乡下赶到城市去上班。

s.en: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day for the dubious privilege of living in the country is beyond me.
s.zh: 我实在无法理解：为什么人们愿意每天忍受长达四小时的通勤时间，只为了获得住在乡下的那种可疑的特权。

s.en: They could be saved so much misery and expense if they chose to live in the city where they rightly belong.
s.zh: 如果他们选择回到自己真正应该居住的城市，就能避免那么多痛苦和开支了。

s.en: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best that life can offer.
s.zh: 如果你能够舍弃乡村生活中那些宁静、惬意的乐趣，你会发现城市能够为你提供生活中最美好的东西。

s.en: You never have to travel miles to see your friends.
s.zh: 你再也不需要长途跋涉去见你的朋友了。

s.en: They invariably live nearby and are always available for an informal chat or an evening's entertainment.
s.zh: 他们总是住在附近，随时可以陪你闲聊或一起享受晚上的娱乐时光。

s.en: Some of my acquaintances in the country come up to town once or twice a year to visit the theatre as a special treat.
s.zh: 我在乡下的一些熟人每年会来城里一两次，专门为了看戏剧而享受这份特别的乐趣。

s.en: For them this is a major operation which involves considerable planning.
s.zh: 对他们来说，这是一项规模较大的行动，需要周密的规划。

s.en: As the play draws to its close, they wonder whether they will ever catch that last train home.
s.zh: 随着戏剧接近尾声，他们开始怀疑自己是否还能赶上回家的最后一班火车。

s.en: The city dweller never experiences anxieties of this sort.
s.zh: 城市居民从来不会经历这种焦虑。

s.en: The latest exhibitions, films, or plays are only a short bus ride away.
s.zh: 最新的展览、电影或戏剧演出，都只需乘坐公交车很短的距离就能到达。

s.en: Shopping, too, is always a pleasure.
s.zh: 购物也总是一种令人愉悦的体验。

s.en: There is so much variety that you never have to make do with second best.
s.zh: 选择如此丰富多样，以至于你永远不必将就于次优的选择。

s.en: Country people run wild when they go shopping in the city and stagger home loaded with as many of the exotic items as they can carry.
s.zh: 乡下人一到城里购物，就会变得兴奋不已，他们会尽可能多地购买各种新奇的物品，然后摇摇晃晃地带着这些东西回家。

s.en: Nor is the city without its moments of beauty.
s.zh: 这座城市也有它美丽的时刻。

s.en: There is something comforting about the warm glow shed by advertisements on cold wet winter nights.
s.zh: 在寒冷潮湿的冬夜里，广告散发出的温暖光芒总有一种令人感到舒适的感觉。

s.en: Few things could be more impressive than the peace that descends on deserted city streets at weekends
s.zh: 没有什么比周末时那些空旷的城市街道上降临的宁静更令人印象深刻的了。

s.en: when the thousands that travel to work every day are tucked away in their homes in the country.
s.zh: 当每天成千上万通勤的人都安顿在乡下的家里时。

s.en: It has always been a mystery to me why city dwellers, who appreciate all these things,
s.zh: 我一直很困惑：为什么城市居民——他们明明很享受这些便利和美好的事物——却固执地假装自己更喜欢住在乡下。

s.en: obstinately pretend that they would prefer to live in the country.

q: What particular anxiety spoils the country dweller's visit to the theatre?
乡下人去剧院时，哪种担忧会破坏他们的兴致？

s.en: Cave exploration, or pot-holing, as it has come to be known, is a relatively new sport.
s.zh: 洞穴探险，也就是现在人们常说的“pot-holing”，其实是一项相对较新的运动。

s.en: Perhaps it is the desire for solitude or the chance of making an unexpected discovery that lures people down to the depths of the earth.
s.zh: 也许，正是对孤独的渴望，或是希望做出意外发现的心情，驱使人们前往地球的深处。

s.en: It is impossible to give a satisfactory explanation for a pot-holer's motives.
s.zh: 对于洞穴探险者的动机，根本不可能给出一个令人满意的解释。

s.en: For him, caves have the same peculiar fascination which high mountains have for the climber.
s.zh: 对他来说，洞穴具有与高山对登山者同样的独特吸引力。

s.en: They arouse instincts which can only be dimly understood.
s.zh: 它们唤醒了一些我们只能勉强理解的本能。

s.en: Exploring really deep caves is not a task for the Sunday afternoon rambler.
s.zh: 探索那些极其深邃的洞穴，绝不是适合在周日午后闲逛时去完成的任务。

s.en: Such undertakings require the precise planning and foresight of military operations.
s.zh: 这样的行动需要军事行动般的精确计划和远见。

s.en: It can take as long as eight days to rig up rope ladders and to establish supply bases before a descent can be made into a very deep cave.
s.zh: 在进入一个非常深的洞穴之前，搭建绳梯并建立补给基地可能需要长达八天的时间。

s.en: Precautions of this sort are necessary, for it is impossible to foretell the exact nature of the difficulties which will confront the pot-holer.
s.zh: 采取这样的预防措施是必要的，因为我们无法预知洞穴探险者将会遇到的具体困难。

s.en: The deepest known cave in the world is the Gouffre Berger near Grenoble.
s.zh: 世界上已知最深的洞穴是位于格勒诺布尔附近的贝尔热洞穴（Gouffre Berger）。

s.en: It extends to a depth of 3,723 feet.
s.zh: 它的深度达到了3,723英尺。

s.en: This immense chasm has been formed by an underground stream which has tunnelled a course through a flaw in the rocks.
s.zh: 这个巨大的峡谷是由一条地下溪流形成的；这条溪流在岩石的裂缝中穿行，逐渐侵蚀出了这条通道。

s.en: The entrance to the cave is on a plateau in the Dauphine Alps.
s.zh: 洞穴的入口位于多菲内阿尔卑斯山脉的一个高原上。

s.en: As it is only six feet across, it is barely noticeable.
s.zh: 由于它的宽度只有六英尺，几乎看不出来它的存在。

s.en: The cave might never have been discovered had not the entrance been spotted by the distinguished French pot-holer, Berger.
s.zh: 如果那个洞穴的入口没有被那位著名的法国洞穴探险家伯杰发现的话，它可能永远都不会被人发现。

s.en: Since its discovery, it has become a sort of pot-holers' Everest.
s.zh: 自从它被发现以来，它就成了洞穴探险者的'珠穆朗玛峰'。

s.en: Though a number of descents have been made, much of it still remains to be explored.
s.zh: 尽管已经有人多次尝试探索那里，但仍有很大一部分区域尚未被人类发现或探索。

s.en: A team of pot-holers recently went down the Gouffre Berger.
s.zh: 最近，一支由洞穴探险者组成的团队进入了贝尔热洞（Gouffre Berger）。

s.en: After entering the narrow gap on the plateau,
s.zh: 在进入高原上的那个狭窄缝隙之后，

s.en: they climbed down the steep sides of the cave until they came to a narrow corridor.
s.zh: 他们沿着洞穴陡峭的侧壁向下爬行，直到来到一条狭窄的通道前。

s.en: They had to edge their way along this,
s.zh: 他们不得不沿着这条路小心翼翼地前行。

s.en: sometimes wading across shallow streams, or swimming across deep pools.
s.zh: 有时候需要涉水穿过浅流；有时候则需要游过深水区。

s.en: Suddenly they came to a waterfall which dropped into an underground lake at the bottom of the cave.
s.zh: 突然，他们来到了一处瀑布前；那瀑布的水流直接注入了洞穴底部的一个地下湖泊中。

s.en: They plunged into the lake, and after loading their gear on an inflatable rubber dinghy, let the current carry them to the other side.
s.zh: 他们跳进了湖里，然后将装备装上了一个充气橡胶小艇，让水流将他们带到对岸。

s.en: To protect themselves from the icy water, they had to wear special rubber suits.
s.zh: 为了防止被冰冷的水冻伤，他们不得不穿上特制的橡胶防护服。

s.en: At the far end of the lake, they came to huge piles of rubble which had been washed up by the water.
s.zh: 在湖的尽头，他们看到了一堆堆巨大的碎石，这些碎石是被水冲上岸来的。

s.en: In this part of the cave, they could hear an insistent booming sound
s.zh: 在这个洞穴的区域内，他们能听到一种持续不断的、低沉的轰鸣声。

s.en: which they found was caused by a small waterspout shooting down into a pool from the roof of the cave.
s.zh: 他们发现，这种现象是由于一个小型水柱从洞穴的顶部冲下来，落入了一个水池中而引起的。

s.en: Squeezing through a cleft in the rocks, the pot-holers arrived at an enormous cavern, the size of a huge concert hall.
s.zh: 穿过岩石间的裂缝，那些洞穴探险者终于来到了一处巨大的洞穴——其规模相当于一座大型音乐厅。

s.en: After switching on powerful arc lights,
s.zh: 在打开强力的弧光灯之后，

s.en: they saw great stalagmites--some of them over forty feet high--rising up like tree-trunks to meet the stalactites suspended from the roof.
s.zh: 他们看到了那些巨大的石笋——其中一些高达四十多英尺——这些石笋像树干一样矗立着，与从屋顶悬挂下来的钟乳石相接。

s.en: Round about, piles of limestone glistened in all the colours of the rainbow.
s.zh: 周围，成堆的石灰岩闪烁着彩虹般的各种色彩。

s.en: In the eerie silence of the cavern, the only sound that could be heard was made by water which dripped continuously from the high dome above them.
s.zh: 在洞穴那令人毛骨悚然的寂静中，唯一能听到的声音，就是从他们头顶的高耸穹顶上不断滴落的水声。

q: With what does the writer compare the Gouffre Berger?
作者将“贝杰尔洞穴”（Gouffre Berger）比作什么？

s.en: Insurance companies are normally willing to insure anything.
s.zh: 保险公司通常愿意为任何物品提供保险服务。

s.en: Insuring public or private property is a standard practice in most countries in the world.
s.zh: 在世界上大多数国家，为公共或私人财产投保都是常规做法。

s.en: If, however, you were holding an open air garden party or a fete it would be equally possible to insure yourself in the event of bad weather.
s.zh: 不过，如果你在户外举办花园派对或游园会，也可以为可能发生的恶劣天气情况购买保险。

s.en: Needless to say, the bigger the risk an insurance company takes, the higher the premium you will have to pay.
s.zh: 不用说，保险公司承担的风险越大，你需要支付的保费也就越高。

s.en: It is not uncommon to hear that a shipping company has made a claim for the cost of salvaging a sunken ship.
s.zh: 航运公司要求赔偿打捞沉船的费用，这样的事并不罕见。

s.en: But the claim made by a local authority to recover the cost of salvaging a sunken pie dish must surely be unique.
s.zh: 但是，一个地方政府为打捞一个沉没的派盘而提出的索赔，肯定是非常独特的。

s.en: Admittedly it was an unusual pie dish, for it was eighteen feet long and six feet wide.
s.zh: 这个派盘确实很不寻常——它的长度为18英尺，宽度为6英尺。

s.en: It had been purchased by a local authority so that an enormous pie could be baked for an annual fair.
s.zh: 它是被当地政府购买的，用于为年度集市制作一个巨大的派。

s.en: The pie committee decided that the best way to transport the dish would be by canal so they insured it for the trip.
s.zh: 派委员会认为，通过运河运输是运送派盘的最佳方式，因此他们为这次行程购买了保险。

s.en: Shortly after it was launched, the pie committee went to a local inn to celebrate.
s.zh: 派盘下水后不久，派委员会成员们便前往一家当地酒馆庆祝。

s.en: At the same time, a number of teenagers climbed on to the dish and held a little party of their own.
s.zh: 与此同时，一些青少年爬上了那个盘子，并在那里举办了一场属于自己的小型聚会。

s.en: Dancing proved to be more than the dish could bear,
s.zh: 跳舞的震动超出了派盘所能承受的范围，

s.en: for during the party it capsized and sank in seven feet of water.
s.zh: 因为在派对期间，派盘翻了，沉入了七英尺深的水中。

s.en: The pie committee telephoned a local garage owner who arrived in a recovery truck to salvage the pie dish.
s.zh: 派委员会给当地一家修车厂老板打了电话，他开着一辆救援卡车前来打捞派盘。

s.en: Shivering in their wet clothes, the teenagers looked on while three men dived repeatedly into the water to locate the dish.
s.zh: 那些青少年穿着湿衣服瑟瑟发抖地看着，三个男人一次又一次地潜入水中寻找派盘。

s.en: They had little difficulty in finding it, but hauling it out of the water proved to be a serious problem.
s.zh: 他们找到它并不费什么劲，但将其从水中拖出来却成了一个严重的问题。

s.en: The sides of the dish were so smooth that it was almost impossible to attach hawsers and chains to the rim without damaging it.
s.zh: 这个盘子的边缘非常光滑，几乎不可能在不损坏它的情况下将缆绳或链条固定在盘子的边缘上。

s.en: Eventually chains were fixed to one end of the dish and a powerful winch was put into operation.
s.zh: 最终，那些链条被固定在盘子的一端；随后，一台强大的绞车也被启动了起来。

s.en: The dish rose to the surface and was gently drawn towards the canal bank.
s.zh: 派盘浮到水面，被缓缓地拉向运河岸边。

s.en: For one agonizing moment, the dish was perched precariously on the bank of the canal,
s.zh: 在令人揪心的一瞬间，派盘摇摇晃晃地停在运河岸边，

s.en: but it suddenly overbalanced and slid back into the water.
s.zh: 但它突然失去了平衡，又滑回了水中。

s.en: The men were now obliged to try once more.
s.zh: 这些人现在不得不再次尝试。

s.en: This time they fixed heavy metal clamps to both sides of the dish so that they could fasten the chains.
s.zh: 这次，他们在盘子的两侧安装了沉重的金属夹具，以便固定链条。

s.en: The dish now had to be lifted vertically because one edge was resting against the side of the canal.
s.zh: 由于盘子的一边紧贴着运河的侧壁，因此必须将其垂直抬起。

s.en: The winch was again put into operation and one of the men started up the truck.
s.zh: 绞车再次被启动，其中一名男子启动了卡车。

s.en: Several minutes later, the dish was successfully hauled above the surface of the water.
s.zh: 几分钟后，盘子终于被成功吊到了水面上方。

s.en: Water streamed in torrents over its sides with such force that it set up a huge wave in the canal.
s.zh: 水从派盘边缘倾泻而下，水流如此之猛，在运河里掀起了一阵巨浪。

s.en: There was a danger that the wave would rebound off the other side of the bank and send the dish plunging into the water again.
s.zh: 有危险的是，这股浪可能会从对岸反弹回来，把派盘重新冲回水里。

s.en: By working at tremendous speed, the men managed to get the dish on to dry land before the wave returned.
s.zh: 以极快的速度工作，这些人总算在浪头返回前把派盘弄上了岸。

q: Who owned the pie dish and why?
谁拥有那个派盘，为什么？

s.en: People travelling long distances frequently have to decide whether they would prefer to go by land, sea, or air.
s.zh: 长途旅行的人经常需要决定是选择陆路、海路还是航空方式来出行。

s.en: Hardly anyone can positively enjoy sitting in a train for more than a few hours.
s.zh: 几乎没有人能够真正享受在火车上坐上几个小时以上的时光。

s.en: Train compartments soon get cramped and stuffy.
s.zh: 火车车厢很快就会变得拥挤不堪、空气也不流通（即非常闷热）。

s.en: It is almost impossible to take your mind off the journey.
s.zh: 几乎不可能让你把注意力从这段旅程上移开。

s.en: Reading is only a partial solution, for the monotonous rhythm of the wheels clicking on the rails soon lulls you to sleep.
s.zh: 阅读只能提供部分缓解；车轮在铁轨上单调地咔嗒作响，这种声音很快就会让你入睡。

s.en: During the day, sleep comes in snatches.
s.zh: 白天里，睡眠总是断断续续的。

s.en: At night, when you really wish to go to sleep, you rarely manage to do so.
s.zh: 到了晚上，当你真的想入睡的时候，却往往难以入睡。

s.en: If you are lucky enough to get a sleeper,
s.zh: 如果你有幸买到一张卧铺票，

s.en: you spend half the night staring at the small blue light in the ceiling, or fumbling to find your ticket for inspection.
s.zh: 你会花上半个晚上盯着天花板上的小蓝灯，或者摸索着找票接受检查。

s.en: Inevitably you arrive at your destination almost exhausted.
s.zh: 最终，你几乎精疲力尽地到达了目的地。

s.en: Long car journeys are even less pleasant, for it is quite impossible even to read.
s.zh: 长途驾车旅行更加令人不适，因为在这种情况下甚至连看书都几乎不可能做到。

s.en: On motorways you can, at least, travel fairly safely at high speeds,
s.zh: 在高速公路上，至少你可以以较高的速度安全地行驶。

s.en: but more often than not, the greater part of the journey is spent on roads with few service stations and too much traffic.
s.zh: 但大多数情况下，旅途中的大部分时间都是在那些服务站稀少、交通拥堵严重的道路上度过的。

s.en: By comparison, ferry trips or cruises offer a great variety of civilized comforts.
s.zh: 相比之下，渡轮旅行或游轮旅行提供了多种舒适的设施和服务。

s.en: You can stretch your legs on the spacious decks, play games,
s.zh: 你可以在宽敞的甲板上伸展双腿、玩游戏，

s.en: meet interesting people and enjoy good food--always assuming, of course, that the sea is calm.
s.zh: 结识有趣的人，享受美味的美食——当然，这一切的前提都是海面必须风平浪静。

s.en: If it is not, and you are likely to get seasick, no form of transport could be worse.
s.zh: 如果海面不平静，而你又容易晕船，那就没有比这更糟糕的交通方式了。

s.en: Even if you travel in ideal weather, sea journeys take a long time.
s.zh: 即使你在理想的天气条件下旅行，海上航行仍然需要很长时间。

s.en: Relatively few people are prepared to sacrifice holiday time for the pleasure of travelling by sea.
s.zh: 只有少数人愿意牺牲假期时间，去享受海上旅行的乐趣。

s.en: Aeroplanes have the reputation of being dangerous and even hardened travellers are intimidated by them.
s.zh: 飞机一直被认为是一种危险的交通工具，就连那些经验丰富的旅客也会对它们感到恐惧。

s.en: They also have the disadvantage of being an expensive form of transport.
s.zh: 它们的另一个缺点是费用昂贵。

s.en: But nothing can match them for speed and comfort.
s.zh: 但是，在速度和舒适度方面，没有任何东西能比得上它们。

s.en: Travelling at a height of 30,000 feet, far above the clouds, and at over 500 miles an hour is an exhilarating experience.
s.zh: 在30,000英尺的高空飞行——远远高于云层之上——并以每小时超过500英里的速度前进，确实是一种令人兴奋的体验。

s.en: You do not have to devise ways of taking your mind off the journey, for an aeroplane gets you to your destination rapidly.
s.zh: 你不必费心去寻找方法来转移自己的注意力，因为飞机能迅速将你送到目的地。

s.en: For a few hours, you settle back in a deep armchair to enjoy the flight.
s.zh: 你可以安坐在宽大的扶手椅里，享受飞行的乐趣。

s.en: The real escapist can watch a film and sip champagne on some services.
s.zh: 在有些航班上，真正想放松的人可以看看电影，喝喝香槟。

s.en: But even when such refinements are not available, there is plenty to keep you occupied.
s.zh: 但即使没有这些精致的服务，也有足够多的事情让你打发时间。

s.en: An aeroplane offers you an unusual and breathtaking view of the world.
s.zh: 从飞机上，你可以看到一个独特而令人惊叹的世界景象。

s.en: You soar effortlessly over high mountains and deep valleys.
s.zh: 你轻松地翱翔在高山之上，穿过幽深的山谷。

s.en: You really see the shape of the land.
s.zh: 你真的能够清楚地看到这片土地的轮廓和地形特征。

s.en: If the landscape is hidden from view,
s.zh: 如果地面景色被云层遮挡，

s.en: you can enjoy the extraordinary sight of unbroken cloud plains that stretch out for miles before you, while the sun shines brilliantly in a clear sky.
s.zh: 你可以欣赏到那令人惊叹的景象：连绵不断的云层平铺在眼前，一望无际；而太阳则在清澈的天空下闪耀着耀眼的光芒。

s.en: The journey is so smooth that there is nothing to prevent you from reading or sleeping.
s.zh: 旅途非常平稳，没有任何因素会妨碍你阅读或睡觉。

s.en: However you decide to spend your time, one thing is certain: you will arrive at your destination fresh and uncrumpled.
s.zh: 无论你如何度过时光，有一点是确定的：到达目的地时，你会精神焕发，毫无倦意。

s.en: You will not have to spend the next few days recovering from a long and arduous journey.
s.zh: 你不必在接下来的几天里，为恢复长途跋涉造成的疲劳而休息。

q: Which type of transport does the writer prefer, do you think?
你认为作者更喜欢哪种交通工具呢？

s.en: In democratic countries any efforts to restrict the freedom of the press are rightly condemned.
s.zh: 在民主国家中，任何限制新闻自由的行为都应受到谴责。

s.en: However, this freedom can easily be abused.
s.zh: 然而，这种自由很容易被滥用。

s.en: Stories about people often attract far more public attention than political events.
s.zh: 关于普通人的故事往往比政治事件更能吸引公众的注意力。

s.en: Though we may enjoy reading about the lives of others,
s.zh: 虽然我们可能会喜欢阅读关于他人生活的故事，

s.en: it is extremely doubtful whether we would equally enjoy reading about ourselves.
s.zh: 我们是否也会同样喜欢阅读关于自己的内容，这一点实在非常值得怀疑。

s.en: Acting on the contention that facts are sacred,
s.zh: 基于“事实是神圣的”这一观点，

s.en: reporters can cause untold suffering to individuals by publishing details about their private lives.
s.zh: 记者通过公开个人的私生活细节，可能会给这些人带来难以估量的痛苦。

s.en: Newspapers exert such tremendous influence that they can not only bring about major changes to the lives of ordinary people but can even overthrow a government.
s.zh: 报纸的影响力极其巨大；它们不仅能够对普通人的生活产生重大影响，甚至有可能推翻一个政府。

s.en: The story of a poor family that acquired fame and fortune overnight, dramatically illustrates the power of the press.
s.zh: 这个关于一个贫困家庭如何一夜之间获得名望和财富的故事，生动地展示了媒体的影响力。

s.en: The family lived in Aberdeen, a small town of 23,000 inhabitants in South Dakota.
s.zh: 这家人住在阿伯丁（Aberdeen），一个位于南达科他州（South Dakota）的小镇上，该镇共有23,000名居民。

s.en: As the parents had five children, life was a perpetual struggle against poverty.
s.zh: 由于这对父母有五个孩子，他们的生活始终在与贫困作斗争。

s.en: They were expecting their sixth child and were faced with even more pressing economic problems.
s.zh: 他们即将迎来第六个孩子，同时也面临着更加紧迫的经济问题。

s.en: If they had only had one more child, the fact would have passed unnoticed.
s.zh: 如果他们这一次只生了一个孩子的话，这件事可能就会被忽视、无人注意了。

s.en: They would have continued to struggle against economic odds and would have lived in obscurity.
s.zh: 他们本会继续在艰难的经济环境中挣扎，过着默默无闻的生活。

s.en: But they suddenly became the parents of quintuplets, four girls and a boy, an event which radically changed their lives.
s.zh: 但他们突然成为了五胞胎的父母——四个女孩和一个男孩，这一事件彻底改变了他们的生活。

s.en: The day after the birth of the five children, an aeroplane arrived in Aberdeen bringing sixty reporters and photographers.
s.zh: 在五个孩子出生的第二天，一架飞机抵达阿伯丁，带来了六十名记者和摄影师。

s.en: The rise to fame was swift.
s.zh: 他们一举成名。

s.en: Television cameras and newspapers carried the news to everyone in the country.
s.zh: 电视摄像机与报纸将这一消息传遍了全国的每一个人。

s.en: Newspapers and magazines offered the family huge sums for the exclusive rights to publish stories and photographs.
s.zh: 报纸和杂志向这家人提供了巨额报酬，以获得独家报道这些事件和发布相关照片的权利。

s.en: Gifts poured in not only from unknown people,
s.zh: 礼物不仅来自陌生人，

s.en: but from baby food and soap manufacturers who wished to advertise their products.
s.zh: 也来自希望借此宣传产品的婴儿食品和肥皂制造商。

s.en: The old farmhouse the family lived in was to be replaced by a new $500,000 home.
s.zh: 他们曾经居住的旧农舍将被一座价值50万美元的新房子所取代。

s.en: Reporters kept pressing for interviews so lawyers had to be employed to act as spokesmen for the family at press conferences.
s.zh: 记者们不断要求采访，因此这家人不得不聘请律师在新闻发布会上担任发言人。

s.en: While the five babies were still quietly sleeping in oxygen tents in a hospital nursery,
s.zh: 当这五个婴儿还在医院婴儿房的氧气帐篷里安静地睡着时，

s.en: their parents were paying the price for fame.
s.zh: 他们的父母正在为他们的名气付出代价。

s.en: It would never again be possible for them to lead normal lives.
s.zh: 他们再也无法过上正常的生活了。

s.en: They had become the victims of commercialization, for their names had acquired a market value.
s.zh: 他们成为了商业化的受害者，因为他们的名字已经具有了市场价值。

s.en: Instead of being five new family members, these children had immediately become a commodity.
s.zh: 这些孩子没有成为家庭的新成员，反而立刻被当成了商品。

q: Does the writer think the parents were lucky or unlucky to gain prosperity in this way? Why?
作者认为，这些父母通过这种方式获得财富是幸运的，还是不幸的？为什么？

s.en: So great is our passion for doing things for ourselves,
s.zh: 我们对亲自动手做事的热情是如此之强烈，

s.en: that we are becoming increasingly less dependent on specialized labour.
s.zh: 以至于我们越来越不依赖专业劳动力了。

s.en: No one can plead ignorance of a subject any longer, for there are countless do-it-yourself publications.
s.zh: 如今，再没有人能够以“对某个主题一无所知”为借口了，因为市面上有数不胜数的 DIY（自己动手做）类出版物可供参考。

s.en: Armed with the right tools and materials, newlyweds gaily embark on the task of decorating their own homes.
s.zh: 配备了合适的工具和材料后，新婚夫妇便兴高采烈地开始装饰自己的家。

s.en: Men, particularly, spend hours of their leisure time installing their own fireplaces,
s.zh: 尤其是男性，他们会花费大量的闲暇时间来自己安装壁炉。

s.en: laying out their own gardens; building garages and making furniture.
s.zh: 他们自己规划花园的布局，建造车库，并制作家具。

s.en: Some really keen enthusiasts go so far as to build their own computers.
s.zh: 一些非常热衷的爱好者甚至会自己组装电脑。

s.en: Shops cater for the do-it-yourself craze not only by running special advisory services for novices,
s.zh: 商店不仅通过为新手提供专门的咨询服务，

s.en: but by offering consumers bits and pieces which they can assemble at home.
s.zh: 还通过向消费者提供各种可以自行组装的零件来迎合这股热潮。

s.en: Such things provide an excellent outlet for pent up creative energy, but unfortunately not all of us are born handymen.
s.zh: 这类活动为人们提供了释放内心创造力的绝佳途径，可惜并不是每个人天生就擅长动手做事。

s.en: Some wives tend to believe that their husbands are infinitely resourceful and can fix anything.
s.zh: 有些妻子总是认为自己的丈夫无所不能，什么问题都能解决。

s.en: Even men who can hardly drive a nail in straight are supposed to be born electricians, carpenters, plumbers and mechanics.
s.zh: 即使是那些连把钉子都钉不直的男人，也被认为天生就适合从事电工、木匠、水管工或机械师等工作。

s.en: When lights fuse, furniture gets rickety, pipes get clogged, or vacuum cleaners fail to operate,
s.zh: 当保险丝烧断、家具摇晃、管道堵塞或吸尘器失灵时，

s.en: some women assume that their husbands will somehow put things right.
s.zh: 有些女性认为，她们的丈夫会想办法把事情解决好。

s.en: The worst thing about the do-it-yourself game is that sometimes even men live under the delusion that they can do anything,
s.zh: 自己动手这事儿最糟糕的地方在于，有时候连男人自己都会误以为无所不能，

s.en: even when they have repeatedly been proved wrong.
s.zh: 即使他们的观点已经被多次证明是错误的，他们仍然坚持自己的立场。

s.en: It is a question of pride as much as anything else.
s.zh: 这主要是面子问题。

s.en: Last spring my wife suggested that I call in a man to look at our lawn mower.
s.zh: 去年春天，我妻子建议我请一位专业人士来检查一下我们的割草机。

s.en: It had broken down the previous summer, and though I promised to repair it, I had never got round to it.
s.zh: 它在前一个夏天就坏掉了，虽然我答应过要修理它，但一直没能抽空去修。

s.en: I would not hear of the suggestion and said that I would fix it myself.
s.zh: 我断然拒绝了她的建议，说我自己能修。

s.en: One Saturday afternoon, I hauled the machine into the garden and had a close look at it.
s.zh: 一个星期六的下午，我把那台机器搬到了花园里，仔细地观察了它一番。

s.en: As far as I could see, it needed only a minor adjustment:
s.zh: 据我所见，它只需要进行微小的调整即可。

s.en: a turn of a screw here, a little tightening up there, a drop of oil and it would be as good as new.
s.zh: 这里拧个螺丝，那里紧一紧，再滴几滴油，它就能焕然一新了。

s.en: Inevitably the repair job was not quite so simple.
s.zh: 不可避免地，这次维修工作并没有那么简单。

s.en: The mower firmly refused to mow, so I decided to dismantle it.
s.zh: 割草机就是不肯割草，于是我决定把它拆开。

s.en: The garden was soon littered with chunks of metal which had once made up a lawn mower.
s.zh: 花园里很快就散落着许多金属碎片——那些碎片原本是割草机的一部分。

s.en: But I was extremely pleased with myself. I had traced the cause of the trouble.
s.zh: 但我对自己感到非常满意。我已经找到了问题的根源。

s.en: One of the links in the chain that drives the wheels had snapped.
s.zh: 驱动轮子的链条上有一节断了。

s.en: After buying a new chain I was faced with the insurmountable task of putting the confusing jigsaw puzzle together again.
s.zh: 买了新链条后，我面临着一个无法完成的任务：把这个令人头疼的拼图重新装回去。

s.en: I was not surprised to find that the machine still refused to work after I had reassembled it,
s.zh: 当我重新组装好这台机器后，发现它仍然无法正常工作时，我并不感到惊讶。

s.en: for the simple reason that I was left with several curiously shaped bits of metal which did not seem to fit anywhere.
s.zh: 原因很简单：我手里还剩几块形状古怪的金属片，怎么也装不上去。

s.en: I gave up in despair.
s.zh: 我绝望地放弃了。

s.en: The weeks passed and the grass grew.
s.zh: 几周过去了，草也长高了。

s.en: When my wife nagged me to do something about it,
s.zh: 当妻子催我处理这事时，

s.en: I told her that either I would have to buy a new mower or let the grass grow.
s.zh: 我告诉她，要么我得买一台新的割草机，要么就任由草继续长下去。

s.en: Needless to say our house is now surrounded by a jungle.
s.zh: 不用说，我们家现在被一片丛林包围了。

s.en: Buried somewhere in deep grass there is a rusting lawn mower which I have promised to repair one day.
s.zh: 在茂密的草丛中，埋着一把生锈的割草机；我曾承诺有朝一日一定会把它修好。

q: Did the writer repair his lawn mower in the end? Why/Why not?
最后，作者修好了他的割草机吗？为什么（或为什么不）？

s.en: Pollution is the price we pay for an overpopulated, overindustrialized planet.
s.zh: 污染是我们这个人口过剩、过度工业化的星球所必须付出的代价。

s.en: When you come to think about it, there are only four ways you can deal with rubbish:
s.zh: 仔细想想，处理垃圾其实只有四种方法：

s.en: dump it, burn it, turn it into something you can use again, attempt to produce less of it.
s.zh: 把它扔掉、烧掉，或者把它改造成可以再次使用的东西；尽量减少它的生产量。

s.en: We keep trying all four methods, but the sheer volume of rubbish we produce worldwide threatens to overwhelm us.
s.zh: 我们一直在尝试这四种方法，但全球产生的垃圾数量实在庞大，几乎让我们应接不暇。

s.en: Rubbish, however, is only part of the problem of polluting our planet.
s.zh: 然而，垃圾仅仅是污染我们地球问题的一个方面罢了。

s.en: The need to produce ever increasing quantities of cheap food leads to a different kind of pollution.
s.zh: 对廉价食品日益增长的需求导致了另一种形式的污染。

s.en: Industrialized farming methods produce cheap meat products: beef, pork and chicken.
s.zh: 工业化农业生产方式能够制造出价格低廉的肉类产品，包括牛肉、猪肉和鸡肉。

s.en: The use of pesticides and fertilizers produces cheap grain and vegetables.
s.zh: 使用农药和化肥可以生产出价格低廉的谷物和蔬菜。

s.en: The price we pay for cheap food may be already too high:
s.zh: 我们为廉价食品所支付的价格可能已经太高了。

s.en: Mad Cow Disease (BSE) in cattle, salmonella in chicken and eggs, and listeria in dairy products.
s.zh: 牛的疯牛病（BSE）、鸡肉和鸡蛋中的沙门氏菌、乳制品中的李斯特菌……

s.en: And if you think you'll abandon meat and become a vegetarian,
s.zh: 如果你打算放弃吃肉、成为素食者，

s.en: you have the choice of very expensive organically-grown vegetables
s.zh: 你也有选择：要么购买价格昂贵的有机蔬菜，

s.en: or a steady diet of pesticides every time you think you're eating fresh salads and vegetables,
s.zh: 要么每次以为自己在吃新鲜沙拉或蔬菜时，其实都在摄入农药；

s.en: or just having an innocent glass of water!
s.zh: 甚至只是喝一杯看似无害的水，也可能摄入农药。

s.en: However, there is an even more insidious kind of pollution that particularly affects urban areas and invades our daily lives, and that is noise.
s.zh: 然而，还有一种更为隐蔽的污染形式，它尤其影响城市地区，并渗透到我们的日常生活中，那就是噪音。

s.en: Burglar alarms going off at any time of the day or night serve only to annoy passers-by and actually assist burglars to burgle.
s.zh: 防盗警报在日夜任何时候突然响起，不仅会惹恼路人，反而会帮助窃贼作案；

s.en: Car alarms constantly scream at us in the street and are a source of profound irritation.
s.zh: 汽车警报声在街上不断刺耳地鸣叫，令人极度烦躁。

s.en: A recent survey of the effects of noise revealed (surprisingly?)
s.zh: 最近一项关于噪音影响的调查显示（令人惊讶的是），

s.en: that dogs barking incessantly in the night rated the highest form of noise pollution on a scale ranging from 1 to 7.
s.zh: 夜间狗不停地吠叫被列为噪音污染中最严重的形式（在1到7的评分体系中得分最高）。

s.en: The survey revealed a large number of sources of noise that we really dislike.
s.zh: 这项调查还揭示了许多我们非常讨厌的噪音来源：

s.en: Lawn mowers whining on a summer's day, late-night parties in apartment blocks,
s.zh: 夏日里割草机的嗡嗡声、公寓楼里的深夜聚会……

s.en: noisy neighbours, vehicles of all kinds,
s.zh: 吵闹的邻居们，各种各样的车辆……

s.en: especially large container trucks thundering through quiet villages,
s.zh: 尤其是那些巨大的集装箱卡车，在宁静的村庄里轰鸣着驶过……

s.en: planes and helicopters flying overhead, large radios carried round in public places and played at maximum volume.
s.zh: 飞机和直升机在头顶上飞过；在公共场所，人们会携带大型收音机，并将音量调至最大来播放音乐。

s.en: New technology has also made its own contribution to noise.
s.zh: 新技术也为噪音问题做出了自己的'贡献'。

s.en: A lot of people object to mobile phones, especially when they are used in public places like restaurants or on public transport.
s.zh: 很多人反对在公共场所（如餐厅或公共交通工具上）使用手机。

s.en: Loud conversations on mobile phones invade our thoughts or interrupt the pleasure of meeting friends for a quiet chat.
s.zh: 手机上大声的通话声会干扰我们的思绪，或者打断我们与朋友安静交谈的乐趣。

s.en: The noise pollution survey revealed a rather surprising and possibly amusing old-fashioned source of noise.
s.zh: 噪音污染调查显示了一个相当令人惊讶、甚至有点滑稽的老式噪音来源。

s.en: It turned out to be snoring! Men were found to be the worst offenders.
s.zh: 原来问题出在打鼾上！研究发现，男性是打鼾问题最严重的群体。

s.en: It was revealed that 20% of men in their mid-thirties snore.
s.zh: 据调查显示，20%的三十多岁男性有打鼾的习惯。

s.en: This figure rises to a staggering 60% of men in their sixties.
s.zh: 而在六十多岁的男性中，这个数字惊人地高达60%。

s.en: Against these figures, it was found that only 5% of women snore regularly,
s.zh: 与这些数据相比，研究发现只有5%的女性经常打鼾。

s.en: while the rest are constantly woken or kept awake by their trumpeting partners.
s.zh: 而其余的女性则不断被她们如吹号般的伴侣吵醒或无法入睡。

s.en: Whatever the source of noise, one thing is certain: silence, it seems, has become a golden memory.
s.zh: 无论噪音的来源是什么，有一点是肯定的：宁静似乎已经成为了一段珍贵的回忆。

q: What does the writer describe as an 'amusing old-fashioned source of noise' ?
作者将什么描述为“一种有趣的老式噪音来源”？

s.en: In this much-travelled world, there are still thousands of places which are inaccessible to tourists.
s.zh: 在这个充满旅行的世界里，仍然有成千上万的地方对游客来说是无法到达的。

s.en: We always assume that villagers in remote places are friendly and hospitable.
s.zh: 我们总是认为偏远地区的村民友好且好客。

s.en: But people who are cut off not only from foreign tourists, but even from their own countrymen can be hostile to travellers.
s.zh: 然而，那些不仅与外国游客隔绝、甚至与本国人隔绝的人，可能会对旅行者怀有敌意。

s.en: Visits to really remote villages are seldom enjoyable--as my wife and I discovered during a tour through the Balkans.
s.zh: 真正偏远村庄的游览往往并不愉快——我和妻子在巴尔干半岛旅行时就深有体会。

s.en: We had spent several days in a small town and visited a number of old churches in the vicinity.
s.zh: 我们在一个小镇上待了几天，还参观了附近的几座古老教堂。

s.en: These attracted many visitors, for they were not only of great architectural interest, but contained a large number of beautifully preserved frescoes as well.
s.zh: 这些教堂吸引了许多游客，因为它们不仅在建筑上很有价值，而且还保存着大量精美的壁画。

s.en: On the day before our departure, several bus loads of tourists descended on the town.
s.zh: 出发前一天，一大批游客乘巴士来到了这个小镇。

s.en: This was more than we could bear, so we decided to spend our last day exploring the countryside.
s.zh: 这让我们难以忍受，于是我们决定在最后一天去乡村探索一番。

s.en: Taking a path which led out of the town, we crossed a few fields until we came to a dense wood.
s.zh: 我们沿着一条小路离开小镇，穿过几片田野，最终来到了一片茂密的森林。

s.en: We expected the path to end abruptly, but we found that it traced its way through the trees.
s.zh: 我们原本以为这条小路会突然结束，但实际上它蜿蜒穿过树林，继续延伸下去。

s.en: We tramped through the wood for over two hours until we arrived at a deep stream.
s.zh: 我们跋涉穿过森林，花了两个多小时的时间，终于来到了一条很深的小溪边。

s.en: We could see that the path continued on the other side, but we had no idea how we could get across the stream.
s.zh: 我们可以看到小路在另一边继续延伸，但我们完全不知道该如何穿过那条小溪。

s.en: Suddenly my wife spotted a boat moored to the bank.
s.zh: 突然，我的妻子发现有一艘船停靠在岸边。

s.en: In it there was a boatman fast asleep.
s.zh: 里面有一个正在熟睡的船夫。

s.en: We gently woke him up and asked him to ferry us to the other side.
s.zh: 我们轻轻地唤醒了他，然后请他带我们到另一边去。

s.en: Though he was reluctant to do so at first, we eventually persuaded him to take us.
s.zh: 虽然他一开始并不愿意，但我们最终说服了他带我们一起去。

s.en: The path led to a tiny village perched on the steep sides of a mountain.
s.zh: 这条小路通向一个坐落在陡峭山坡上的小村庄。

s.en: The place consisted of a straggling unmade road which was lined on either side by small houses.
s.zh: 这个地方有一条蜿蜒曲折、尚未铺好的道路，道路两旁排列着一些小房子。

s.en: Even under a clear blue sky, the village looked forbidding, as all the houses were built of grey mud bricks.
s.zh: 即使是在万里无云的蓝天下，这个村庄看起来依然令人望而生畏——所有的房屋都是用灰色的泥砖建造的。

s.en: The village seemed deserted,
s.zh: 这个村庄看起来像是被遗弃了。

s.en: the only sign of life being an ugly-looking black goat on a short length of rope tied to a tree in a field nearby.
s.zh: 唯一的生命迹象是一只长相丑陋的黑色山羊，它被用一根短绳子拴在附近田野里的一棵树上。

s.en: Sitting down on a dilapidated wooden fence near the field, we opened a couple of tins of sardines and had a picnic lunch.
s.zh: 我们坐在田野旁边那道破旧的木栅栏上，打开了几罐沙丁鱼，然后享用了一顿野餐午餐。

s.en: All at once, I noticed that my wife seemed to be filled with alarm.
s.zh: 突然间，我注意到我的妻子似乎显得非常惊恐。

s.en: Looking up I saw that we were surrounded by children in rags who were looking at us silently as we ate.
s.zh: 我抬头一看，发现，我们周围围着一群衣衫褴褛的孩子们；当我们吃饭时，他们静静地注视着我们。

s.en: We offered them food and spoke to them kindly, but they remained motionless.
s.zh: 我们给了他们食物，并用温和的语气与他们交谈，但他们依然一动不动。

s.en: I concluded that they were simply shy of strangers.
s.zh: 我得出结论：他们只是对陌生人感到害羞而已。

s.en: When we later walked down the main street of the village, we were followed by a silent procession of children.
s.zh: 后来，当我们沿着村庄的主街走去时，有一群沉默的孩子们跟在我们后面。

s.en: The village which had seemed deserted, immediately came to life.
s.zh: 这个原本看似荒无人烟的村庄立刻变得热闹起来。

s.en: Faces appeared at windows.
s.zh: 人们的身影出现在窗户前。

s.en: Men in shirt sleeves stood outside their houses and glared at us.
s.zh: 那些只穿着衬衫、没有穿外套的男人们站在自家房子外面，怒视着我们。

s.en: Old women in black shawls peered at us from doorways.
s.zh: 那些披着黑色披肩的老妇人从门缝里向我们张望。

s.en: The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard.
s.zh: 最可怕的是，竟然一点声音都听不到。

s.en: There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors.
s.zh: 毫无疑问，我们是不受欢迎的访客。

s.en: We needed no further warning.
s.zh: 我们不需要任何进一步的警告。

s.en: Turning back down the main street,
s.zh: 拐回主街道后，

s.en: we quickened our pace and made our way rapidly towards the stream where we hoped the boatman was waiting.
s.zh: 我们加快了步伐，迅速朝小溪走去，希望船夫正在那里等着我们。

q: Why was the village silent?
为什么这个村庄如此寂静？

s.en: It is a good thing my aunt Harriet died years ago.
s.zh: 幸好我的阿姨哈丽特几年前就去世了。

s.en: If she were alive today she would not be able to air her views on her favourite topic of conversation: domestic servants.
s.zh: 如果她今天还活着，她将无法再公开表达自己最热衷讨论的话题——也就是关于家庭佣人的看法了。

s.en: Aunt Harriet lived in that leisurely age when servants were employed to do housework.
s.zh: 哈丽特阿姨生活在那个时代：那时人们还会雇佣仆人来帮忙做家务。

s.en: She had a huge, rambling country house called 'The Gables'.
s.zh: 她拥有一座规模庞大、布局错综复杂的乡村住宅，名叫“The Gables”。

s.en: She was sentimentally attached to this house,
s.zh: 她对这栋房子怀有深厚的情感依恋。

s.en: for even though it was far too big for her needs, she persisted in living there long after her husband's death.
s.zh: 尽管那套房子远远超出了她的实际需求（空间太大，不符合她的居住要求），但在丈夫去世后，她仍然坚持住在那里很长时间。

s.en: Before she grew old, aunt Harriet used to entertain lavishly.
s.zh: 在哈丽特阿姨年老之前，她总是非常热情地招待客人，总是准备丰盛的美食和精彩的娱乐活动来款待他们。

s.en: I often visited The Gables when I was a boy.
s.zh: 我小时候经常去“The Gables”那个地方。

s.en: No matter how many guests were present, the great house was always immaculate.
s.zh: 无论有多少客人来访，那座宏伟的房子总是保持得一尘不染、整洁有序。

s.en: The parquet floors shone like mirrors;
s.zh: 镶木地板闪闪发光，就像镜子一样。

s.en: highly polished silver was displayed in gleaming glass cabinets;
s.zh: 那些经过精心打磨的银器被陈列在闪闪发光的玻璃柜中。

s.en: even my uncle's huge collection of books was kept miraculously free from dust.
s.zh: 就连我叔叔那庞大的藏书量，也奇迹般地没有一点灰尘。

s.en: Aunt Harriet presided over an invisible army of servants that continuously scrubbed, cleaned, and polished.
s.zh: 哈丽特阿姨指挥着一支“看不见的仆人队伍”，这支队伍不断地擦拭、清洁和抛光各种物品。

s.en: She always referred to them as 'the shifting population',
s.zh: 她总是把他们称为“流动人口”。

s.en: for they came and went with such frequency that I never even got a chance to learn their names.
s.zh: 因为他们来得频繁，去得也快，以至于我根本没机会记住他们的名字。

s.en: Though my aunt pursued what was, in those days an enlightened policy,
s.zh: 尽管我的姑姑在当时推行了一项被认为具有前瞻性的政策，

s.en: in that she never allowed her domestic staff to work more than eight hours a day, she was extremely difficult to please.
s.zh: 她从不让家中的佣人每天工作超过八小时，然而她仍很难伺候。

s.en: While she always criticized the fickleness of human nature,
s.zh: 虽然她总是批评人性的善变，

s.en: she carried on an unrelenting search for the ideal servant to the end of her days,
s.zh: 她一生都在不懈地寻找那个理想的仆人，直到生命的最后一刻。

s.en: even after she had been sadly disillusioned by Bessie.
s.zh: 即使在贝西（Bessie）使她大失所望之后，她也没有放弃。

s.en: Bessie worked for aunt Harriet for three years.
s.zh: 贝西在哈丽特阿姨家工作了三年。

s.en: During that time she so gained my aunt's confidence, that she was put in charge of the domestic staff.
s.zh: 在那段时间里，她赢得了我阿姨的充分信任，以至于被委以管理所有家务人员的重任。

s.en: Aunt Harriet could not find words to praise Bessie's industriousness and efficiency.
s.zh: 哈丽特阿姨实在找不到合适的词语来赞扬贝西的勤奋和高效。

s.en: In addition to all her other qualifications, Bessie was an expert cook.
s.zh: 除了拥有其他各种技能外，贝西还是一位烹饪高手。

s.en: She acted the role of the perfect servant for three years before Aunt Harriet discovered her 'little weakness'.
s.zh: 她扮演了“完美仆人”的角色长达三年，直到哈丽特阿姨发现了她的“小缺点”。

s.en: After being absent from The Gables for a week,
s.zh: 在离开“The Gables”这座宅邸一周之后，

s.en: my aunt unexpectedly returned one afternoon with a party of guests and instructed Bessie to prepare dinner.
s.zh: 一天下午，我的阿姨突然带着一群客人回来了，她吩咐贝西准备晚餐。

s.en: Not only was the meal well below the usual standard, but Bessie seemed unable to walk steadily.
s.zh: 这顿饭的质量远低于平时的标准；而且贝西似乎也走不稳了。

s.en: She bumped into the furniture and kept mumbling about the guests.
s.zh: 她撞到了家具，然后不停地嘟囔着关于那些客人的事情。

s.en: When she came in with the last course--a huge pudding--she tripped on the carpet
s.zh: 当她端着最后一道菜（一道巨大的布丁）进来时，她在地毯上绊倒了。

s.en: and the pudding went flying through the air, narrowly missed my aunt, and crashed on the dining table with considerable force.
s.zh: 布丁突然飞到了空中，差点撞到我的阿姨，然后猛烈地摔在了餐桌上。

s.en: Though this caused great mirth among the guests, Aunt Harriet was horrified.
s.zh: 虽然这引起了在场宾客们的阵阵笑声，但哈丽特阿姨却感到非常震惊。

s.en: She reluctantly came to the conclusion that Bessie was drunk.
s.zh: 她勉强得出结论：贝西肯定是喝醉了。

s.en: The guests had, of course, realized this from the moment Bessie opened the door for them and, long before the final catastrophe,
s.zh: 当然，客人们从贝西为他们开门的那一刻起就意识到了这一点；早在最终灾难发生之前，他们就已经察觉到了不对劲。

s.en: had had a difficult time trying to conceal their amusement.
s.zh: 他们很难掩饰自己的笑意。

s.en: The poor girl was dismissed instantly.
s.zh: 那个可怜的女孩立刻就被解雇了。

s.en: After her departure, Aunt Harriet discovered that there were piles of empty wine bottles of all shapes and sizes neatly stacked in what had once been Bessie's wardrobe.
s.zh: 在她离开后，哈丽特阿姨发现：曾经是贝西衣柜的地方，现在整齐地堆放着一堆堆形状各异、大小不一的空酒瓶。

s.en: They had mysteriously found their way there from the wine cellar!
s.zh: 它们竟然神秘地从酒窖里找到了通往那里的路！

q: What was Bessie's 'little weakness' ?
贝西的“小缺点”是什么？

s.en: The New Year is a time for resolutions.
s.zh: 新年是一个制定新目标的时刻。

s.en: Mentally, at least, most of us could compile formidable lists of 'dos' and 'don'ts'.
s.zh: 至少在精神层面上，我们大多数人都能列出一份详尽的“该做”与“不该做”的清单。

s.en: The same old favourites recur year in year out with monotonous regularity.
s.zh: 那些老掉牙的决心年复一年地重复出现，单调得令人厌烦。

s.en: We resolve to get up earlier each morning, eat less,
s.zh: 我们决定每天早上早起一些，少吃一些食物。

s.en: find more time to play with the children, do a thousand and one jobs about the house,
s.zh: 多花些时间陪孩子们玩耍，同时还要处理家里的各种琐事（比如打扫卫生、做饭、洗衣服等等）。

s.en: be nice to people we don't like, drive carefully, and take the dog for a walk every day.
s.zh: 对待那些我们不喜欢的人也要友善；开车时要小心谨慎；每天还要带狗狗去散步。

s.en: Past experience has taught us that certain accomplishments are beyond attainment.
s.zh: 过去的经验告诉我们，有些成就其实是无法实现的。

s.en: If we remain inveterate smokers, it is only because we have so often experienced the frustration that results from failure.
s.zh: 如果我们还是顽固的烟民，那只是因为我们太多次地经历了因失败而产生的挫败感。

s.en: Most of us fail in our efforts at self-improvement because our schemes are too ambitious and we never have time to carry them out.
s.zh: 我们大多数人在自我提升的努力中失败，是因为我们的计划过于宏大，而我们根本没有时间去执行。

s.en: We also make the fundamental error of announcing our resolutions to everybody
s.zh: 我们还有一个根本性的错误：那就是把我们的决心或计划公之于众。

s.en: so that we look even more foolish when we slip back into our bad old ways.
s.zh: 这样，当我们重新回到那些糟糕的老习惯时，看起来就会更加愚蠢了。

s.en: Aware of these pitfalls, this year I attempted to keep my resolutions to myself.
s.zh: 意识到这些陷阱后，今年我试着把决心只留给自己。

s.en: I limited myself to two modest ambitions: to do physical exercises every morning and to read more of an evening.
s.zh: 我给自己设定了两个简单的目标：每天早上坚持做体育锻炼，晚上多读书。

s.en: An all-night party on New Year's Eve provided me with a good excuse for not carrying out either of these new resolutions on the first day of the year,
s.zh: 新年前夜的通宵派对为我提供了一个很好的借口，让我能够在新年的第一天不执行任何这些新年决心。

s.en: but on the second, I applied myself assiduously to the task.
s.zh: 但到了第二天，我勤勉地执行起这项任务。

s.en: The daily exercises lasted only eleven minutes and I proposed to do them early in the morning before anyone had got up.
s.zh: 每天的锻炼只有十一分钟，我打算在清晨大家还没起床前做。

s.en: The self-discipline required to drag myself out of bed 11 minutes earlier than usual was considerable.
s.zh: 要比平时早11分钟起床，所需要的自制力是相当大的。

s.en: Nevertheless, I managed to creep down into the living room for two days before anyone found me out.
s.zh: 尽管如此，我还是设法在两天里悄悄溜进客厅，直到被家人发现。

s.en: After jumping about on the carpet and twisting the human frame into uncomfortable positions,
s.zh: 在地毯上跳来跳去、把身体扭成各种不舒服的姿势之后，

s.en: I sat down at the breakfast table in an exhausted condition.
s.zh: 我疲惫不堪地坐到了早餐桌前。

s.en: It was this that betrayed me.
s.zh: 正是这个状态出卖了我。

s.en: The next morning the whole family trooped in to watch the performance.
s.zh: 第二天早上，全家人都聚在一起观看这场表演。

s.en: That was really unsettling but I fended off the taunts and jibes of the family good-humouredly and soon everybody got used to the idea.
s.zh: 那确实让人不自在，但我用幽默的态度抵挡了家人的嘲笑和讥讽，大家很快就习惯了。

s.en: However, my enthusiasm waned.
s.zh: 然而，我的热情逐渐消退了。

s.en: The time I spent at exercises gradually diminished.
s.zh: 我花在锻炼上的时间逐渐减少了。

s.en: Little by little the eleven minutes fell to zero.
s.zh: 渐渐地，这十一分钟减少到了零。

s.en: By January 10th, I was back to where I had started from.
s.zh: 到了1月10日，我又回到了起点。

s.en: I argued that if I spent less time exhausting myself at exercises in the morning,
s.zh: 我心想，如果早上少花些时间把自己累得筋疲力尽，

s.en: I would keep my mind fresh for reading when I got home from work.
s.zh: 下班回家后我就能保持头脑清醒来读书了。

s.en: Resisting the hypnotizing effect of television,
s.zh: 为抵抗电视的催眠效果，

s.en: I sat in my room for a few evenings with my eyes glued to a book.
s.zh: 有好几个晚上，我待在房间里，眼睛一直粘在书上。

s.en: One night, however, feeling cold and lonely, I went downstairs and sat in front of the television pretending to read.
s.zh: 然而，有一天晚上，我感到寒冷又孤独，于是下楼坐在电视机前，假装在看书。

s.en: That proved to be my undoing, for I soon got back to my old bad habit of dozing off in front of the screen.
s.zh: 这证明是我的败因，因为我很快又恢复了在屏幕前打瞌睡的老毛病。

s.en: I still haven't given up my resolution to do more reading.
s.zh: 我仍然没有放弃多读书的决心。

s.en: In fact, I have just bought a book entitled How to Read a Thousand Words a Minute.
s.zh: 事实上，我刚刚买了一本书，书名是《如何一分钟读完一千个单词》。

s.en: Perhaps it will solve my problem, but I just haven't had time to read it!
s.zh: 也许这本书能解决我的问题，只是我还没时间去读它罢了！

q: What marked the end of the writer's New Year resolutions?
是什么标志着这位作家新年决心的结束呢？

s.en: Predicting the future is notoriously difficult.
s.zh: 预测未来向来是一件极其困难的事情。

s.en: Who could have imagined, in the mid 1970s, for example,
s.zh: 例如，在20世纪70年代中期，谁能想到，

s.en: that by the end of the 20th century, computers would be as common in people's homes as TV sets?
s.zh: 到20世纪末，计算机会在人们的家中变得像电视机一样普遍呢？

s.en: In the 1970s, computers were common enough,
s.zh: 在20世纪70年代，计算机已经相当普及了。

s.en: but only in big business, government departments and large organizations.
s.zh: 但这仅限于大企业、政府部门以及大型组织。

s.en: These were the so-called mainframe machines.
s.zh: 这些就是所谓的“大型机”（mainframe machines）。

s.en: Mainframe computers were very large indeed often occupying whole air-conditioned rooms,
s.zh: 大型机确实体积庞大，常常占据整个装有空调的房间。

s.en: employing full-time technicians and run on specially-written software.
s.zh: 这些机器配有全职技术人员，并运行专门编写的软件。

s.en: Though these large machines still exist,
s.zh: 尽管这些大型机器仍然存在，

s.en: many of their functions have been taken over by small powerful personal computers, commonly known as PCs.
s.zh: 它们的许多功能已经被功能强大、体积小巧的个人电脑（通常称为“PC”）所取代了。

s.en: In 1975, a primitive machine called the Altair, was launched in the USA.
s.zh: 1975年，一种名为 Altair 的早期计算机在美国问世。

s.en: It can properly be described as the first 'home computer' and it pointed the way to the future.
s.zh: 它完全可以被称作第一台“家用电脑”，并且为未来的发展方向指明了方向。

s.en: This was followed, at the end of the 1970s, by a machine called an Apple.
s.zh: 随后，在20世纪70年代末，出现了一种名为“Apple”的机器。

s.en: In the early 1980s, the computer giant, IBM produced the world's first Personal Computer.
s.zh: 20世纪80年代初，计算机巨头IBM推出了世界上第一台个人电脑（Personal Computer）。

s.en: This ran on an 'operating system' called DOS,
s.zh: 它运行在一个名为DOS的“操作系统”上。

s.en: produced by a then small company named Microsoft.
s.zh: 这款产品是由当时还是一家小型公司的微软（Microsoft）开发的。

s.en: The IBM Personal Computer was widely copied.
s.zh: IBM个人电脑被广泛地模仿和复制。

s.en: From those humble beginnings,
s.zh: 从这些简陋的起步阶段开始，

s.en: we have seen the development of the user-friendly home computers and multimedia machines which are in common use today.
s.zh: 我们已经见证了如今广泛使用的、用户友好的家用电脑和多媒体设备的不断发展。

s.en: Considering how recent these developments are, it is even more remarkable that as long ago as the 1960s, an Englishman,
s.zh: 考虑到这些发展都发生得如此之近，更令人惊讶的是：早在20世纪60年代，就有一位英国人——

s.en: Leon Bagrit, was able to predict some of the uses of computers which we know today.
s.zh: 莱昂·巴格里特（Leon Bagrit）成功预测了计算机的一些我们今天所知的用途。

s.en: Bagrit dismissed the idea that computers would learn to 'think' for themselves and would 'rule the world', which people liked to believe in those days.
s.zh: 巴格里特驳斥了这样一种观点：计算机能够学会“自主思考”并“统治世界”。在那个时候，许多人确实相信这种可能性。

s.en: Bagrit foresaw a time when computers would be small enough to hold in the hand,
s.zh: 巴格里特预见了一个时代：那时计算机会变得足够小巧，可以放在手中使用。

s.en: when they would be capable of providing information about traffic jams and suggesting alternative routes,
s.zh: 那时，它们能提供交通拥堵信息并建议备选路线；

s.en: when they would be used in hospitals to help doctors to diagnose illnesses,
s.zh: 能在医院里帮助医生诊断疾病；

s.en: when they would relieve office workers and accountants of dull, repetitive clerical work.
s.zh: 还能替办公室职员和会计承担枯燥、重复的文书工作。

s.en: All these computer uses have become commonplace.
s.zh: 所有这些计算机的使用方式都已经变得非常普遍了。

s.en: Of course, Leon Bagrit couldn't possibly have foreseen the development of the Internet,
s.zh: 当然，莱昂·巴格里特根本不可能预见到互联网的发展。

s.en: the worldwide system that enables us to communicate instantly with anyone in any part of the world by using computers linked to telephone networks.
s.zh: 互联网是一个全球系统，它让我们能够通过连接电话网络的计算机，与世界任何地方的任何人即时交流。

s.en: Nor could he have foreseen how we could use the Internet to obtain information on every known subject,
s.zh: 他也无法预见到我们如何能够利用互联网来获取关于所有已知主题的信息。

s.en: so we can read it on a screen in our homes and even print it as well if we want to.
s.zh: 这样我们就可以在家里的屏幕上阅读这些信息，如果需要的话，还可以打印出来。

s.en: Computers have become smaller and smaller, more and more powerful and cheaper and cheaper.
s.zh: 计算机变得越来越小，性能越来越强大，价格也越来越便宜。

s.en: This is what makes Leon Bagrit's predictions particularly remarkable.
s.zh: 这正是让莱昂·巴格里特的预测显得格外引人注目的原因。

s.en: If he, or someone like him, were alive today, he might be able to tell us what to expect in the next fifty years.
s.zh: 如果他或像他这样的人今天还活着，或许能告诉我们未来五十年会发生什么。

q: What was the 'future' electronic development that Leon Bagrit wasn't able to foresee?
莱昂·巴格里特没能预见的那项“未来”电子发展是什么？

s.en: My cousin, Harry, keeps a large curiously-shaped bottle on permanent display in his study.
s.zh: 我的表弟哈里在他的书房里永久性地展示着一个形状非常奇特的瓶子。

s.en: Despite the fact that the bottle is tinted a delicate shade of green,
s.zh: 尽管这个瓶子的颜色是一种淡雅的绿色，

s.en: an observant visitor would soon notice that it is filled with what looks like a thick, greyish substance.
s.zh: 一个细心的访客很快就会注意到，瓶子里装满了某种看起来像浓稠的、灰色的物质。

s.en: If you were to ask Harry what was in the bottle, he would tell you that it contained perfumed mud.
s.zh: 如果你问哈利瓶子里装的是什么，他会告诉你里面装的是香味的泥浆。

s.en: If you expressed doubt or surprise, he would immediately invite you to smell it and then to rub some into your skin.
s.zh: 如果你表现出怀疑或惊讶，他就会立刻邀请你闻一闻这种物质，然后让你把它涂抹在皮肤上。

s.en: The brief experiment would dispel any further doubts you might have.
s.zh: 这个简短的实验将会消除你可能存在的任何疑虑。

s.en: The bottle really does contain perfumed mud.
s.zh: 这个瓶子里确实装着带有香味的泥浆。

s.en: How Harry came into the possession of this outlandish stuff makes an interesting story which he is fond of relating.
s.zh: 哈利是如何得到这些奇怪物品的，这本身就是一个有趣的故事，而他也很喜欢讲这个故事。

s.en: Furthermore, the acquisition of this bottle cured him of a bad habit he had been developing for years.
s.zh: 此外，买到这个瓶子后，他改掉了自己多年来一直养成的一个坏习惯。

s.en: Harry used to consider it a great joke to go into expensive cosmetic shops and make outrageous requests for goods that do not exist.
s.zh: 哈里过去常常觉得：去那些高档的化妆品店，然后提出一些根本不存在的商品、并要求购买这些商品，这简直是个天大的笑话。

s.en: He would invent fanciful names on the spot.
s.zh: 他总能即兴想出一些奇特、富有想象力的名字。

s.en: On entering a shop,
s.zh: 当走进一家商店时，

s.en: he would ask for a new perfume called 'Scented Shadow' or for 'insoluble bath cubes'.
s.zh: 他会要求购买一款名为“Scented Shadow”的新香水，或者“insoluble bath cubes”（即不可溶解的浴盐块）。

s.en: If a shop assistant told him she had not heard of it, he would pretend to be considerably put out.
s.zh: 如果店员告诉他她从未听说过那个产品，他就会假装非常失望（或很不高兴）。

s.en: He loved to be told that one of his imaginary products was temporarily out of stock
s.zh: 他很喜欢听到这样的消息：他想象中的某个产品暂时缺货了。

s.en: and he would faithfully promise to call again at some future date, but of course he never did.
s.zh: 他会郑重承诺将来某个时候再来光顾，但当然，他从未兑现过这个承诺。

s.en: How Harry managed to keep a straight face during these performances is quite beyond me.
s.zh: 我实在无法理解：哈利在那些表演过程中是如何始终保持面无表情的……

s.en: Harry does not need to be prompted to explain how he bought his precious bottle of mud.
s.zh: 哈利根本不需要别人提醒，他就能解释自己是如何买到那瓶珍贵的“泥”的。

s.en: One day, he went to an exclusive shop in London and asked for 'Myrolite'.
s.zh: 有一天，他去了伦敦的一家高档商店，询问是否有“Myrolite”这种商品。

s.en: The shop assistant looked puzzled and Harry repeated the word, slowly stressing each syllable.
s.zh: 店员看起来很困惑，于是哈利又重复了这个词，慢慢地、一个音节一个音节地念了出来。

s.en: When the woman shook her head in bewilderment,
s.zh: 当那位女士困惑地摇头时，

s.en: Harry went on to explain that 'myrolite' was a hard, amber-like substance which could be used to remove freckles.
s.zh: 哈里接着解释说，“myrolite”是一种质地坚硬、呈琥珀色的物质，可以用来去除雀斑。

s.en: This explanation evidently conveyed something to the woman who searched shelf after shelf.
s.zh: 这个解释显然让那位在货架间翻找东西的女士明白了些什么。

s.en: She produced all sorts of weird concoctions, but none of them met with Harry's requirements.
s.zh: 她拿出了各种各样的奇怪混合物，但没有一种能满足哈里的要求。

s.en: When Harry put on his act of being mildly annoyed, the assistant promised to order some for him.
s.zh: 当哈里装出一副有点恼火的样子时，助手答应会帮他订购一些东西。

s.en: Intoxicated by his success, Harry then asked for perfumed mud.
s.zh: 被自己的成功冲昏了头脑，哈里随后要求得到那种带有香味的泥浆。

s.en: He expected the assistant to look at him in blank astonishment.
s.zh: 他期待着助手会惊讶地、一脸茫然地看着他。

s.en: However, it was his turn to be surprised, for the woman's eyes immediately lit up
s.zh: 然而，轮到他感到惊讶了——因为那个女人的眼睛立刻亮了起来。

s.en: and she fetched several bottles which she placed on the counter for Harry to inspect.
s.zh: 然后她拿来了几瓶香泥，把它们放在柜台上让哈里查看。

s.en: For once, Harry had to admit defeat.
s.zh: 这一次，哈利不得不承认自己失败了。

s.en: He picked up what seemed to be the smallest bottle and discreetly asked the price.
s.zh: 他拿起了那个看起来是最小的瓶子，然后悄悄地询问了价格。

s.en: He was glad to get away with a mere twenty pounds and he beat a hasty retreat, clutching the precious bottle under his arm.
s.zh: 他很庆幸只花了二十英镑，于是急忙逃走了，同时紧紧地把那个珍贵的瓶子夹在腋下。

s.en: From then on, Harry decided that this little game he had invented might prove to be expensive.
s.zh: 从那以后，哈利意识到自己发明的这个“小游戏”可能会带来严重的后果（或者：这个小游戏可能会让他付出沉重的代价）。

s.en: The curious bottle which now adorns the bookcase in his study was his first and last purchase of rare cosmetics.
s.zh: 那个现在摆放在他书房书架上的奇特瓶子，是他第一次也是最后一次购买的稀有化妆品。

q: Why did Harry decide to give up his little game?
为什么哈利决定放弃他的那个小把戏（或：为什么哈利决定不再玩那个小游戏）？

s.en: The Scandinavian countries are much admired all over the world for their enlightened social policies.
s.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚国家因其开明的社会政策而受到全世界的广泛赞誉。

s.en: Sweden has evolved an excellent system for protecting the individual citizen from high-handed or incompetent public officers.
s.zh: 瑞典已经建立了一套非常完善的制度，旨在保护公民免受专横或无能的公职人员的侵害。

s.en: The system has worked so well, that it has been adopted in other countries too.
s.zh: 该系统运行得非常出色，因此也被其他国家采纳使用了。

s.en: The Swedes were the first to recognize that public officials like civil servants,
s.zh: 瑞典人是最早意识到像公务员这样的公职人员可能会犯错或行为过激的人。

s.en: police officers, health inspectors or tax-collectors can make mistakes or act over-zealously in the belief that they are serving the public.
s.zh: 警察、卫生检查员或税务官员都可能犯错，或者因为自认为是在为公众服务而表现得过于热心（即行为过于激进）。

s.en: As long ago as 1809, the Swedish Parliament introduced a scheme to safeguard the interest of the individual.
s.zh: 早在1809年，瑞典议会就出台了一项旨在保护个人权益的方案。

s.en: A parliamentary committee representing all political parties appoints a person who is suitably qualified to investigate private grievances against the State.
s.zh: 一个代表所有政党的议会委员会，会任命一位具备适当资格的人来调查公民对政府提出的个人投诉。

s.en: The official title of the person is 'Justiteombudsman', but the Swedes commonly refer to him as the 'J.O.' or 'Ombudsman'.
s.zh: 这个人的正式头衔是“司法监察专员”（Justice Ombudsman），但瑞典人通常称他为“J.O.”或“Ombudsman”。

s.en: The Ombudsman is not subject to political pressure.
s.zh: 监察专员不受政治压力的影响。

s.en: He investigates complaints large and small that come to him from all levels of society.
s.zh: 他负责调查来自社会各个阶层的各种投诉，无论这些投诉的规模大小如何。

s.en: As complaints must be made in writing, the Ombudsman receives an average of 1,200 letters a year.
s.zh: 由于投诉必须以书面形式提出，因此监察专员每年平均会收到 1,200 封来信。

s.en: He has eight lawyer assistants to help him and he examines every single letter in detail.
s.zh: 他有八名律师助理协助他工作，他会仔细审查每一封信的内容。

s.en: There is nothing secretive about the Ombudsman's work, for his correspondence is open to public inspection.
s.zh: 监察专员的工作没有任何保密性；他的所有通信记录都可供公众查阅。

s.en: If a citizen's complaint is justified the Ombudsman will act on his behalf.
s.zh: 如果公民的投诉是合理的，监察专员将会代表该公民采取行动。

s.en: The action he takes varies according to the nature of the complaint.
s.zh: 他采取的行动会根据投诉的性质而有所不同。

s.en: He may gently reprimand an official or even suggest to parliament that a law be altered.
s.zh: 他可能会温和地告诫某位官员，甚至向议会提出修改法律的建议。

s.en: The following case is a typical example of the Ombudsman's work.
s.zh: 以下案例是监察专员工作的典型例子。

s.en: A foreigner living in a Swedish village wrote to the Ombudsman complaining that he had been ill-treated by the police,
s.zh: 一位居住在瑞典村庄的外国人写信给监察专员，投诉称自己受到了警方的虐待。

s.en: simply because he was a foreigner.
s.zh: 仅仅因为他是外国人。

s.en: The Ombudsman immediately wrote to the Chief of Police in the district asking him to send a record of the case.
s.zh: 监察专员立即致函该地区的警察局长，要求他提供该案件的详细记录。
