s.en: There was nothing in the record to show that the foreigner's complaint was justified
s.zh: 记录中没有任何内容表明那位外国人的投诉是合理的

s.en: and the Chief of Police strongly denied the accusation.
s.zh: 警方局长强烈否认了这一指控。

s.en: It was impossible for the Ombudsman to take action,
s.zh: 监察专员根本无法采取任何行动。

s.en: but when he received a similar complaint from another foreigner in the same village,
s.zh: 但是当他收到同一村庄里另一位外国人类似的投诉时，

s.en: he immediately sent one of his lawyers to investigate the matter.
s.zh: 他立即派了自己的律师去调查这件事。

s.en: The lawyer ascertained that a policeman had indeed dealt roughly with foreigners on several occasions.
s.zh: 律师证实，确实有警察在多次场合中对外国人采取了粗暴的态度。

s.en: The fact that the policeman was prejudiced against foreigners could not be recorded in the official files.
s.zh: 这名警察对外国人存在偏见这一事实，无法被记录在官方文件中。

s.en: It was only possible for the Ombudsman to find this out by sending one of his representatives to check the facts.
s.zh: 只有通过派遣他的代表去核实事实，监察专员才得以发现这一情况。

s.en: The policeman in question was severely reprimanded
s.zh: 这名涉事的警察受到了严厉的训斥。

s.en: and was informed that if any further complaints were lodged against him, he would be prosecuted.
s.zh: 并且被告知，如果再有人对他提出投诉，他将会被起诉。

s.en: The Ombudsman's prompt action at once put an end to an unpleasant practice which might have gone unnoticed.
s.zh: 监察专员的迅速行动立即制止了这一可能被忽视的不良行为。

q: What could not be reported in the official files?
有哪些内容是无法被记录在官方文件中的呢？

s.en: We have been brought up to fear insects.
s.zh: 我们从小就被教导要害怕昆虫。

s.en: We regard them as unnecessary creatures that do more harm than good.
s.zh: 我们认为它们是毫无必要的生物，带来的危害远大于好处。

s.en: We continually wage war on them, for they contaminate our food, carry diseases, or devour our crops.
s.zh: 我们一直在与它们作斗争——因为它们会污染我们的食物、传播疾病，或者啃食我们的庄稼。

s.en: They sting or bite without provocation; they fly uninvited into our rooms on summer nights, or beat against our lighted windows.
s.zh: 它们会无缘无故地蜇人或咬人；在夏夜，它们会不请自来地飞进我们的房间，或者撞击我们亮着的窗户。

s.en: We live in dread not only of unpleasant insects like spiders or wasps, but of quite harmless ones like moths.
s.zh: 我们不仅害怕像蜘蛛或黄蜂这样的令人不快的昆虫，也害怕像蛾子这样其实完全无害的昆虫。

s.en: Reading about them increases our understanding without dispelling our fears.
s.zh: 阅读关于它们的信息确实能增加我们的理解，但并不会消除我们的恐惧。

s.en: Knowing that the industrious ant lives in a highly organized society
s.zh: 我们知道，勤劳的蚂蚁生活在一种高度有序的社会中。

s.en: does nothing to prevent us from being filled with revulsion when we find hordes of them crawling over a carefully prepared picnic lunch.
s.zh: 这丝毫无法阻止我们看到成群这样的生物爬在我们精心准备的野餐食物上时感到极度厌恶。

s.en: No matter how much we like honey,
s.zh: 无论我们多么喜欢蜂蜜，

s.en: or how much we have read about the uncanny sense of direction which bees possess, we have a horror of being stung.
s.zh: 无论我们读过多少关于蜜蜂惊人方向感的描述，我们仍然对被蜜蜂蜇伤感到恐惧。

s.en: Most of our fears are unreasonable, but they are impossible to erase.
s.zh: 我们的大多数恐惧都是毫无道理的，但它们却无法被彻底消除。

s.en: At the same time, however, insects are strangely fascinating.
s.zh: 然而，昆虫同时又有一种奇妙的魅力，让人着迷。

s.en: We enjoy reading about them, especially when we find that, like the praying mantis, they lead perfectly horrible lives.
s.zh: 我们喜欢阅读关于它们的内容，尤其是当发现它们（就像螳螂一样）过着极其恐怖的生活时。

s.en: We enjoy staring at them, entranced as they go about their business, unaware (we hope) of our presence.
s.zh: 我们喜欢凝视着它们，看着它们忙着自己的事情；希望它们没有察觉到我们的存在。

s.en: Who has not stood in awe at the sight of a spider pouncing on a fly,
s.zh: 谁没有在看到蜘蛛突然扑向一只苍蝇的瞬间感到惊叹呢？

s.en: or a column of ants triumphantly bearing home an enormous dead beetle?
s.zh: 或者是一队蚂蚁，胜利地抬着一只巨大的死甲虫回家？

s.en: Last summer I spent days in the garden watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
s.zh: 去年夏天，我在花园里待了好几天，观察成千上万的蚂蚁爬上我那棵珍贵的桃树的树干。

s.en: The tree has grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.
s.zh: 这棵树生长在房子背风的一侧，紧靠着一面温暖的墙壁。

s.en: I am especially proud of it,
s.zh: 我对此感到特别自豪。

s.en: not only because it has survived several severe winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.
s.zh: 不仅因为它经受住了几个严冬的考验，还因为它偶尔会结出美味的桃子。

s.en: During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.
s.zh: 夏天时，我注意到树上的叶子开始枯萎了。

s.en: Clusters of tiny insects called aphides were to be found on the underside of the leaves.
s.zh: 在叶子的背面，可以发现一群被称为蚜虫的微小昆虫。

s.en: They were visited by a large colony of ants which obtained a sort of honey from them.
s.zh: 有一大群蚂蚁造访了它们，并从它们身上获取了一种类似蜂蜜的物质。

s.en: I immediately embarked on an experiment which even though it failed to get rid of the ants kept me fascinated for twenty-four hours.
s.zh: 我立刻开始了一项实验。尽管这项实验未能彻底消灭那些蚂蚁，但它让我着迷了整整24个小时。

s.en: I bound the base of the tree with sticky tape, making it impossible for the ants to reach the aphides.
s.zh: 我用粘性胶带把树干的底部缠了起来，这样蚂蚁就无法接触到蚜虫了。

s.en: The tape was so sticky that they did not dare to cross it.
s.zh: 胶带非常粘，它们不敢爬过去。

s.en: For a long time, I watched them scurrying around the base of the tree in bewilderment.
s.zh: 很长时间里，我看着它们困惑地在树根周围慌乱地爬来爬去。

s.en: I even went out at midnight with a torch and noted with satisfaction (and surprise)
s.zh: 我甚至在午夜时分拿着手电筒出门，满意地（又惊讶地）看到

s.en: that the ants were still swarming around the sticky tape without being able to do anything about it.
s.zh: 那些蚂蚁仍然在粘性胶带周围团团转，却对此束手无策。

s.en: I got up early next morning hoping to find that the ants had given up in despair.
s.zh: 第二天早上我早早起床，希望看到蚂蚁们已经绝望地放弃了。

s.en: Instead, I saw that they had discovered a new route.
s.zh: 相反，我发现它们找到了一条新的路线。

s.en: They were climbing up the wall of the house and then on to the leaves of the tree.
s.zh: 它们沿着房子的墙壁爬上去，然后又爬到了树上的叶子上。

s.en: I realized sadly that I had been completely defeated by their ingenuity.
s.zh: 遗憾的是，我发现自己完全被它们的聪明才智给打败了。

s.en: The ants had been quick to find an answer to my thoroughly unscientific methods!
s.zh: 蚂蚁们很快就找到了对付我那些完全不科学的方法的办法！

q: Was the writer successful in protecting his peach tree? Why not?
作者成功保护了他的桃树吗？为什么没有呢？

s.en: Recent developments in astronomy have made it possible to detect planets in our own Milky Way and in other galaxies.
s.zh: 天文学的最新发展使得我们能够探测到我们自己的银河系以及其他星系中的行星。

s.en: This is a major achievement because, in relative terms, planets are very small and do not emit light.
s.zh: 这是一个重大成就，因为从相对的角度看，行星体积很小，而且自身并不发光。

s.en: Finding planets is proving hard enough, but finding life on them will prove infinitely more difficult.
s.zh: 找到行星已经够难了，但在其上寻找生命将更加困难。

s.en: The first question to answer is whether a planet can actually support life.
s.zh: 首先要回答的问题是：行星是否真的能够支持生命。

s.en: In our own solar system, for example, Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
s.zh: 例如在我们的太阳系中，金星太热，火星又太冷，都无法维持生命。

s.en: Only the Earth provides ideal conditions, and even here it has taken more than four billion years for plant and animal life to evolve.
s.zh: 只有地球提供了理想的条件，但即便如此，植物和动物生命的进化也花费了四十多亿年。

s.en: Whether a planet can support life depends on the size and brightness of its star, that is its 'sun'.
s.zh: 行星能否支持生命取决于其恒星（也就是它的“太阳”）的大小和亮度。

s.en: Imagine a star up to twenty times larger, brighter and hotter than our own sun.
s.zh: 设想一颗比我们的太阳大、亮、热都高出二十倍的恒星。

s.en: A planet would have to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
s.zh: 行星必须离它非常遥远，才有可能维持生命。

s.en: Alternatively, if the star were small,
s.zh: 或者，如果那颗恒星很小，

s.en: the life-supporting planet would have to have a close orbit round it and also provide the perfect conditions for life forms to develop.
s.zh: 这颗能够维持生命的行星必须拥有一个靠近该恒星的轨道，并且必须提供适合生命形式发展的完美条件。

s.en: But how would we find such a planet?
s.zh: 但是，我们该如何找到这样一颗行星呢？

s.en: At present, there is no telescope in existence that is capable of detecting the presence of life.
s.zh: 目前，还没有任何现有的望远镜能够探测到生命的存在。

s.en: The development of such a telescope will be one of the great astronomical projects of the 21st century.
s.zh: 开发这样的望远镜将是21世纪最重要的天文项目之一。

s.en: It is impossible to look for life on another planet using earth-based telescopes.
s.zh: 使用地球上的望远镜，是不可能在其他行星上寻找生命的。

s.en: Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope
s.zh: 我们自身温暖的大气层，以及望远镜产生的热量，

s.en: would make it impossible to detect objects as small as planets.
s.zh: 会使得检测像行星这样微小的物体变得不可能。

s.en: Even a telescope in orbit round the earth, like the very successful Hubble telescope,
s.zh: 即使是像哈勃望远镜这样非常成功的、位于地球轨道上的望远镜，

s.en: would not be suitable because of the dust particles in our solar system.
s.zh: 由于太阳系中存在大量的尘埃颗粒，这种方法并不适用。

s.en: A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter to look for life in outer space,
s.zh: 望远镜必须远到像木星那样远的地方，才能在外太空寻找生命，

s.en: because the dust becomes thinner the further we travel towards the outer edges of our own solar system.
s.zh: 因为我们越往太阳系外围走，尘埃就越稀薄。

s.en: Once we detected a planet, we would have to find a way of blotting out the light from its star,
s.zh: 一旦我们发现了一颗行星，我们就必须想办法遮挡掉来自该行星恒星的光线。

s.en: so that we would be able to 'see' the planet properly and analyse its atmosphere.
s.zh: 这样我们就能清楚地“看到”这颗行星，并分析其大气层了。

s.en: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life, rather than 'little green men'.
s.zh: 首先，我们寻找的是植物生命，而不是所谓的“小绿人”。

s.en: The life forms most likely to develop on a planet would be bacteria.
s.zh: 最有可能在行星上生存的生命形式是细菌。

s.en: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
s.zh: 正是细菌产生了我们地球上所呼吸的氧气。

s.en: For most of the earth's history they have been the only form of life on our planet.
s.zh: 在地球历史的大部分时间里，它们都是地球上唯一的生命形式。

s.en: As Earth-dwellers, we always cherish the hope that we will be visited by little green men and that we will be able to communicate with them.
s.zh: 作为地球人，我们始终怀揣着这样的希望：有一天，外星的小绿人会来到我们身边，我们能够与他们进行交流。

s.en: But this hope is always in the realms of science fiction.
s.zh: 然而，这种希望始终只存在于科幻作品的范畴之中。

s.en: If we were able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.
s.zh: 如果我们能够在另一颗行星上发现像细菌这样的简单生命形式，那将彻底改变我们对自己的认知。

s.en: As Daniel Goldin of NASA observed, 'Finding life elsewhere would change everything.
s.zh: 正如NASA的丹尼尔·戈尔丁所说：“在其它地方发现生命将会改变一切。

s.en: No human endeavour or thought would be unchanged by it.'
s.zh: 人类的任何努力或思想都会因此改变。”

q: Which life forms are most likely to develop on a distant planet?
哪些生命形式最有可能在遥远的行星上出现？

s.en: The river which forms the eastern boundary of our farm has always played an important part in our lives.
s.zh: 那条构成我们农场东部边界的河流，一直在我们的生活中扮演重要角色。

s.en: Without it we could not make a living.
s.zh: 没有它，我们就无法谋生。

s.en: There is only enough spring water to supply the needs of the house so we have to pump from the river for farm use.
s.zh: 这里的泉水仅够满足房屋的需求，因此我们必须从河里抽水来用于农场灌溉。

s.en: We tell the river all our secrets.
s.zh: 我们会把所有的秘密都告诉这条河流。

s.en: We know instinctively, just as beekeepers with their bees,
s.zh: 我们凭直觉明白，就像养蜂人对待他们的蜜蜂一样，

s.en: that misfortune might overtake us if the important events of our lives were not related to it.
s.zh: 如果我们生活中的重要事件没有告诉这条河流，不幸就可能降临到我们头上。

s.en: We have special river birthday parties in the summer.
s.zh: 夏天，我们会在河边举办特别的生日聚会。

s.en: Sometimes we go upstream to a favourite backwater,
s.zh: 有时我们会去上游一个我们喜欢的小水湾，

s.en: sometimes we have our party at the boathouse,
s.zh: 有时则会在船屋里举行派对。

s.en: which a predecessor of ours at the farm built in the meadow hard by the deepest pool for swimming and diving.
s.zh: 这是我们农场的一位前辈在草地上建造的，就在最深的池塘旁边，供游泳和跳水使用。

s.en: In a heat wave we choose a midnight birthday party and that is the most exciting of all.
s.zh: 在热浪期间，我们选择在午夜举办生日派对——这真的是所有庆祝方式中最令人兴奋的。

s.en: We welcome the seasons by the riverside, crowning the youngest girl with flowers in the spring,
s.zh: 我们在河边迎接四季的更替；春天来临时，我们会用鲜花为最年幼的女孩戴上花环。

s.en: holding a summer festival on Midsummer Eve, giving thanks for the harvest in the autumn, and throwing a holly wreath into the current in the winter.
s.zh: 在仲夏前夜举办夏季庆典，在秋天感恩丰收；而在冬天，则将冬青花环抛入河流中。

s.en: After a long period of rain the river may overflow its banks.
s.zh: 经过长时间的降雨，河流可能会泛滥出河岸。

s.en: This is a rare occurrence as our climate seldom goes to extremes.
s.zh: 这种情况很少见，因为我们的气候很少会走极端。

s.en: We are lucky in that only the lower fields,
s.zh: 我们很幸运的是，只有下方的田地，

s.en: which make up a very small proportion of our farm, are affected by flooding,
s.zh: 这些田地只占我们农场的很小一部分，会受到洪水影响，

s.en: but other farms are less favourably sited, and flooding can sometimes spell disaster for their owners.
s.zh: 但其他农场的地理位置较为不利，洪水有时会对农场主造成严重的灾难性后果。

s.en: One bad winter we watched the river creep up the lower meadows.
s.zh: 有一个严冬，我们眼睁睁看着河水逐渐淹没了下游的草地。

s.en: All the cattle had been moved into stalls and we stood to lose little.
s.zh: 所有的牛都被赶进了牛棚里，所以我们几乎不会有什么损失。

s.en: We were, however, worried about our nearest neighbours, whose farm was low lying and who were newcomers to the district.
s.zh: 然而，我们很担心我们的近邻——他们的农场位于地势较低的地方，而且他们是刚搬到这个地区来的新居民。

s.en: As the floods had put the telephone out of order, we could not find out how they were managing.
s.zh: 由于洪水使电话中断，我们无法知道他们的情况如何。

s.en: From an attic window we could get a sweeping view of the river where their land joined ours,
s.zh: 从阁楼的窗户里，我们可以看到河流的全景；他们的土地与我们的土地在那里交汇。

s.en: and at the most critical juncture we took turns in watching that point.
s.zh: 在最关键的时刻，我们轮流监视那个地点。

s.en: The first sign of disaster was a dead sheep floating down.
s.zh: 灾难的第一个征兆是一只死羊漂浮在水面上。

s.en: Next came a horse, swimming bravely,
s.zh: 接下来是一匹马，它勇敢地游着。

s.en: but we were afraid that the strength of the current would prevent its landing anywhere before it became exhausted.
s.zh: 但我们担心，水流的力量会使它在精疲力竭之前无法靠岸。

s.en: Suddenly a raft appeared, looking rather like Noah's ark, carrying the whole family, a few hens, the dogs, a cat, and a bird in a cage.
s.zh: 突然，一只木筏出现了，它看起来很像诺亚方舟；木筏上载着整个家庭、几只母鸡、几只狗、一只猫，以及一只关在笼子里的鸟。

s.en: We realized that they must have become unduly frightened by the rising flood,
s.zh: 我们意识到，他们一定是被不断上涨的洪水吓坏了。

s.en: for their house, which had sound foundations, would have stood stoutly even if it had been almost submerged.
s.zh: 他们的房子地基非常坚固，即使几乎被水淹没，也能依然屹立不倒。

s.en: The men of our family waded down through our flooded meadows with boat hooks,
s.zh: 我们家的男人们拿着船钩，蹚过被洪水淹没的草地。

s.en: in the hope of being able to grapple a corner of the raft and pull it out of the current towards our bank.
s.zh: 希望能钩住木筏的一角，把它从急流中拉到我们岸边。

s.en: We still think it a miracle that they were able to do so.
s.zh: 我们至今仍认为他们能这样做是个奇迹。

q: Why had the neighbours left their farm?
邻居为什么离开他们的农场？

s.en: I stopped to let the car cool off and to study the map.
s.zh: 我停下来，让车子冷却一下，同时仔细研究地图。

s.en: I had expected to be near my objective by now, but everything still seemed alien to me.
s.zh: 我本以为自己应该已经接近目的地了，但周围的一切依然让我感到陌生。

s.en: I was only five when my father had taken me abroad, and that was eighteen years ago.
s.zh: 我五岁的时候，父亲把我带到了国外，那已经是十八年前的事了。

s.en: When my mother had died after a tragic accident, he did not quickly recover from the shock and loneliness.
s.zh: 母亲在一次悲剧性的事故中去世后，他久久无法从震惊和孤独中走出来。

s.en: Everything around him was full of her presence, continually reopening the wound.
s.zh: 他身边的每一样东西都让他想起她，那些回忆不断重新揭开他的伤痛。

s.en: So he decided to emigrate.
s.zh: 于是，他决定移民。

s.en: In the new country he became absorbed in making a new life for the two of us, so that he gradually ceased to grieve.
s.zh: 在新的国家里，他全身心地投入到为我们俩创造新生活的过程中，渐渐地，他的悲伤也减轻了。

s.en: He did not marry again and I was brought up without a woman's care; but I lacked for nothing, for he was both father and mother to me.
s.zh: 他再也没有再婚，我在没有女性照顾的环境中长大；不过我并不缺乏什么，因为父亲同时扮演着母亲的角色。

s.en: He always meant to go back one day, but not to stay.
s.zh: 他一直说总有一天会回去，但并不是为了定居。

s.en: His roots and mine had become too firmly embedded in the new land.
s.zh: 他的根基和我的根基都已经深深地扎根在这片新的土地上。

s.en: But he wanted to see the old folk again and to visit my mother's grave.
s.zh: 但他想再见见那些老朋友，也想去看看我母亲的坟墓。

s.en: He became mortally ill a few months before we had planned to go and, when he knew that he was dying, he made me promise to go on my own.
s.zh: 就在我们计划出发的几个月前，他病入膏肓。当他知道自己时日无多时，他让我答应独自完成这次旅程。

s.en: I hired a car the day after landing and bought a comprehensive book of maps,
s.zh: 我落地后的第二天就租了一辆车，并买了一本内容详尽的地图册。

s.en: which I found most helpful on the cross-country journey, but which I did not think I should need on the last stage.
s.zh: 这在我长途旅行的过程中确实非常有用，不过我觉得在最后一段旅程中应该并不需要它。

s.en: It was not that I actually remembered anything at all.
s.zh: 其实我根本什么都不记得了。

s.en: But my father had described over and over again what we should see at every milestone after leaving the nearest town,
s.zh: 但我父亲一遍又一遍地描述过，在离开最近的那个小镇之后，我们在每一块里程碑处应该看到什么。

s.en: so that I was positive I should recognize it as familiar territory.
s.zh: 这样我就能肯定自己会认出这片熟悉的地方。

s.en: Well, I had been wrong, for I was now lost.
s.zh: 好吧，我错了——因为我现在真的迷路了。

s.en: I looked at the map and then at the milometer.
s.zh: 我先看了看地图，然后又看了看里程表。

s.en: I had come ten miles since leaving the town and at this point, according to my father,
s.zh: 自从离开小镇后，我已经走了十英里。据我父亲说，

s.en: I should be looking at farms and cottages in a valley,
s.zh: 我本应看到山谷里的农场和小屋，

s.en: with the spire of the church of our village showing in the far distance.
s.zh: 远处，我们村庄教堂的尖顶清晰可见。

s.en: I could see no valley, no farms, no cottages and no church spire-only a lake.
s.zh: 我看不到任何山谷、农场、小屋，也没有教堂的尖塔——只有一片湖泊。

s.en: I decided that I must have taken a wrong turning somewhere.
s.zh: 我意识到自己肯定在某个地方走错了路（即选择了错误的方向或路径）。

s.en: So I drove back to the town and began to retrace the route, taking frequent glances at the map.
s.zh: 于是我开车回到了镇上，开始沿着原来的路线返回，同时不时地查看地图。

s.en: I landed up at the same corner.
s.zh: 结果我又回到了同一个路口。

s.en: The curious thing was that the lake was not marked on the map.
s.zh: 奇怪的是，这个湖泊在地图上根本没有标注。

s.en: I felt as if I had stumbled into a nightmare country, as you sometimes do in dreams.
s.zh: 我感觉自己仿佛闯入了一个噩梦般的国度——就像在梦中有时会遇到的那样。

s.en: And, as in a nightmare, there was nobody in sight to help me.
s.zh: 就像在噩梦中一样，周围根本没有人能够帮助我。

s.en: Fortunately for me, as I was wondering what to do next,
s.zh: 幸运的是，就在我思考接下来该做什么的时候，

s.en: there appeared on the horizon a man on horseback, riding in my direction.
s.zh: 地平线上出现了一个骑马的人，他正朝我的方向走来。

s.en: I waited till he came near, then I asked him the way to our old village.
s.zh: 我等他走近后，便向他打听去我们老村庄的路。

s.en: He said that there was now no village.
s.zh: 他说，那个村庄现在已经不存在了。

s.en: I thought he must have misunderstood me, so I repeated its name.
s.zh: 我以为他一定误解了我的意思，于是我又重复了一遍那个名字。

s.en: This time he pointed to the lake.
s.zh: 这次他指向了那个湖泊。

s.en: The village no longer existed because it had been submerged, and all the valley too.
s.zh: 那个村庄已经不存在了——因为它被水淹没了，整个山谷也都消失了。

s.en: The lake was not a natural one, but a man-made reservoir.
s.zh: 那个湖泊并不是天然的，而是一个人工建造的水库。

q: Did the narrater find his mother's grave?
叙述者找到了母亲的坟墓吗？

s.en: The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats where she lived.
s.zh: 那位老太太很高兴能够回到她居住的公寓楼。

s.en: Her shopping had tired her and her basket had grown heavier with every step of the way home.
s.zh: 她的购物让她感到疲惫不堪；而随着她一步步往家走，她手中的购物篮也越来越重了。

s.en: In the lift her thoughts were on lunch and a good rest;
s.zh: 在电梯里，她一心想着吃午饭和好好休息。

s.en: but when she got out at her own floor, both were forgotten in her sudden discovery that her front door was open.
s.zh: 但当她走到自己所在的楼层时，她突然发现前门是开着的，这一发现让她完全忘记了午饭和休息。

s.en: She was thinking that she must reprimand her home help the next morning for such a monstrous piece of negligence,
s.zh: 她正想着，第二天早上一定要严厉责备家政人员如此疏忽，

s.en: when she remembered that she had gone shopping after the home help had left and she knew that she had turned both keys in their locks.
s.zh: 这时却想起自己是在家政人员离开之后才去购物的，而且她清楚记得自己用两把钥匙分别锁好了门。

s.en: She walked slowly into the hall and at once noticed that all the room doors were open,
s.zh: 她缓缓走进大厅，立刻注意到所有的房间门都敞开着。

s.en: yet following her regular practice she had shut them before going out.
s.zh: 然而，按照她平时的习惯，她在出门前还是把它们关上了。

s.en: Looking into the drawing room, she saw a scene of confusion over by her writing desk.
s.zh: 她走进客厅，看到她的书桌旁一片混乱的景象。

s.en: It was as clear as daylight then that burglars had forced an entry during her absence.
s.zh: 当时就很明显了：在她的不在期间，窃贼强行进入了房子。

s.en: Her first impulse was to go round all the rooms looking for the thieves,
s.zh: 她的第一反应是去各个房间寻找小偷。

s.en: but then she decided that at her age it might be more prudent to have someone with her,
s.zh: 但后来她想，以她的年纪来说，有个人陪在身边可能会更稳妥些。

s.en: so she went to fetch the porter from his basement.
s.zh: 于是她下楼去把门房从他的地下室叫了出来。

s.en: By this time her legs were beginning to tremble, so she sat down and accepted a cup of very strong tea, while he telephoned the police.
s.zh: 这时，她的双腿已经开始颤抖了，于是她坐下来喝了一杯浓茶；与此同时，他拨打了报警电话。

s.en: Then, her composure regained, she was ready to set off with the porter's assistance to search for any intruders who might still be lurking in her flat.
s.zh: 随后，她恢复了镇定，便在门卫的协助下准备出发，去搜寻可能还潜伏在她公寓里的入侵者。

s.en: They went through the rooms, being careful to touch nothing,
s.zh: 他们走过一个又一个房间，小心翼翼地避免触碰任何东西。

s.en: as they did not want to hinder the police in their search for fingerprints.
s.zh: 因为他们不想妨碍警方寻找指纹的工作。

s.en: The chaos was inconceivable.
s.zh: 那种混乱简直难以想象。

s.en: She had lived in the flat for thirty years and was a veritable magpie at hoarding:
s.zh: 她已经在这套公寓里住了三十年，是个十足的“收集狂”——总是喜欢囤积各种东西。

s.en: and it seemed as though everything she possessed had been tossed out and turned over and over.
s.zh: 仿佛她拥有的一切都被彻底翻了个个儿，被彻底弄乱了。

s.en: At least sorting out the things she should have discarded years ago was now being made easier for her.
s.zh: 至少，把她那些早就该扔掉的东西整理好这件事，现在对她来说变得容易多了。

s.en: Then a police inspector arrived with a constable and she told them of her discovery of the ransacked flat.
s.zh: 随后，一名警督带着一名警察来到了现场，她向他们报告了自己发现公寓被洗劫的情况。

s.en: The inspector began to look for fingerprints, while the constable checked that the front door locks had not been forced,
s.zh: 检查员开始寻找指纹，而警察则确认前门的锁没有被强行破坏。

s.en: thereby proving that the burglars had either used skeleton keys or entered over the balcony.
s.zh: 由此可以证明，窃贼要么使用了万能钥匙，要么是从阳台上进入屋内的。

s.en: There was no trace of fingerprints, but the inspector found a dirty red bundle that contained jewellery which the old lady said was not hers.
s.zh: 没有发现任何指纹的痕迹，但检查员发现了一个脏兮兮的红色包裹，里面装着一些首饰。那位老妇人声称这些首饰并不属于她。

s.en: So their entry into this flat was apparently not the burglars' first job that day and they must have been disturbed.
s.zh: 显然，他们当天进入这套公寓并不是第一次作案；他们肯定遇到了什么干扰（或者：他们的行动被别人发现了）。

s.en: The inspector then asked the old lady to try to check what was missing by the next day,
s.zh: 然后，检查员让那位老太太在第二天之前试着看看到底少了什么东西。

s.en: and advised her not to stay alone in the flat for a few nights.
s.zh: 并建议她在接下来的几个晚上不要独自待在公寓里。

s.en: The old lady thought he was a fussy creature,
s.zh: 那位老太太认为他是个挑剔的人。

s.en: but since the porter agreed with him, she rang up her daughter and asked for her help in what she described as a little spot of bother.
s.zh: 但由于门房同意了他的请求，她便给女儿打了电话，请求她的帮助来处理这个她所说的“小麻烦”。

q: What did the old lady find when she got home?
那位老太太回家后发现了什么？

s.en: People tend to amass possessions, sometimes without being aware of doing so.
s.zh: 人们往往会积累财物，有时甚至自己都没有意识到这一点。

s.en: Indeed they can have a delightful surprise when they find something useful which they did not know they owned.
s.zh: 确实，当他们发现某些自己原本不知道拥有的、但却非常实用的东西时，会感到非常惊喜。

s.en: Those who never have to move house become indiscriminate collectors of what can only be described as clutter.
s.zh: 那些从未搬过家的人，会无差别地收集各种杂物——这些杂物其实只能被归类为“杂乱无章的堆积物”。

s.en: They leave unwanted objects in drawers, cupboards and attics for years, in the belief that they may one day need just those very things.
s.zh: 他们把不需要的物品放在抽屉、橱柜或阁楼里多年，认为有朝一日自己可能会用到那些东西。

s.en: As they grow old, people also accumulate belongings for two other reasons,
s.zh: 随着年龄的增长，人们积累物品还有另外两个原因：

s.en: lack of physical and mental energy, both of which are essential in turning out and throwing away, and sentiment.
s.zh: 缺乏体力和精力——这两者都是清理和丢弃物品所必需的；此外还有情感因素。

s.en: Things owned for a long time are full of associations with the past,
s.zh: 那些已经拥有很长时间的东西，都承载着与过去相关的种种回忆和情感联系。

s.en: perhaps with relatives who are dead, and so they gradually acquire a value beyond their true worth.
s.zh: 也许这些物品与已经去世的亲人有关联，因此它们逐渐被赋予了超出其实际价值的意义（或：这些物品因为与逝去亲人的联系而变得更有价值）。

s.en: Some things are collected deliberately in the home in an attempt to avoid waste.
s.zh: 有些物品是人们特意在家里收集起来的，目的是为了减少浪费。

s.en: Among these I would list string and brown paper,
s.zh: 在这些物品中，我会列举细绳和牛皮纸。

s.en: kept by thrifty people when a parcel has been opened, to save buying these two requisites.
s.zh: 节俭的人在拆开包裹后，会保留这些物品，以避免再次购买这两样必需品。

s.en: Collecting small items can easily become a mania.
s.zh: 收集小物件很容易变成一种狂热。

s.en: I know someone who always cuts sketches out from newspapers of model clothes that she would like to buy if she had the money.
s.zh: 我认识一个人，她总是从报纸上剪下那些她想要购买的时装款式的图片；如果她有钱的话，一定会买下这些衣服。

s.en: As she is not rich, the chances that she will ever be able to afford such purchases are remote;
s.zh: 由于她并不富裕，她能够负担得起这类购买的费用的可能性微乎其微。

s.en: but she is never sufficiently strongminded to be able to stop the practice.
s.zh: 但她始终缺乏足够的意志力来改掉这个习惯。

s.en: It is a harmless habit, but it litters up her desk to such an extent that every time she opens it, loose bits of paper fall out in every direction.
s.zh: 这其实是个无伤大雅的习惯，但这个习惯让她的办公桌变得非常杂乱——每次她打开桌子时，都会有一堆散落的纸屑从各个方向掉出来。

s.en: Collecting as a serious hobby is quite different and has many advantages.
s.zh: 将收藏作为一种严肃的爱好来从事，其实有着许多独特的优势。

s.en: It provides relaxation for leisure hours, as just looking at one's treasures is always a joy.
s.zh: 它为休闲时光带来了放松与愉悦；仅仅欣赏自己的收藏品，本身就是一种享受。

s.en: One does not have to go outside for amusement, since the collection is housed at home.
s.zh: 人们不必外出寻找娱乐方式，因为这些藏品都收藏在家里。

s.en: Whatever it consists of, stamps, records, first editions of books, china, glass,
s.zh: 无论是邮票、唱片、初版书籍、瓷器、玻璃制品，

s.en: antique furniture, pictures, model cars, stuffed birds, toy animals, there is always something to do in connection with it,
s.zh: 古董家具、画作、模型汽车、标本鸟、玩具动物……总有相关的事情可做，

s.en: from finding the right place for the latest addition, to verifying facts in reference books.
s.zh: 从为新藏品找到合适的位置，到在参考书中核实有关情况。

s.en: This hobby educates one not only in the chosen subject, but also in general matters which have some bearing on it.
s.zh: 这个爱好不仅能让人在所选择的领域内学到知识，还能帮助人们了解与该领域相关的一些通用性知识。

s.en: There are also other benefits.
s.zh: 还有其他一些好处。

s.en: One wants to meet like-minded collectors, to get advice, to compare notes, to exchange articles, to show off the latest find.
s.zh: 人们希望结识志同道合的收藏家，获取建议，交流心得，交换藏品，展示最新发现。

s.en: So one's circle of friends grows.
s.zh: 因此，一个人的朋友圈子也会逐渐扩大。

s.en: Soon the hobby leads to travel, perhaps to a meeting in another town,
s.zh: 很快，这个爱好还会促使人们去旅行，也许到另一个城镇参加聚会，

s.en: possibly a trip abroad in search of a rare specimen, for collectors are not confined to any one country.
s.zh: 也许他们会去国外寻找稀有的标本，因为收藏家们并不局限于某个特定的国家。

s.en: Over the years, one may well become an authority on one's hobby and will very probably be asked to give informal talks to little gatherings
s.zh: 随着时间的推移，一个人很可能会在自己的爱好领域成为专家，并且很可能会被邀请在一些小型聚会上进行非正式的演讲。

s.en: and then, if successful, to larger audiences.
s.zh: 然后，如果讲得成功，就会面向更多听众演讲。

s.en: In this way self-confidence grows, first from mastering a subject, then from being able to talk about it.
s.zh: 通过这种方式，自信心得以增长：先是源于对一门学科的掌握，然后是源于能够就此侃侃而谈。

s.en: Collecting, by occupying spare time so constructively, makes a person contented, with no time for boredom.
s.zh: 通过利用空闲时间来从事有意义的活动，一个人会感到满足，从而不会有无聊的感觉。

q: What in particular does a person gain when he or she becomes a serious collector?
一个人成为真正的收藏家后，具体能获得什么呢？

s.en: Punctuality is a necessary habit in all public affairs in civilized society.
s.zh: 在文明社会的所有公共事务中，守时是一种必不可少的习惯。

s.en: Without it, nothing could ever be brought to a conclusion; everything would be in a state of chaos.
s.zh: 没有它，任何事情都无法办成；一切都将陷入混乱。

s.en: Only in a sparsely-populated rural community is it possible to disregard it.
s.zh: 只有在人口稀少的农村社区，人们才可能忽视它。

s.en: In ordinary living, there can be some tolerance of unpunctuality.
s.zh: 在日常生活中，对于迟到这种行为，人们通常可以有一定的宽容度。

s.en: The intellectual, who is working on some abstruse problem, has everything coordinated and organized for the matter in hand.
s.zh: 这位正在研究某个复杂问题的学者，已经将自己手头的工作所需的一切资料和信息都整理得井井有条、有条不紊了。

s.en: He is therefore forgiven if late for a dinner party.
s.zh: 因此，如果他赴宴迟到，也是可以被原谅的。

s.en: But people are often reproached for unpunctuality when their only fault is cutting things fine.
s.zh: 但是，人们常常因为不守时而受到指责，而他们唯一的过错只是把时间算得太紧。

s.en: It is hard for energetic, quick-minded people to waste time,
s.zh: 对于那些精力充沛、思维敏捷的人来说，浪费时间是一件很难做到的事情。

s.en: so they are often tempted to finish a job before setting out to keep an appointment.
s.zh: 因此，他们常常会忍不住在赴约之前先把工作完成。

s.en: If no accidents occur on the way, like punctured tyres, diversions of traffic, sudden descent of fog, they will be on time.
s.zh: 如果途中没有发生任何意外（比如轮胎爆裂、交通改道、雾突然变浓等情况），他们就能准时到达。

s.en: They are often more industrious, useful citizens than those who are never late.
s.zh: 他们通常比那些从不迟到的人更勤奋、更有用。

s.en: The over-punctual can be as much a trial to others as the unpunctual.
s.zh: 过分守时和迟到一样，都可能让人难以忍受。

s.en: The guest who arrives half an hour too soon is the greatest nuisance.
s.zh: 那位提前半小时就到的客人真是最让人烦恼的人了。

s.en: Some friends of my family had this irritating habit.
s.zh: 我家的一些朋友有个让人很恼火的习惯。

s.en: The only thing to do was ask them to come half an hour later than the other guests.
s.zh: 唯一可行的办法就是让他们比其他客人晚半小时到达。

s.en: Then they arrived just when we wanted them.
s.zh: 然后他们正好在我们需要的时候到了。

s.en: If you are catching a train, it is always better to be comfortably early than even a fraction of a minute too late.
s.zh: 如果你要赶火车，宁可从容地早到，也绝不迟到哪怕一秒钟。

s.en: Although being early may mean wasting a little time,
s.zh: 虽然提前行动可能会浪费一些时间，

s.en: this will be less than if you miss the train and have to wait an hour or more for the next one;
s.zh: 这总比你错过火车、然后不得不等待下一班火车（一个小时或更长时间）要好吧。

s.en: and you avoid the frustration of arriving at the very moment when the train is drawing out of the station and being unable to get on it.
s.zh: 这样你就避免了那种令人沮丧的情况：当你赶到车站时，火车正好已经启动离开，而你却无法上车。

s.en: An even harder situation is to be on the platform in good time for a train and still to see it go off without you.
s.zh: 更糟糕的情况是：你虽然及时赶到了站台，却还是眼睁睁看着火车开走，把你丢下。

s.en: Such an experience befell a certain young girl the first time she was travelling alone.
s.zh: 这样的经历发生在一个年轻女孩第一次独自旅行的时候。

s.en: She entered the station twenty minutes before the train was due,
s.zh: 她在火车预定到站前二十分钟进了车站。

s.en: since her parents had impressed upon her
s.zh: 因为父母已反复叮嘱她，

s.en: that it would be unforgivable to miss it and cause the friends with whom she was going to stay to make two journeys to meet her.
s.zh: 错过这班火车是不可原谅的，因为这会让要来接她的朋友们不得不跑两趟。

s.en: She gave her luggage to a porter and showed him her ticket.
s.zh: 她把行李交给搬运工，并给他看了车票。

s.en: To her horror he said that she was two hours too soon.
s.zh: 令她惊恐的是，他说她来得太早了——比预定的时间早了两个小时。

s.en: She felt in her handbag for the piece of paper on which her father had written down all the details of the journey and gave it to the porter.
s.zh: 她在手提包里寻找那张纸，上面写着父亲记录的所有旅行细节，然后把纸交给了行李员。

s.en: He agreed that a train did come into the station at the time on the paper and that it did stop, but only to take on mail, not passengers.
s.zh: 他承认，根据记录，当时确实有一列火车驶入了车站并且停了下来，但那列火车只是来取邮件的，不让乘客上车。

s.en: The girl asked to see a timetable, feeling sure that her father could not have made such a mistake.
s.zh: 女孩要求查看时刻表，因为她确信她的父亲不可能犯这样的错误。

s.en: The porter went to fetch one and arrived back with the station master,
s.zh: 搬运工去取时刻表，回来时带着站长。

s.en: who produced it with a flourish and pointed out a microscopic 'o' beside the time of the arrival of the train at his station;
s.zh: 站长拿着时刻表，夸张地一挥，指出了他车站火车到站时间旁边一个极小的'o'；

s.en: this little 'o' indicated that the train only stopped for mail.
s.zh: 这个小小的“O”符号表示火车只是为了取邮件而停靠的。

s.en: Just at that moment the train came into the station.
s.zh: 就在那一刻，火车驶进了车站。

s.en: The girl, tears streaming down her face, begged to be allowed to slip into the guard's van.
s.zh: 女孩泪流满面，恳求允许她溜进列车员车厢。

s.en: But the station master was adamant: rules could not be broken.
s.zh: 但站长态度坚决：规定不能违反。

s.en: And she had to watch that train disappear towards her destination while she was left behind.
s.zh: 她只能眼睁睁看着火车驶向目的地，而自己却被留在了车站。

q: Why did the young girl miss the train?
为什么那个小女孩错过了火车？
